## What this row is

`baseline-array` declares itself the naive anchor (`packages/bench/src/adapters/baseline-array.ts:28-55`,
`admission` at 972-975): a `Map<string, TRow>` that is the store, one `dirty` boolean, and a settle
that re-derives every view from the whole population. Version `"0"` is the adapter's own
`version` (955); there is no library to compare against `node_modules`. There is no
`baseline-array.md` beside the adapter; the header points at `baseline-array-indexed.md` for the
other anchor (34).

`frame` is `run()` in all five bindings (186, 347, 520, 796, 931). With no library there is no
batching API to enter, and every write already only marks state that the next settle reads.

## Is it artificially slow

- The full rescan per view per settle (87-96) and the redundant deliveries for writes no view reads
  are the declared design (45-48), and the sibling `baseline-indexed` exists to price the index this
  row lacks.
- `bindPerGroup` multiplies that rescan by fifty (988).
- The churn settle probes the `label` column map for every written row (539), even in scripts that
  mount no column subscriber; one `Map.get` keyed by the row id the loop already holds, disclosed in
  `departure` (962-971).
- Unmount is `indexOf` plus `splice` (638-650). `churnColumn`'s standing names this as what a
  person writes, so it is not a handicap.

## Is it artificially fast

- `pin` keeps the stored object and writes through it (162-185); `patchPinnedLabel` skips the
  `byId.get` that `patchLabel` pays. The cellDelivery standing states this and accepts it.
- `holdRelation` resolves owner objects and pair records once (813-835); `writePair` still composes
  and probes per call (851-855).
- `churn.chain` builds no derivation; the body still applies every level per wake. churnChain's B1
  is declared not met for the mount.
- `churn.diamond` computes the two sides inline in the one callback; there is no node per side to
  build or tear down, which is the hand-written shape and the mount cost a library is read against.
  churnDiamond's B1 is declared not met for exactly this (scenarios.ts, churnDiamond standing B1).
- `readKeys` resolves nothing in advance (357-365).

No place was found where this binding skips work a scenario's `check` or oracle demands.

## Not verified

- Nothing was run. The churnDiamond and viewSwitch checks were read against this wiring
  (see the two notes above), not executed.
- `departure` (962-971) says "three things" and then names four (wide body, chain, diamond, column
  probe); the content is accurate, the count is not.

The render runs the shared top-k over the view's own bucket (77-86). A patchNote still re-renders the view over its row's group (142-147): the bucket knows the row, not the column, and column routing is left out on purpose (baseline-array-indexed.md, 'What the index is, and what is part of it'). A write to a key the store does not hold marks nothing (137-138 and the same guard in each patch), where baseline-array sets dirty anyway; no view's content can change in that case. Once pinned, any dirty group re-delivers both cell views (90-97, 181-190). frame calls run() (191).

churn.row.note: Declined by noChurn (405-411): a churn binding derives no view, so the group index has nothing to do and the row would be baseline-array's churn store under a second name.

churn.wide.note: The same declaration as churn.row (noChurn, 405); justified for the same reason.

churn.column.note: The same declaration as churn.row (noChurn, 405); justified for the same reason.

churn.chain.note: The same declaration as churn.row (noChurn, 405); justified for the same reason. chainFrameWrite, a churn.chain script, has no row here either.

reads.byWindow.note: scrollTo sets an offset and dirty (346-349); the settle selects top-(offset+window) out of view A's bucket and delivers the tail (254-269, 356-360). The read binding keeps one dirty flag rather than a bucket set (departure, 383-385; baseline-array-indexed.md, 'What the index is'). ## What this row is

`packages/bench/src/adapters/baseline-array-indexed.ts` is `baseline-array` with a group index:
a per-group array bucket (42-59) maintained in `write` (102-124), `remove` (125-133) and `setGroup`
(150-160), and the set of groups written since the last settle (69). Order is kept nowhere; each
render selects its window from the bucket with the same top-k the other anchor runs over the
population (73-88). Version `"0"` is the adapter's `version` (376); no library is involved.
`frame` is `run()` in both bindings (191, 331).

## Is it what a competent developer writes

Yes for the two things a person keeping a bucket per group writes together: the bucket, and the
knowledge of which buckets moved. A label write in group A re-renders group A alone, and under
`bindPerGroup` (404) a single-row move re-renders one group of fifty. The companion note
(`baseline-array-indexed.md`) states what is left out so the `indexed − lean` gap carries nothing
else: no column routing, no coalescing beyond the settle, no sort.

A view switch is a key and an offset (350-355): every group's bucket already exists because `write`
files every row, which is the hand-written cost of a group index and the reason a switch here is
cheap.

`leave` is `indexOf` plus `splice` over a bucket of roughly a group's size (53-59); the md
('Why the bucket is an array and not a set') argues the array over a `Set` and leaves it open.

## Is it artificially fast

No. Every write goes through `byId.get`, and `readKeys` resolves nothing in advance (334-342). A
settle skips a view only when no write touched its group, and a view's rows are by construction the
rows of its group, so no skipped view could have changed.

## The declines

All five churn shapes, `relations` and `single` are declined (405-436) with the argument that no
group index exists in those wirings, so the code would be byte-for-byte baseline-array's. That
reason is about this row's purpose, not a library capability, and it holds: the bindings would be
identical. Every read shape is supplied (415-417).

## Not verified

- Whether a `Set` bucket would be faster here was not measured.
- Nothing was run; the viewSwitch check was read against this wiring, not executed.

bind.note: bindViews (oimdb.ts:332) builds the OIMDB, an OIMEffectService, the collection from createRows (86) and orderByGroup from createGroupOrders (92-106): an OIMComputedCollectionSorted over createOIMIndexSetDriven on group with columns BY_RANK_THEN_ID. Each view holds one group-order slot (makeView, 234-257) with one effect on it and one effect over the column-group slots of its window entities (resync, 259-293); settle is channel.flush then paint (383). The row-store methods are bindRowWrites (144): write is insertEntities then upsertEntities, label and note patches assign slot.entity and call markEntityChanged with the one column, with no equality check (161-174), setRank and setGroup are updateEntityByKey, so the index files the move itself; frame is channel.openSubframe/closeSubframe (182-189). dispose (442) is channel.dropEverythingUnchecked and the adapter's arrays cleared. Not measured.

bindPerGroup.note: The same body with fifty held groups (oimdb.ts:1066), so the same write path paid across fifty maintained buckets and fifty sorted computeds.

churn.row.note: bindChurnStore (oimdb.ts:551) builds its own OIMDB and one OIMEntityCollection and nothing else: no index, no order, so a churn write is a slot write and its effects; groupOrder answers undefined, which the churn standings allow. The plain writes come from bindRowWrites (144). holdChurnRows (605) resolves the slots once with rows.getSlotByKey; one effectService.createEffect over the root slots per mount whose body reads row `from` (mountOnRows, 617-624), disposeEffect on unmount (641). Under the churn read fold every standing slot's read is checked.

churn.wide.note: One effect over count roots; the body reads the first root only, declared in departure.

churn.column.note: mountOnColumn (oimdb.ts:625-631) takes rows.holdColumn(slot, 'label'), subscribes one effect to that column slot and gives the hold back at once with rows.unholdColumn, so the effect's subscription keeps the column slot; unmount disposes the effect, so the last unmount of a cycle releases the column slot and the next cycle's first mount mints it again. Not measured.

churn.chain.note: createChurnMounts (oimdb.ts:482) builds the chain levels as slots of one createOIMComputedCollection<number, string> with oimSameValueZeroGuard (490-504), keyed at * CHAIN_KEYS_PER_SUBSCRIBER + level: level 1's sources are the count roots and it derives chainLevelOf of their joined labels, each level above takes the slot below as its source computed and derives chainLevelOf of its value. subscribeHead (528-537) holds the keys bottom up, puts one effectService.createEffect on the head and gives the holds back, so unmount's disposeEffect releases the head and each release gives back the level below. The delivered text is chainHeadOf(label, depth) (harness/derivations.ts).

card.summary: The built engine through its public exports only: one channelled entity collection; an OIMIndex over the group column feeding an OIMComputedCollectionSorted (rank then id as columns) whose held slot is the order of a group (createRows, createGroupOrders); slot, column-group and order effects from OIMEffectService, painted by settle after channel.flush. The churn binding is a channelled entity collection alone, with no index and no order, like every other library's churn wiring. The group filing and the order are the library's: the collection calls keyOf on each write and the sorted computed re-sorts only when a write touches rank or id.

## Version

`oimdbAdapter.version` is `4.0.0` (`adapters/oimdb.ts:1007`). There is no package to compare it with: the adapter imports the built working tree, `../../../core/dist/index.js` (`oimdb.ts:1-30`), and `departure` says 4.0.0 is unpublished.

## Public exports only

`createGroupOrders` (`oimdb.ts:92`) builds `createOIMComputedCollectionSorted(db, { bucketCollectionMemberSlotsReader: createOIMIndexSetDriven(db, { ...indexKeyOptions, sourceEntityCollection: rows, bucketCollectionOptions }), columns: BY_RANK_THEN_ID, slotReleasePolicy })`. A held group order is a `TOIMComputedSlot` from `holdSlotByKey(group)`, read with `getValueForSlot(slot)` (`oimdb.ts:108-116`, `237`, `264`, `297`). The churn derivations are `createOIMComputedCollection` (`oimdb.ts:490`, `506`). Nothing is reached through a private field and no adapter code reports a sort move: the index files the entity and the sorted computed re-sorts when a write changes `rank` or `id`.

## What the engine documents and what the adapter does

- **Entities.** `OIMEntityCollection` over a map-driven store with the default in-place entity writer.
- **Writes.** `write` is `insertEntities` on the first load and `upsertEntities` after; `setGroup` and `setRank` are `updateEntityByKey`; label and note patches assign `slot.entity` and call `markEntityChanged`, guarded only against an absent entity.
- **Signal.** `OIMEffectService.createEffect` on the group-order slot per view, on the column-group slots of the window entities only, and painted in `settle` after `channel.flush()`.
- **Derivations.** Chain levels and diamond nodes are slots of two `createOIMComputedCollection`s keyed by subscriber and level (`createChurnMounts`, `oimdb.ts:482`), read with `getValueForSlot`; the effect subscribes to the head slot.
- **Frame.** The window and read bindings run `frame` inside `channel.openSubframe()` / `closeSubframe()`. The relation and single bindings keep `frame` as `run()`.
- **Teardown.** Every binding with entity collections disposes with `channel.dropEverythingUnchecked()` and clears its own arrays (`oimdb.ts:442`, `648`, `743`, `904`); after the drop `flush` returns at once and the scheduled effects are discarded, so no body runs and `settle` paints nothing.

## Holds

- **Entity holds.** `pin` and `holdRelation` keep the slot `holdSlotByKey` returns; there is no second lookup after the hold. The churn rows are resolved with `getSlotByKey` and held by the effects and derivations that subscribe to them.
- **Column holds.** `pin` keeps its column holds until the channel drop; `mountOnColumn` gives its hold back right after subscribing.
- **Order holds.** Each view holds its group-order slot until the channel drop; `switchGroup` gives the old one back after the new one is held.
- **Untimed resolution.** `pin`, the churn row resolution and `holdRelation` resolve slots before the clock, as the contract allows. `readKeys` resolves nothing ahead.

## Not determined

- Nothing was run, linted by a suite or type-checked; no size for any change and no line count.
- churnDiamond, churnChain and viewSwitch were read against this wiring, not executed; the once-per-frame join rests on the enlist guard and the computed's revision check as read.

bind.note: Kit with OIMSlotWriterFieldMasked and the default merge updater (oimdb-legacy.ts:61-67), derivedArrayIndex by group ordered by compareRows with deps group, rank, id (68-75); one index.emitter.subscribeOnKey per view (107-112), keyed collection subscriptions only on the window's rows (116-136), refresh without re-subscribing when only content changed (139-147, 186-202). Writes are upsertMany/removeManyByPks/upsertOneByPk (208-228). deps make label and note writes irrelevant to the index (core-legacy/src/core/OIMDerivedCollectionIndexArrayBased.ts:40-47); with compareEntities any relevant write marks its bucket for a full re-sort (same file 205-207, 220-222), which the md records as a finding of the library. frame calls run() (278): 3.12.1 has no batch call, and every keyed delivery already waits for queue.flush() (core-legacy/src/core/OIMEventQueue.ts:127-186), which is settle (279).

bindPerGroup.note: The same body with fifty bucket subscriptions (oimdb-legacy.ts:1086).

churn.row.note: collection.emitter.subscribeOnKey per subscriber, release to unmount (415-426, 524-530); the slot is resolved untimed in holdChurnRows and item is read per wake (labelAt 355-358, 405-414), because the merge updater allocates a new entity per write. The body reads row `from`, the row the churn read fold expects of each slot (churnList mounts slot `at` on row `at`, scenarios.ts:2279). The collection is new OIMReactiveCollection with createUpdateEmitter (327-339) instead of the kit, which is the same constructor (core-legacy/src/dx/OIMCollectionKit.ts:24); the field emitter is a subclass that adds one method and leaves subscribeOnKey as it is (core/OIMCarrierKeyedFieldEmitter.ts:47-70). frame calls run() (383).

churn.wide.note: One subscribeOnKeys over the 64 keys (427-442); the body reads all 64 labels in reverse so the first is kept, more body work than the tinybase and baseline wide bodies, which read one.

churn.column.note: collection.emitter.subscribeOnKeyFields(pk, labelMask, body) (444-454), the mask built once from the registry the field-masked writer was handed (326-335, 341), so its bits are the writer's (core/OIMSlotWriterFieldMasked.ts:55-63; core/OIMCarrierKeyedFieldEmitter.ts:56-70).

churn.chain.note: One OIMComputed with an on.collection dependency per root, deriving chainLevelOf(first root's label, 1) (456-471), depth - 1 more over on.computed, level k deriving chainLevelOf(level k-1, k) (472-478), and an OIMEffect on the head that renders head.get() (479-486), so the text is chainHeadOf(label, depth) (harness/derivations.ts:3-7). All on getOIMComputeRuntime(queue) (340), the runtime the kit uses (dx/OIMCollectionKit.ts:29). Unmount destroys the effect then the computeds head-first (487-492); dispose destroys the runtime after the collection (531-539). Constructed directly rather than through kit.computed/kit.effect because those add every node to the kit's OIMDisposeScope (dx/OIMCollectionKit.ts:53, 66), which has no removal (core/OIMDisposeScope.ts:46-53, 65-84). chainFrameWrite builds the same chains in prepare and times the frame alone.

churn.diamond.note: Two OIMComputed over the one root's on.collection deriving diamondLeftOf and diamondRightOf of its label, a third over on.computed of both deriving diamondJoinOf, and an OIMEffect on the join (oimdb-legacy.ts:495-523), on the same runtime as the chain. The runtime schedules by level (modules/effect/core/OIMEffect.ts:65, 138) and OIMEffect.onComputedInvalidate returns when already scheduled (same file 134-139), so the join and the subscriber run once per flush, which churnDiamond's check asserts. Unmount destroys the effect, the join, then both sides (516-521). Not run.

reads.byKey.note: getSlotByPk per key and one item load (673-682); nothing resolved in advance.

reads.byWindow.note: scrollTo moves the page start and marks shapeMoved (685-689); the settle re-reads the live bucket slice and re-points 32 keyed subscriptions (614-630, 701-714). frame calls run() (669).

reads.byTwoAxes.note: A second derivedArrayIndex keyed on group plus axis (563-566), so the library files both predicates; every write that touches group, rank or id maintains both indexes.

reads.bySwitch.note: switchGroup (691-697) releases view A's index.emitter subscription (stops[0], 605-611), subscribes on the other group's key, points the page at that bucket (pagedGroup, 568, read by paged.slotsOf 583) and offset 0, and marks; the settle resyncs exactly as after scrollTo. View B is not marked, so viewSwitch's view-B check is met with no redundant delivery. The derived index keeps every group's bucket already, so the switch fills nothing. Not run.

relations.note: Three kits on one queue, the pairs kit on OIMCollectionStoreTrieDriven keyed by a ctk tuple (747, 753-777); owner and pair slots resolved untimed for reading (846-904); patchOwnerName and writePair go through upsertOneByPk with the tuple built per call (908-918). OIMCollection has no slot-addressed write (core-legacy/src/core/OIMCollection.ts:97-150), so the pin saves only the read. frame calls run() (838).

single.note: OIMReactiveObject with a keyed subscription per property and a FRAME_END render (964-1038). frame calls run() (1024).

improvements: oimdb-legacy.md 'The opt-ins': orderBy with a zero-padded rank joined to the id could express rank-then-id (OIMDerivedCollectionIndexArrayBased.ts:301-305 compares with < and >); neither wired nor measured, and whether every scripted rank is non-negative was not checked. Would move every bind row that writes rank if it is faster than compareEntities.
card.summary: createOIMCollectionKit with a field-masked writer and a derived array index per group, keyed emitters as the signal, renders at FRAME_END; the churn binding builds its collection without the kit so the column shape can subscribe through the exported field emitter, and the chain and diamond shapes build the OIMComputed nodes and OIMEffect the scripts ask for on the queue's compute runtime.

## Version and source

The adapter's `version` is `3.12.1` (`packages/bench/src/adapters/oimdb-legacy.ts:1043`), and
`packages/core-legacy/package.json` declares `"version": "3.12.1"` (line 3). The adapter imports
`packages/core-legacy/src` directly (1-22), not a published tarball. The md says the source was
restored from git at `bbfe0a1` (`oimdb-legacy.md`, first section). Whether that tree is byte-equal
to what npm shipped as `@oimdb/core@3.12.1` was **not verified**.

## What the source says and what the adapter does

`docs` names the source as the recipe (1044). `departure` (1045-1054) says the 3.x README's
`updateEventEmitter.subscribeOnKey` does not exist in 3.12.1 (not verified against the README), and
names the two places the churn binding leaves the kit: the collection is built with
`createUpdateEmitter`, which `TOIMCollectionKit`'s options type cannot carry
(`core-legacy/src/types/TOIMCollectionKit.ts:13-16` is plain `TOIMCollectionOptions`; the option
exists only on the `OIMReactiveCollection` constructor, `core/OIMReactiveCollection.ts:57-66`), and
the chain's and diamond's nodes are built on the queue's compute runtime because the kit's scope
cannot release them. Every other binding follows the kit: `createOIMCollectionKit`,
`indexFactory.derivedArrayIndex`, `collection.emitter` and `index.emitter` subscriptions, and
`queue.flush()` as the settle. Renders run on `FRAME_END` so a re-subscription after a shape change
is outside the effect phase (183-202).

`frame` is `run()` in all five bindings (278, 383, 669, 838, 1024). 3.12.1 exports no batch or
transaction call; nothing is delivered until `queue.flush()`, so the writes between two settles are
already one frame.

## Where it differs

1. **The churn collection is not a kit.** `new OIMReactiveCollection(queue, { …, createUpdateEmitter })`
   (327-339).
2. **The chain and diamond are built off the kit's runtime, not through `kit.computed`.** Reason
   above; the alternative would leave every unmounted node in the scope until dispose.
3. **pin is half a pin.** Reads go through held slots; writes still go through `upsertOneByPk`
   (272-277) because `OIMCollection` has no slot-addressed write (`core/OIMCollection.ts:97-150`).
   That is a library limit, stated in the md.

## Is anything done for the library

No values are held outside the engine: `visible` holds the entity objects the bucket's slots point
at, and `readAll`, `groupOrder` and `readPairs` read the collection, the index bucket and the slots.
The chain's and diamond's computeds read the slots through `labelAt` (355-358) and the effects read
the head computed; nothing caches a derived value outside them. `switchGroup` keeps only the key the
view reads, `pagedGroup`.

## Not verified

- Equality of `packages/core-legacy/src` with the published 3.12.1 package.
- That `OIMReactiveCollection<TRow, string, TChurnFieldEmitter>` is accepted by `on.collection`
  (`dx/on.ts:24-28`, which takes `OIMReactiveCollection<TEntity, TPk>`); not compiled.
- churnDiamond and viewSwitch were read against this wiring, not executed.

bind.note: One query per view selecting rank, label and a calculated order cell where group (tinybase.ts:206-213), window ids from addResultSortedRowIdsListener(order, offset 0, limit window) (watchShape, 133-146), content through one addResultRowListener per window row; when the shape moves only the rows that left lose their listener and only the rows that entered get one (rewatchRows 153-170, renderWindow 174-190, settle 274-292). Outside a frame each write call is its own transaction (store.transaction around a multi-row loop, a bare setCell otherwise), and frame is store.transaction, inside which those nest (transactedStoreOf 61-79, transactionFrameOf 52-56). The order cell is a fixed-width rank joined to the row id (45-50), so TinyBase's one-cell sort produces the rank-then-id order itself; there is no hand sort and no tie left to the library at the window edge. Rows are written as four cells, the id being the key (237-243).

bindPerGroup.note: The same body with fifty queries (tinybase.ts:794), each maintained by TinyBase on every write to the table. The Indexes module (setIndexDefinition(id, table, 'group', sortKey, , rowIdSorter), @types/indexes/index.d.ts:424-431; index.js:1154-1268) keeps a sorted slice per group but has no window: getSliceRowIds copies the whole slice (index.js:1333-1334) and addSliceRowIdsListener fires on any membership or order change in the group (1279, 1341-1342), so a 32-row window over it would wake on reorders outside the window or need an adapter-side window compare, which TBinding forbids. Kept as queries; the reason is in tinybase.md.

churn.row.note: store.addRowListener per subscriber on one row id, delListener to unmount (366-378, 333-337); the body reads row `from`'s label with getCell (labelAt 330-331), the row the churn read fold expects of each slot (churnList mounts slot `at` on row `at`, scenarios.ts:2279). The store carries no queries in this wiring, so nothing else is maintained on write. frame is store.transaction (transactedStoreOf, 78).

churn.wide.note: One addRowListener per row of the 64 (366-378), since addRowListener takes one row id or null; the body reads the first row only, as departure states (752-762). churnWide writes row 0 alone per frame (scenarios.ts:2014, rowsWrittenIn churnRowOnly), so each subscriber wakes once.

churn.column.note: store.addCellListener(TABLE, id, 'label') (379-386): TinyBase's own column identity.

churn.chain.note: Queries from queries (390-418): a root query over TABLE where the stored id cell is one of the subscriber's rows, selecting group, rank, note and a calculated label holding chainLevelOf(label, 1), then depth - 1 queries each defined with setQueryDefinition(id, true, belowQueryId, …) (@types/queries/index.d.ts:2280-2310, since 8.3.0) selecting chainLevelOf(label below, k) as label, and addResultCellListener on the head's label of the first row (409-413), so the text read is chainHeadOf(label, depth). Unmount runs the mount's own release, which deletes the listener and the definitions head first (414-417, unmount 333-337). Defining the root query evaluates its where over every table row (index.js:5365-5368), which is the mount cost the library charges for a derivation. chainFrameWrite builds the same stacks in prepare and times the frame alone.

churn.diamond.note: Queries from queries (419-447): a left and a right query over TABLE, each where('id', rowId) and each selecting one calculated cell (diamondLeftOf(label) as left, diamondRightOf(label) as right), and a join query rooted on the left result that joins the right result by the same row id (join(true, rightId, on-callback), @types/queries/index.d.ts:1440-1444, since 8.3.0) and selects diamondJoinOf(left, right) as join; addResultCellListener on that cell. Once per frame by reading index.js (see the prose), not by a run. Each mount pays two whole-table where evaluations.

reads.byKey.note: Two getCell calls per key, rank and label, a missing row answering undefined (518-534); nothing resolved in advance.

reads.byWindow.note: The window is a property of the listener (@types/queries/index.d.ts:4028-4035), so scrollTo deletes it, registers one at the new offset and reads the page with getResultSortedRowIds on the order cell (pageAt, 498-504; scrollTo 535); the settle then moves the row listeners of the rows that left onto the rows that entered (rewatchRows 153-170). This is the API's only way to move an offset. frame is store.transaction (transactedStoreOf, 78).

reads.byTwoAxes.note: The axis is a where(callback) inside the query over the stored id cell (479-486, callback at 485), so TinyBase evaluates both predicates. This, and the churn chain's root query, are why those two wirings keep the id cell.

reads.bySwitch.note: The paged query filters on where('group', param('group')) with the param seeded to group A (468-478); switchGroup calls queries.setParamValue('paged', 'group', group), which writes the param store (index.js:5496-5501) whose row listener re-runs the definition (5459-5467): the result table is deleted (4973) and the where re-evaluated over the whole table (5365-5368) inside one result-store transaction (4809). switchGroup then moves the window to offset 0 through the same pageAt a scroll uses (537-540). The settle delivers view A; view B's query is untouched, so viewSwitch's view-B check is met with no redundant delivery. The param, not a re-definition, is TinyBase's documented way to change what a live query selects (@types/queries/index.d.ts:820-849 Param, since 7.2.0; setParamValue at 2520). Not run.

relations.note: Three tables in one store, owners and pair records as rows, addCellListener on each touched owner's name and each pair's mark (holdRelation 615-642), patchOwnerName and writePair as single setCell calls, each its own transaction, with the pair id composed per call (645-653). Rows are written as four cells (598-605). frame is store.transaction (transactedStoreOf, 78).

single.note: TinyBase Values: setValue, getValue and addValueListener per value (689-746); frame is store.transaction (726).

improvements: NOT APPLIED. tinybase.ts:794: an Indexes-module wiring (one index by group with a sort key) for consumerPerGroup. bind and bindPerGroup must share one body (harness/types.ts:340-341), and the module has no windowed slice or windowed listener (index.js:1333-1342), so the window's change check would become the adapter's; see tinybase.md, 'Why the views are queries'.
card.summary: TinyBase's documented query path (one query per view, a sorted-row-ids listener with offset and limit on a calculated rank-then-id sort cell, per-row result listeners, one transaction per write call outside a frame and one per script frame), with each churn chain and each diamond built as queries from queries and the view switch as a query param; the read and churn wirings store the row id as a cell because a where callback is handed no row id.
card.body:
## Version

`packages/bench/node_modules/tinybase/package.json:3` is `10.0.1`, equal to the adapter's `version`
(`packages/bench/src/adapters/tinybase.ts:750`). The bench package's copy is the one resolved,
through its `exports` "." entry, `./index.js`. Every `index.js` and `@types` line below is from
10.0.1; the previous card's citations were for 9.3.0 and all moved.

## What the documentation says and what the adapter does

The adapter cites the queries guide (`docs`, 751). It follows it: TinyQL `select`/`where` per view
(206-213), `addResultSortedRowIdsListener` for the window (133-146) and `getResultCell` reads in
`renderWindow` (174-186). TinyBase compares the new window with the old (`arrayIsEqual`,
`index.js:2577`) and calls a sorted-row-ids listener only when row ids changed or a cell it sorts on
changed (`index.js:2420-2454`, listeners keyed by `[tableId, cellId]` at 2591), so a label patch
reaches the view only through the per-row result listener (rewatchRows 153-170). Outside a frame
each write call is its own transaction and its listeners run before the call returns: a multi-row
`write`/`remove` wraps its loop in `store.transaction`, a single `setCell` is wrapped by TinyBase
(`fluentTransaction`, `index.js:2547-2550`). This is the same reading of an unframed write as
`tanstack-db.ts`'s per-call `begin`/`commit`; no transaction is held open across calls until
`settle`. `frame` is `store.transaction(run)` (`index.js:3028-3043`): transactions nest by a counter
(`startTransaction`, 3044-3047), so a write's transaction inside a frame leaves the listeners to the
frame's finish. In 10.0.1
`transaction` runs nothing while the store is in its listener phase (`transactions == -1`, 3029, set
at 3164 and 3193); no adapter listener writes, so this does not reach any binding. `pin` deletes the
query definitions so the cell rows are not charged for two maintained result tables, and the cell
views are `addCellListener` per pinned cell (246-270).

## The order inside the window

A calculated select cell (`select((getTableCell, rowId) => …).as('order')`,
`@types/queries/index.d.ts:997-1012`) holds `rank + 1e15`, zero-padded to 16 digits, a space and the
row id (tinybase.ts:45-50). `defaultSorter` compares with `<` (`index.js:1117-1118`), so on strings
of equal-width numeric prefix the order is rank, then id by code unit, which is `compareRows`
(`dataset.ts:423-424`). The dataset's ranks are integers from small negatives
(`dataset.ts:912, 932, 961`) up to `1000 + 200 × 99 999` (`rankFor`, 432), plus mover and arrival
ranks derived from those (448, 990), well inside the encoding's range; the ranks individual scripts
pass to `setRank` were not traced one by one. TinyBase decides both which rows are in the window
and their order, and a rank tie at the 32nd place is broken on id by the library.

## The row id as a cell

The window and relation wirings write `{ group, rank, label, note }` (tinybase.ts:241, 602); the id
is the row's key, which `readAll` and `groupOrder` read back as the key of `getTable` and
`getResultTable` (`rowsOf` 82-83, `groupOrderOf` 88-98). The read and churn wirings still pass the
whole `TRow` (510, 343), id included, because `where(callback)` is handed `getTableCell` and no row
id (`@types/queries/index.d.ts:1765`; `index.js:5247` calls each where with `getJoinCell` alone): the
second axis (485) and the chain's root rows (399) are both predicates on the id, and the diamond's
two root queries filter `where('id', rowId)` on it.

## The chain

Each subscriber's chain is `depth` query definitions: a root over `TABLE`, and each further level
rooted on the result of the one below, each level's `label` a calculated cell applying
`chainLevelOf` with its own level number, so the head's `label` is `chainHeadOf(label, depth)`.
Each query has its own result store (`getResultStore`, `index.js:4610-4611`), and that store's
transactions are synchronized with the store the query reads (`synchronizeTransactions`,
`index.js:4740-4753`, called at 5383-5387), so the head's `addResultCellListener` runs inside the
write's (or the frame's) own `finishTransaction` and is counted before `settle` delivers. A label write to the
first root changes that row's label at every level once, so each standing subscriber wakes once per
frame. The head is listened to on the first root's `label`, the value the subscriber renders, so a
write that does not change it does not wake it.

## The diamond, and why the join fires once

Three query definitions per subscriber (tinybase.ts:419-447): left and right over `TABLE`, the join
rooted on the left result and joined to the right one. A query's result store is synchronized with
its ROOT store only (`index.js:5383-5387`); the joined right result reaches the join through a row
listener the join adds on it (`index.js:5319-5330`). So the join is not covered by one transaction
the way a chain level is, and whether it fires once rests on this ordering, read from `index.js`
(`finishTransaction`, 3120-3211):

1. The label write lands in the main store's transaction (its own, or the frame's); the main store's will-finish
   listeners (3163) start the left and right result stores' transactions (`index.js:4744`).
2. The main store's non-mutator row listeners (3166-3173) write the new `left` and `right` cells.
   TinyBase applies a cell at once and defers only listeners, so both result stores hold the new
   values from here.
3. The main store's did-finish listeners (3191-3195) finish left and right in turn
   (`index.js:4749-4751`). Whichever finishes first makes the join recompute, and the recompute
   reads BOTH sources through `getCell` (`getJoinCell`, `index.js:5178-5195`), already new, so the
   join cell takes its final value.
4. The second source's finish recomputes the join again to the same string; TinyBase calls no
   cell listener for a cell that did not change, so the listener has run once.

Not executed. If step 2 were wrong (a source's values deferred with its listeners) the join
listener would run twice per frame with an intermediate `new|old` text, and `churnDiamond`
(scenarios.ts:2507-2593) would fail its delivery count for this row rather than report a time.

## The view switch

`setParamValue` writes the param into the queries object's own param store (`index.js:5496-5501`);
a row listener on that store, registered as a mutator listener, re-runs the definition
(`index.js:5459-5467`), which deletes the result table (4973) and re-evaluates the `where` over
every row of `TABLE` (5365-5368), inside one result-store transaction (4809). `switchGroup` then
moves the window to offset 0 through `pageAt`, the listener swap `scrollTo` uses, so the settle
moves the row listeners of the rows that changed and delivers once. The re-evaluation is the cost TinyBase charges for
changing what a live query selects; there is no incremental re-filter.

## Is anything done for the library

No values are held outside the store; every render reads through `getResultCell` or `getCell`. The
`ids` array held per view is what the listener hands back. `groupOrder` defines and deletes a query
of its own, untimed (`groupOrderOf`, 88-98).

## Code volume

The figures are `npm run lines`' cell for each wiring: its builder, every helper it reaches and
every constant it reads, comments and blank lines excluded. Every row wiring pays for the store and
the four cell writes (`transactedStoreOf`, tinybase.ts:61-79).

- **bind** adds what the window needs and TinyBase does not hand over in one call: the calculated
  order cell (45-50, 211), because a sorted result sorts on one cell; a sorted-row-ids listener per
  view (133-146) for the window's membership; and per-row result listeners moved when the window
  moves (148-190), because the sorted-ids listener does not fire on a label change. The cell wiring
  is two cell listeners per pinned row (246-270).
- **reads.byKey** carries both read views, because one binding serves every read shape: the two
  query definitions (468-486), the two window views (488-491) and `pageAt` (498-504), over the same
  window helpers the bind wiring uses.

## Not verified

- Every claim above about time. Nothing was run; the chain and diamond mounts pay a where
  evaluation over the whole table per root query per subscriber per mount, and a view switch
  pays one over the whole table per switch.
- Whether a wildcard `addResultRowListener(queryId, null, …)` would be faster on any row.
- The cascade order of chained result-store transactions, and the once-per-frame join above, were
  read from `index.js` 10.0.1, not executed.
- The per-call transactions and `rewatchRows` (153-170) have not been run.

bind.note: Collection with createIndex('group') (adapters/signaldb.ts:87-89), one find({group}, {sort: {rank: 1, id: 1}, limit}) per view observed with all four callbacks and skipInitial (signaldb.ts:120-144). Writes are updateOne $set per patch (signaldb.ts:245-256) and insert/updateOne inside collection.batch for write/remove (signaldb.ts:214-244); frame is the same collection.batch around the script's writes (signaldb.ts:110, 257), opened once because batch does not nest (createBatchFrame 32-46; node_modules/@signaldb/core/dist/index23.mjs:560-567). Inside a frame the index rebuild and every cursor's requery wait for the frame's end (index23.mjs:391-394, 510-517). Each updateOne copies the memory array and, outside a batch, rebuilds every index over the whole collection (index23.mjs:422-427, 447-449, 391-403, 619-643); that is the library. The settle fetches each pending cursor again because the observer keeps its window private (signaldb.ts:307-318). The adapter-side `written` Set (signaldb.ts:109) holds ids to choose insert over updateOne; disclosed in departure and admission (signaldb.ts:1140-1155).

bindPerGroup.note: The same body with fifty cursors (signaldb.ts:1194); every write requeries all fifty (index23.mjs:510-527), which is SignalDB's model, once per frame inside a frame.

churn.row.note: find({id}) plus observeChanges({added, changed}, false) per subscriber (signaldb.ts:506-530): the mount label comes from `added` on the observer's first run, the one getItems registration already performs (index10.mjs:139-142, index9.mjs:56-104), and a wake reads row `from`'s label off the document `changed` carries; `added` only reads, so a mount is not a wake. unmount stops the observer and cleans up the cursor (561-568). The read is the one the churn read fold expects of each slot (churnList mounts slot `at` on row `at`, scenarios.ts:2279). No group index in this wiring, since no churn cursor selects on group. frame is collection.batch (422, 470).

churn.wide.note: One find({id: {$in: ids}}) cursor per subscriber, the same body as churn.row (signaldb.ts:506-530), SignalDB's way to observe many documents; the $in resolves through the id provider registered at construction (index23.mjs:151; index22.mjs:12-42). The body keeps the first source's label, the one value the line renders, out of the documents `added` and `changed` carry, and counts a wake on every `changed`; no findOne and no second memory-array copy per wake. Declared in departure (1146-1148).

churn.column.note: find({id}, {fields: {label: 1}}) with the same added/changed pair (signaldb.ts:531-553): the observer diffs the projected document (index10.mjs:72-88, index9.mjs:56-80), so a note write produces no changed call. A column identity built from the library's own diff.

churn.chain.note: Declined in churnShapes (signaldb.ts:1161-1166; mountOnChain throws through declinedMount, 554). @signaldb/core exports no derived-value primitive (dist/index.d.ts:1-18) and a cursor's result is not an input to another cursor, so a mount could only be the wide $in cursor with the depth levels re-run by hand in its body. Removes signaldb from churnChain and chainFrameWrite, both churn.chain scripts.

churn.diamond.note: Declined in churnShapes (signaldb.ts:1167-1172; mountOnDiamond throws, 555). The same absence: no computed value to build the two branches or the join from, so the diamond could only be three functions called by hand inside one observer body, which the contract forbids. Removes signaldb from churnDiamond.

reads.byKey.note: One find({id: {$in: page}}).fetch() per page (signaldb.ts:703-708), applied under the ruling that a per-page $in is the library's lookup. getIndexInfo sends a non-scalar id selector to the index providers (index23.mjs:404-420); the first provider is the id index registered at construction (index23.mjs:151), and createExternalIndex resolves $in key by key in the order given (index21.mjs:28-29, index22.mjs:12-42), so positions come back in the page's key order, the id drops out of the residual selector and getItems returns them without a match pass (index23.mjs:458-476). One memory-array copy per page, where the findOne per key it replaces paid one per key (index23.mjs:545-554, 447-449). Nothing is resolved in advance.

reads.byWindow.note: skip is fixed at cursor construction (pagedCursorOf, signaldb.ts:610-614), so scrollTo stops and cleans up the old cursor and observes a new one at the new skip (repointPaged 630-636, scrollTo 714-717). That is SignalDB's model. frame is collection.batch (606, 697).

reads.byTwoAxes.note: Both predicates are in the selector, the axis as $regex '[02468][0-9][0-9]$' on id (signaldb.ts:642-658); onSecondAxis tests the evenness of the third-from-last character's code (dataset.ts:393-394), which for a digit is the digit's evenness, and every dataset id ends in seven digits (dataset.ts:437, 910, 930, 959), so the two agree on every row.

reads.bySwitch.note: A cursor takes its selector at construction, so switchGroup sets the paged group, resets the offset and goes through the same repoint scrollTo uses: stop and clean up the old cursor, observe a new find({group}, {sort, skip: 0, limit}) and mark it (pagedGroup 609, repointPaged 630-636, switchGroup 718-722). The settle delivers it as it delivers a scroll (723-732). View B's cursor is untouched and not marked, so viewSwitch's view-B check is met with no redundant delivery. Not run.

relations.note: Three collections and two observed $in cursors, one per view (holdRelation, signaldb.ts:916-967). Each render is one fetch of the cursor its view observes, placed by an id-to-lines map built in holdRelation (maps 822-823, filled 929-932; renders 833-855), the pattern the cell wiring uses. frame batches the owners and pairs collections, the two the relation scripts write (803-806, 894); the row collection is left out because closing a batch rebuilds that collection's whole id index (index23.mjs:396-403).

single.note: A document per value and a find({id}) cursor per value (signaldb.ts:1061-1134), declared as the nearest thing SignalDB has to a scalar; frame is collection.batch (1115). dispose stops the observers and calls collection.dispose() (1128-1132).

card.summary: SignalDB's framework-free recipe (Collection with a group index, one sorted and limited find cursor per view, observeChanges as the signal, collection.batch per frame); the library's own per-write costs dominate. The keyed read is one find({id: {$in: page}}) per page through the id provider, a scroll and a view switch each build a new cursor, and the chain and diamond shapes are declined because SignalDB has no derivation primitive.
card.body:
## Version

`node_modules/@signaldb/core/package.json:3` (repository root) is `1.8.1`, equal to the adapter's
`version` (`packages/bench/src/adapters/signaldb.ts:1138`). There is no copy under
`packages/bench/node_modules`. SignalDB was not among the 2026-10-17 upgrades, and the `dist`
lines cited here were re-read against the installed build.

## What the documentation says and what the adapter does

The adapter cites the Collection reference and the indexes guide (48-78, `docs` 1139). It installs no
reactivity adapter (`departure`, signaldb.ts:1140-1150), so `Cursor.depend` returns at
once and `observeChanges` is the documented signal. Each view is a sorted, limited cursor
(signaldb.ts:120-144); `Cursor.getItems` applies sort, skip and limit in that order
(`dist/index10.mjs:72-88`), so the window is SignalDB's own. Every collection event
requeries every observed cursor, deferred to the end of a `batch` when one is open
(`dist/index23.mjs:510-527`), and the observer diffs the new list against the last one
(`dist/index9.mjs:56-90`), which is also what makes `resendUnchanged` wake nobody.

## Frame

`frame` runs the script's writes inside `collection.batch` (index23.mjs:560-567).
`batch` sets a flag, runs the callback, clears the flag, rebuilds every index and runs
the deferred requeries, which are a Set, so each cursor re-derives once per frame. It
does not nest: an inner `batch` clears the flag and flushes before the outer callback
returns. `createBatchFrame` (signaldb.ts:32-46) therefore opens the batch once per frame
and runs a nested call (`write` or `remove` inside a frame) directly in the open one.
Outside a frame `write` and `remove` open their own batch, and a single patch is an
unbatched `updateOne`.

## The keyed read

The ruling that one `$in` query per page is the library's lookup is applied
(signaldb.ts:703-708). It is the fast form only because of the id provider SignalDB
registers on every collection (index23.mjs:151): without a provider for the field, a
non-scalar selector falls to `memory.filter(match)` (index23.mjs:468-470), and `match`
builds a mingo `Query` per document (index12.mjs:11-12). With it, the page is resolved
by `idIndex` lookups in key order. `getIndexInfo` answers unmatched while
`indicesOutdated` is set, which happens only inside a batch (index23.mjs:391-394,
415-419); no read script calls `readKeys` inside a frame.

## Where it differs, and in whose favour

- **The `written` Set** (signaldb.ts:109) is the one piece of bookkeeping the adapter
  keeps. It holds ids only and decides insert versus update; `WHY-EACH-ROW.md` ("batch
  insert — signaldb, figure retracted until re-measured") records that the upsert path
  is quadratic on a load (`dist/index23.mjs:422-430`) and that `insert` still scans
  once per row (`:584`); no figure for the current wiring has been measured. For a load into an empty store this is what
  `insertMany` does (`:598-609`). For a write of a row already present it routes to
  `updateOne`, the same call upsert would make.
- **Per-write costs that are the library's:** `updateOne` copies the memory array and,
  outside a batch, rebuilds the id index and every index provider over the whole
  collection (`:391-403`, `:619-643`).
- **Scroll and switch build cursors.** Both cost a cursor construction, an observer and
  one full `getItems` (the observer's initial `runChecks`, index10.mjs `observeRawChanges`)
  plus the settle's `fetch`; that is SignalDB's model of a query, not an adapter choice.

## Not verified

- No figure in this card was measured; directions are from operation counts in the
  shipped build.
- That `updateOne` by `{ id }` inside a batch, after a `removeOne` earlier in the same
  batch, resolves through the shifted id index (`deleteFromIdIndex`, index23.mjs:437-443)
  to the right position; read, not run.
- That `find({ id: { $in } })` returns the page in key order in every read script: read
  from `createExternalIndex` (index22.mjs:12-42) and the order-preserving `Set` in
  `getMergedIndexInfo` (index18.mjs), not run. A page whose key is absent comes back
  short, which fails the digest rather than passing.
- The viewSwitch check was read against this wiring, not executed.

bind.note: One createLiveQueryCollection per view, where(group).orderBy(rank).orderBy(id).limit(window).select(id, rank, label), subscribed with subscribeChanges and includeInitialState false through `watchChanges` (adapters/tanstack-db.ts:227-245, 193-199); delivery from live.toArray in settle (tanstack-db.ts:299-311). A note write yields a projected row deepEqual to the previous one and the commit pushes no event for it (node_modules/@tanstack/db/src/collection/state.ts:1392-1402). After pin, two projected live queries over the pinned ids, one selecting label and one note, each drive their own consumer (tanstack-db.ts:253-292), so a write wakes only its column; each cell is read back with live.get(id) per pinned id (tanstack-db.ts:270-273).

bindPerGroup.note: The same body handed fifty views (tanstack-db.ts:891): fifty ordered, limited, projected live queries over one backing collection.

frame.note: frame is one sync transaction per collection the frame's writes reach: the first write on a collection inside a frame calls begin and every later one joins it; the frame's end commits each opened one (tanstack-db.ts:77-106). Outside a frame each write call is its own begin/write/commit, committed before the call returns; no transaction is held open until settle, the same reading of an unframed write tinybase.ts follows with one store.transaction per call. No script nests a frame, so the frame keeps a flag rather than a depth. The sync interface does not nest: commit takes the last pending transaction (db/src/collection/sync.ts:285-313) and commitPendingTransactions applies only committed ones (state.ts:1060-1120), which is why writes join the open transaction instead of opening their own; the comment at tanstack-db.ts:97 cites sync.ts:285-290.

churn.row.note: subscribeChanges on the backing collection with where eq(row.id, …) and includeInitialState false (tanstack-db.ts:384-401), the documented filtered subscription (db/src/types.ts:1094-1115). The body reads the row back with rows.get and stores it per slot, so the verify pass's per-slot read fold sees each subscriber's own read (tanstack-db.ts:347, 389, 400; harness/render.ts:124-141).

churn.wide.note: One subscribeChanges with where inArray(row.id, sources) (tanstack-db.ts:393-396). The body reads the first source alone; the dependency set is the where clause, not the reads, so this does not shrink the subscription, and the first source is what churnWide's model expects every subscriber to read (scenarios.ts:2149-2154). Declared in departure (tanstack-db.ts:846-848).

churn.column.note: A live query per subscriber over the one row with select(id, label) (tanstack-db.ts:402-423): TanStack DB's where filters rows, and a projection is its only column narrowing. A pipeline per subscriber is the price; WHY-EACH-ROW.md (churnColumn) says the same. The body reads the label from the backing collection, not from the live query (tanstack-db.ts:418).

churn.chain.note: depth live queries built in the mount: level 1 is where inArray(row.id, roots) over the backing collection with fn.select deriving chainLevelOf(label, 1) (tanstack-db.ts:427-438); each level k from 2 is a live query from the one below with fn.select deriving chainLevelOf(text, k) (tanstack-db.ts:442-456). The subscriber is on the head and reads the head's row for root `from` with head.get(id) (tanstack-db.ts:458-468). Every level is cleaned up in the unmount (tanstack-db.ts:352-359); cleanup() returns a promise but retires local state synchronously (db/src/collection/lifecycle.ts:466-480, 512-522). fn.select is the library's functional projection, documented as not optimisable (db/src/query/builder/index.ts:946-985); nothing above level 1 has a where or an orderBy to optimise.

churn.diamond.note: Two live queries over root `from` (where eq(row.id, id), fn.select of diamondLeftOf / diamondRightOf, tanstack-db.ts:472-483) and a third that innerJoins them on id and fn.selects diamondJoinOf(left.text, right.text) (tanstack-db.ts:484-494); the subscriber is on the join and reads its one row (tanstack-db.ts:495-504). All three are cleaned up on unmount. In 0.15 emitEvents publishes every committed batch inside withPublicationContext (db/src/collection/changes.ts:255-283; db/src/scheduler.ts:183-216), and a live query's graph run is scheduled into that context with its source builders as dependencies (db/src/query/live/graph-scheduler.ts:13-29; collection-config-builder.ts:710-736), so the join waits until both branches have run and runs once per write. Read, not run; the adapter's departure says the same (tanstack-db.ts:843-845).

reads.byKey.note: collection.get per key on the backing collection (tanstack-db.ts:568-576; db/src/collection/index.ts:734-736); nothing resolved in advance.

reads.byWindow.note: Declined by the adapter (tanstack-db.ts:868-871, reason UNINDEXED_WINDOW_IS_ASYNC at tanstack-db.ts:850-856): with autoIndex off and no index, setWindow in 0.15 starts a subset load and returns a promise (db/src/query/live/collection-config-builder.ts:299-410, the promise branch at 392-410), and the harness never yields. The two indexed rows carry this table.

reads.byTwoAxes.note: Second predicate as q.fn.where inside the pipeline (tanstack-db.ts:542-555); a move of a row the predicate excludes produces no output change and no event, so view B is woken only by the library.

reads.bySwitch.note: A live query's where is fixed at construction and setWindow moves offset and limit only, so switchGroup unsubscribes and cleans up the paged live query and builds one over the new group from the same factory (tanstack-db.ts:527-540, 589-594), as useLiveQuery does on a changed dependency. It subscribes with includeInitialState true (tanstack-db.ts:593), whose snapshot requestSnapshot publishes synchronously (db/src/collection/changes.ts:349-355; db/src/collection/subscription.ts:1181-1310), and that is the mark the settle delivers at offset 0. View B is untouched. On this unindexed row the new query loads the whole group; whether that load is synchronous in 0.15 when setWindow's is not was not settled.

relations.note: Three collections on the sync interface; owner and pair live queries via inArray (tanstack-db.ts:646-658); pair records committed before either query exists (tanstack-db.ts:685-704); each line is read back with live.get(owner id) or live.get(pair key) (tanstack-db.ts:662-669); writePair composes the key per call (tanstack-db.ts:713-719). A frame opens a sync transaction only on the collections its writes reach (tanstack-db.ts:77-106).

single.note: TanStack DB has no scalar; one row per value in a collection and a subscribeChanges narrowed by where eq(row.id, name) (tanstack-db.ts:785-812). An equal re-write is dropped by the library's deepEquals at commit (state.ts:1392-1402).

card.summary: TanStack DB 0.15 on its default autoIndex 'off', written through the sync interface (one sync transaction per frame) and read through live queries and subscribeChanges; chain and diamond are live queries over live queries deriving with fn.select, and a view switch builds a new live query. The scroll wiring is declined on this row because an unindexed setWindow returns a promise in 0.15. In 0.15 a committed batch is published inside a scheduler context, so the diamond's join runs once per write on the sync path too, which is what the adapter's departure string now says.
card.body:
## Version

`version` is `0.15.0` (adapters/tanstack-db.ts:864, through `adapterWith`) and
`node_modules/@tanstack/db/package.json` declares `0.15.0`. The adapter also runs
`@tanstack/db-ivm`, installed at `0.2.0`. Source read:
`node_modules/@tanstack/db/src` and `node_modules/@tanstack/db-ivm/src`.

## What the library documents and what the adapter does

The cited recipe is the collection-options-creator guide: a collection whose `sync`
function receives `begin`/`write`/`commit`/`markReady` (`syncedCollectionOf`,
tanstack-db.ts:110-138). The three registered rows share every builder and differ by one
argument, `TIndexing` (tanstack-db.ts:60-69); this row is `'off'`.

- **Write path — the caveat on every number of these three rows.** No write goes
  through `collection.insert/update/delete`, the API an application calls; every
  write is a message on the sync handles a collection-options creator receives
  (`rowsStoreOf`, tanstack-db.ts:145-180), so the optimistic path is never entered and
  nothing here prices it. The optimistic
  path resolves `isPersisted` from the transaction machinery
  (db/src/collection/mutations.ts:229), and `localOnlyCollectionOptions` confirms its
  optimistic writes through the same sync `write` (`confirmOperationsSync`,
  db/src/local-only.ts:209-210, 375-400). Declared in `departure`
  (tanstack-db.ts:836-848).
- **Frame.** See the `frame` wiring: one sync transaction per collection reached
  (tanstack-db.ts:77-106). The upsert's `rows.has` sees visible state, so a frame that
  deletes and re-writes a row sends an `update`; the pending projection merges it onto
  the staged deletion (`{ ...undefined, ...value }`, db/src/collection/state.ts:936-942)
  and the commit does the same onto the deleted key (state.ts:1262-1266), so the full row
  sent by `write` is what is stored. An `insert` over an existing key throws unless it is
  deepEqual to the current value (state.ts:900-914).
- **Partial updates.** `rowUpdateMode: 'partial'` spreads the message onto the stored row
  into a fresh object (state.ts:1262-1266), so a one-column patch is sent as one column
  and the harness's object is not retained on update. Inserts are copied by the adapter.
- **Value check.** The commit compares previous and new visible values with
  `deepEquals` and pushes no event when equal (state.ts:1392-1402). That is the
  library's check, and what drops a note write on the projected window and label-cell
  queries.
- **Delivery timing.** Without an active transaction the scheduler runs a job at once
  (db/src/scheduler.ts:65-69), but 0.15 wraps every collection publication in
  `withPublicationContext` (scheduler.ts:183-216, collection/changes.ts:272-283), so the
  live-query graphs a commit wakes are queued and flushed, in dependency order, before
  `commit()` returns. A live query's `subscribeChanges` callback has therefore run when
  the write returns, and `settle` only renders the flagged views.
- **Read.** `toArray` is `Array.from(values())` (db/src/collection/index.ts:1114-1116,
  777-784), each row enriched with virtual props; the enriched copy is cached per KEY and
  reused while the stored row object is the same (state.ts:167-178, 325-363). `readAll`,
  `readOwners` and `readPairs` return the backing collection's `toArray` as it is
  (tanstack-db.ts:177, 736, 740); the audits compare fields, so the virtual props it adds
  are not read.
- **GC.** `gcTime: 0` disables the collection's GC timer
  (db/src/collection/lifecycle.ts:306-312); every live query is cleaned up explicitly.

## autoIndex 'off'

This row is the library default (db/src/types.ts:785-794, `@default "off"`). Every
ordered live query here logs the warning at db/src/query/compiler/order-by.ts:211-220
and falls back to loading the group. The warning offers two remedies, both registered:
an explicit `createIndex` on rank (`tanstack-db-indexed`) and `autoIndex: 'eager'`
(`tanstack-db-eager`). The adapter header (tanstack-db.ts:49-55) and the three
`departure` strings say exactly that.

## Scroll and switch

On this row the scroll wiring is declined (tanstack-db.ts:868-871): `setWindow`
(collection-config-builder.ts:299-410) runs the window function inside a publication
context and then returns `loadOperation.wait()`, a promise whenever a subset load was
started (collection-config-builder.ts:392-410), which the adapter states happens here
with no index. `scrollTo` (tanstack-db.ts:579-587) is still in the binding and still
throws on a promise, but nothing on this row calls it.

`switchGroup` cannot reuse `setWindow` anyway: the window function moves offset and
limit, and the `where` is compiled into the pipeline. A new live query over the new
group is the library's way.

## Churn read fold

Every churn mount stores its subscriber's read per slot (`churnRead[at]`) at mount and
in the body, and clears it on unmount (tanstack-db.ts:358, 389, 400, 417, 422, 463, 468,
500, 505), so the verify pass's fold over every standing subscriber
(harness/render.ts:124-141) checks each one's own source.

## Hoisting

Nothing is hoisted: the sync interface is addressed by key and hands back no handle.
`pin` copies the harness's ids for the `inArray` filter (tanstack-db.ts:280-292), which
is address, not value. `holdRelation` commits the pair records before the queries exist
(tanstack-db.ts:685-704), so no timed step mints. No chain or diamond level caches a
value: every read is out of the head or join collection the library maintains.

## Code volume

The figures are `npm run lines`' cell for each wiring: its builder, every helper it
reaches and every constant it reads, comments and blank lines excluded. Every wiring
pays for the collection-options-creator contract — a collection whose `sync` callback
hands out `begin`/`write`/`commit` (tanstack-db.ts:110-138) and the frame that keeps one
sync transaction open per collection (:78-107) — and the six row writes as sync
messages, insert and update told apart by `has` (:146-181), because the sync interface
is the only synchronous write path (see Write path).

- **churn.row** adds a `subscribeChanges` per subscriber with its `where` (:385-402) and
  the unmount (:353-360).
- **relations** adds two more collections on the same contract (:628-629), two
  `inArray` live queries and their change flags (:647-659), and the per-line reads
  (:662-669). The library has no relation primitive short of a join query, so each type
  is its own collection.
- **bind** adds one ordered, limited, projected live query per view (:229-247), the two
  per-column cell queries (:255-293) and the audit query for `groupOrder` (:206-215).

## Not determined

- That the diamond's join runs once per write under the publication context; derived
  from the scheduler and changes source above, not run.
- That `get(id)` on a live query is keyed by the source row's key — `head.get(id)` on a
  live query built `from` another live query, and the cell, owner and pair reads
  (tanstack-db.ts:270-273, 661-668); read from the compiler keeping the source key
  through `finalizeRow(key, …)` (db/src/query/compiler/index.ts:1274-1278), not run.
- That `includeInitialState: true` on the rebuilt, unindexed paged query delivers its
  rows synchronously in 0.15, given that the adapter declares the unindexed `setWindow`
  asynchronous.
- Time effects of every claim on this card.

bind.note: Identical body to tanstack-db (bindWith('eager') through adapterWith, adapters/tanstack-db.ts:858-892, 905-917): projected window queries (tanstack-db.ts:227-245) and, after pin, one projected live query per cell column (tanstack-db.ts:253-273). Under eager the orderBy compiler calls ensureIndexForField on the first order key (node_modules/@tanstack/db/src/query/compiler/order-by.ts:180-197), so an auto:rank index is built and the ordered query lazy-loads instead of warning.

bindPerGroup.note: Fifty projected live queries over one eagerly indexed collection (tanstack-db.ts:891); the first one mints auto:rank and the rest find it (db/src/indexes/auto-index.ts:40-47).

frame.note: One sync transaction per collection the frame reaches, as on tanstack-db (tanstack-db.ts:77-106). Each committed batch with events also updates every index on the collection before it is emitted (db/src/collection/state.ts:1408-1411).

churn.row.note: subscribeChanges with where eq(row.id, …) (tanstack-db.ts:384-401). Under eager the subscription constructor calls ensureIndexForExpression (db/src/collection/subscription.ts:231-234), so the first mount on a churn binding's collection (created at tanstack-db.ts:334 through `syncedCollectionOf`, :111-139) builds an auto:id index over the population inside a timed cycle (auto-index.ts:58-73), and every later mount scans the index list to find it (auto-index.ts:40-47). That is what eager does for this call; declared in departure (tanstack-db.ts:909-912). Per-slot reads feed the verify pass's read fold as on tanstack-db.

churn.wide.note: where inArray(row.id, sources) (tanstack-db.ts:393-396); inArray compiles to 'in', an indexable operation (db/src/query/builder/functions.ts:707-714), so it shares the auto:id index. The body reads the first source alone, which is what churnWide's model expects; declared (tanstack-db.ts:846-848).

churn.column.note: A select(id, label) live query per subscriber (tanstack-db.ts:402-423), TanStack DB's only column narrowing.

churn.chain.note: depth live queries deriving chainLevelOf with fn.select, built in the mount and cleaned up in the unmount (tanstack-db.ts:424-469, 352-359); as on tanstack-db.

churn.diamond.note: Two fn.select branches over root `from` and an innerJoin live query over both selecting diamondJoinOf (tanstack-db.ts:470-505). Eager changes how the branches load, not when the graphs run: in 0.15 each committed batch is published inside withPublicationContext (db/src/scheduler.ts:183-216; db/src/collection/changes.ts:272-283) and the join is scheduled with its branches as dependencies (db/src/query/live/graph-scheduler.ts:13-29), so it runs once per write. Read, not run; the adapter's departure says the same (tanstack-db.ts:843-845).

reads.byKey.note: collection.get per key (tanstack-db.ts:568-576).

reads.byWindow.note: Supplied on this row (only the 'off' row declines it, tanstack-db.ts:868-871). paged.utils.setWindow({ offset, limit }) (tanstack-db.ts:579-587) runs the window function that moves db-ivm's top-K in place (db/src/query/live/collection-config-builder.ts:299-410, 881-889; db-ivm/src/operators/topKWithFractionalIndex.ts:59, 68) inside a publication context, and returns true when no subset load was started (collection-config-builder.ts:392-396); rows a moved window needs come through the lazy load the auto:rank index serves. The binding throws if setWindow ever returns a promise.

reads.byTwoAxes.note: q.fn.where inside the pipeline (tanstack-db.ts:542-555); the library decides when view B changes.

reads.bySwitch.note: A new paged live query over the new group, the old one unsubscribed and cleaned up, marked by its own includeInitialState snapshot (tanstack-db.ts:527-540, 589-594). Under eager the auto:rank index the first paged query minted is found again by the new one's orderBy compile (auto-index.ts:40-47 returns on an existing index matching field and compare options), so the switch lazy-loads the new group's first window rather than the whole group.

relations.note: As on tanstack-db (tanstack-db.ts:622-753), with all three collections on eager: each is built by `syncedCollectionOf`, which passes `autoIndexOf(indexing)` (tanstack-db.ts:122, 626-628).

single.note: A row per value and subscribeChanges narrowed by where eq(row.id, …) (tanstack-db.ts:785-812); under eager holdSingle's first subscription builds the auto:id index, untimed, and every write then maintains it.

improvements: Create the backing collection for the churn and single wirings with autoIndex 'off', if this row is meant to measure eager only where it serves a query (every collection takes its autoIndex from `syncedCollectionOf`, tanstack-db.ts:122). Not done: what the row stands for is the registry owner's decision; the departure states what eager does there.
card.summary: The same adapter as tanstack-db with autoIndex 'eager' on every backing collection, one of the two remedies the library's orderBy warning offers. On the churn and single wirings eager builds an index on id that only the column, chain and diamond mounts' initial loads read; the scroll wiring is supplied here because an indexed window moves synchronously. Under 0.15's publication context the diamond's join runs once per write, as on tanstack-db.
card.body:
## Version

`version` is `0.15.0` (adapters/tanstack-db.ts:864, through `adapterWith`) and
`node_modules/@tanstack/db/package.json` declares `0.15.0`; `@tanstack/db-ivm` is
installed at `0.2.0`.

## Relation to tanstack-db

The three rows share every builder; the only argument is `TIndexing`
(tanstack-db.ts:60-69), and this row is `'eager'`. Everything on the `tanstack-db` card
about the sync write path, the one-sync-transaction frame (db/src/collection/sync.ts:
285-313), the partial merge (db/src/collection/state.ts:1262-1266), the `deepEquals`
value check that drops note writes on the projected queries (state.ts:1392-1402),
delivery before `commit()` returns under the publication context
(db/src/scheduler.ts:183-216), the chain and diamond shapes, the switch, the churn read
fold, the read through `toArray` (db/src/collection/index.ts:1114-1116) and the code
volume applies here unchanged and is not repeated. The one wiring that differs in kind is
`reads.byWindow`: declined on `tanstack-db`, supplied here. Registering several
configurations is allowed by BENCHMARKING.md §4 at the repository root.

## What 'eager' does in these wirings

`autoIndex: 'eager'` requires `defaultIndexType`; the constructor throws without it
(db/src/collection/index.ts:476-483), and the adapter passes `BTreeIndex`
(tanstack-db.ts:125): eager builds every auto index with that one type
(auto-index.ts:57-70), and BasicIndex's own doc says "Use BTreeIndex for write-heavy
workloads with large collections" (db/src/indexes/basic-index.ts:28-36), which is
what a rank rewritten across ten thousand rows is. The installed type documentation describes eager as
"Automatically create indexes for simple where expressions in subscribeChanges" and
`'off'` as the default, "Use explicit indexes for better bundle size"
(db/src/types.ts:785-794) — that is `tanstack-db-indexed`. The orderBy warning offers
eager as one of two remedies (db/src/query/compiler/order-by.ts:211-220).
`ensureIndexForField` mints only when `autoIndex === 'eager'`
(db/src/indexes/auto-index.ts:10-15, 29-56). It is reached from:

- the orderBy compiler, for the first order key of an ordered query
  (order-by.ts:180-197) — the `rank` index the window and paged queries use;
- every `subscribeChanges` with a `where`, through `ensureIndexForExpression`
  (db/src/collection/subscription.ts:231-234, auto-index.ts:86-100);
- an ordered `currentStateAsChanges` (db/src/collection/change-events.ts:335-350);
- join and include compilation for lazy targets (db/src/query/compiler/joins.ts:490-494,
  compiler/index.ts:808-820) — reachable by the diamond's innerJoin against the branch
  live query collections, which are created without `autoIndex` and so take the default,
  off.

Whether the live query's own subscription to the backing collection passes its `group`
predicate as a `whereExpression` (and so builds a `group` index) was not traced.

On the churn wiring every row subscriber is `subscribeChanges` with `where` on `id`
(tanstack-db.ts:384-401). The first mount on the binding's collection builds `auto:id`
over every row (auto-index.ts:58-73); each mount after it runs
`Array.from(collection.indexes.values()).find(...)` before returning
(auto-index.ts:40-47). Every write that emits an event then updates that index
(state.ts:1408-1411). The row and wide subscribers ask for no initial state, so they
never read it; the column, chain and diamond mounts build live queries whose initial load
can go through it.

## Hoisting

Nothing is hoisted beyond what `tanstack-db` hoists: the sync interface returns no
handle.

## Not determined

- Which indexes exist on the backing collection under `bind` beyond `rank`.
- That a moved window, and the switched query's first window, are filled synchronously
  by the lazy load (no subset promise); read from source, not run.
- That the rebuilt paged query finds the existing `auto:rank` index instead of minting a
  second one; read from auto-index.ts and order-by.ts, not run.
- How often a churn binding (and so its `auto:id` build) is created per process; the
  index lives on the binding's collection.
- The diamond running once per write; derived from the scheduler source, not run.
- The cost of the `auto:id` index on the churn rows, and the time effect of every claim
  on this card. Nothing was run.

bind.note: Identical body to tanstack-db (bindWith('explicit') through adapterWith, adapters/tanstack-db.ts:858-892, 919-932), plus two indexes created right after the backing collection and before any live query (tanstack-db.ts:221-224): group with BasicIndex, rank with BTreeIndex. rank is the first order key of the window queries, so the orderBy compiler finds it (node_modules/@tanstack/db/src/query/compiler/order-by.ts:199-207; utils/index-optimization.ts:45-70) instead of warning and loading the whole group. An id BTreeIndex is created in pin, before the pinned-cell queries that filter on id with inArray (tanstack-db.ts:288, 253-268), so only the cell scripts, the ones that call pin, maintain it.

bindPerGroup.note: Fifty projected live queries over one explicitly indexed collection (tanstack-db.ts:891).

frame.note: One sync transaction per collection the frame reaches, as on tanstack-db (tanstack-db.ts:77-106). Each committed batch with events updates the explicit indexes before it is emitted (db/src/collection/state.ts:1408-1411).

churn.row.note: subscribeChanges with where eq(row.id, …) (tanstack-db.ts:384-401). An id BTreeIndex exists on this collection (tanstack-db.ts:335-337), built at bind, untimed; these subscriptions ask for no initial state and do not read it. autoIndex is off, so ensureIndexForExpression mints nothing (db/src/indexes/auto-index.ts:10-15, 86-93) and no mount builds an index; outside dev mode it returns before searching the list. Per-slot reads feed the verify pass's read fold as on tanstack-db.

churn.wide.note: where inArray(row.id, sources) (tanstack-db.ts:393-396); the body reads the first source alone, which is what churnWide's model expects; declared (tanstack-db.ts:846-848).

churn.column.note: A select(id, label) live query per subscriber (tanstack-db.ts:402-423); its initial load of the one row can go through the id index.

churn.chain.note: depth live queries deriving chainLevelOf with fn.select (tanstack-db.ts:424-469), cleaned up on unmount (tanstack-db.ts:352-359); level 1's inArray over the roots can load through the id index (every index supports 'in': db/src/indexes/base-index.ts:174; db/src/query/builder/functions.ts:707-714).

churn.diamond.note: Two fn.select branches over root `from`, each loading its one row through the id index, and an innerJoin live query over both selecting diamondJoinOf (tanstack-db.ts:470-505). Indexes change how the branches load, not when the graphs run: in 0.15 each committed batch is published inside withPublicationContext (db/src/scheduler.ts:183-216; db/src/collection/changes.ts:272-283) and the join is scheduled with its branches as dependencies (db/src/query/live/graph-scheduler.ts:13-29), so it runs once per write. Read, not run; the adapter's departure says the same (tanstack-db.ts:843-845).

reads.byKey.note: collection.get per key (tanstack-db.ts:568-576); a keyed get reads the state map, not an index (db/src/collection/index.ts:734-736).

reads.byWindow.note: Supplied on this row (only the 'off' row declines it, tanstack-db.ts:868-871). group (BasicIndex) and rank (BTreeIndex) on the read binding's backing collection (tanstack-db.ts:522-525). paged.utils.setWindow({ offset, limit }) (tanstack-db.ts:579-587) moves the top-K window (db/src/query/live/collection-config-builder.ts:299-410) and returns true when no subset load was started (collection-config-builder.ts:392-396); a window that needs rows not yet loaded is filled through the lazy load the rank index serves. The binding throws if setWindow ever returns a promise.

reads.byTwoAxes.note: q.fn.where inside the pipeline (tanstack-db.ts:542-555); the library decides when view B changes.

reads.bySwitch.note: A new paged live query over the new group, the old one unsubscribed and cleaned up, marked by its own includeInitialState snapshot (tanstack-db.ts:527-540, 589-594). The new query's orderBy finds the same rank index, so its first window lazy-loads instead of loading the group.

relations.note: As on tanstack-db (tanstack-db.ts:622-753), with a BTreeIndex on owner id and on pair key (tanstack-db.ts:629-632), the columns the two relation live queries filter on with inArray (tanstack-db.ts:646-658). The rows collection carries none: no relation query reads it.

single.note: A row per value and subscribeChanges narrowed by where eq(row.id, …) (tanstack-db.ts:785-812). No index: neither subscription reads initial state, so one would be maintained on every write and read by nothing; the departure says so (tanstack-db.ts:926-927).

card.summary: The same adapter as tanstack-db with autoIndex 'off' and explicit collection.createIndex on what each wiring's live queries filter and sort on, the remedy the library's orderBy warning names first and the configuration its type docs recommend. The scroll wiring is supplied here because an indexed window moves synchronously; under 0.15's publication context the diamond's join runs once per write, as on tanstack-db.

## Version

`version` is `0.15.0` (adapters/tanstack-db.ts:864, through `adapterWith`; the export
is tanstack-db.ts:919-932) and `node_modules/@tanstack/db/package.json` declares
`0.15.0`; `@tanstack/db-ivm` is installed at `0.2.0`. The row is registered in
`src/harness/registry.ts:41`.

## Relation to tanstack-db

The three rows share every builder; the only argument is `TIndexing`
(tanstack-db.ts:60-69), and this row is `'explicit'`. `autoIndex` is `'off'`
(`autoIndexOf`, tanstack-db.ts:62-63), so nothing is minted by a subscription or a
compile; every index on this row is a `createIndex` call made at bind, before the first
live query, and so built over an empty collection and maintained by the load. Everything
on the `tanstack-db` card about the sync write path, the frame, the partial merge, the
`deepEquals` value check, delivery under the publication context, the chain and diamond
shapes, the switch, the churn read fold and the code volume applies here unchanged and is
not repeated, beyond the `createIndex` calls each wiring adds. The one wiring that
differs in kind is `reads.byWindow`: declined on `tanstack-db`, supplied here.

## What the library documents, and what this row follows

- The type docs: `autoIndex` `"off"` is the default, "No automatic indexing (default).
  Use explicit indexes for better bundle size." (db/src/types.ts:785-794).
- The orderBy warning: "Consider creating an index on the collection with
  collection.createIndex((row) => row.rank) or enable auto-indexing with autoIndex:
  'eager' and a defaultIndexType." (db/src/query/compiler/order-by.ts:211-220). This row
  is the first remedy; `tanstack-db-eager` is the second.
- `createIndex` takes an expression callback and `{ indexType }`, falling back to the
  collection's `defaultIndexType` and throwing when neither is set
  (db/src/collection/indexes.ts:284-300). The adapter passes `BTreeIndex` as the default
