  (tanstack-db.ts:125) and names `indexType` on every explicit index, so the default
  decides nothing on this row.
- Index type: `BasicIndex` is "Map + sorted Array … O(n) updates to maintain sort order
  … Use BTreeIndex for write-heavy workloads with large collections"
  (db/src/indexes/basic-index.ts:28-36). `group` has fifty distinct values, so a sorted
  array of them is cheap and `BasicIndex` is kept; `rank` and `id` have one value per
  row and the scripts write rank, so they get `BTreeIndex`. Both index types skip the
  bucket and tree work when an update leaves the indexed value unchanged
  (btree-index.ts:109-131, basic-index.ts:148-169), but each still evaluates the index
  expression twice and moves a per-domain counter (base-index.ts:277-293), so a label or
  note write pays that per index.
- Which fields: the ones a live query of that wiring filters on, and the first order
  key, because the orderBy compiler consults an index only for the first one
  (order-by.ts:180-207). Fields nothing reads (the rows collection under relations, the
  values collection under single) get no index; the read binding indexes group and rank
  but not id, since its only id access is a keyed get (tanstack-db.ts:522-525); the
  window binding indexes id only once `pin` builds queries that filter on it.

## Hoisting

Nothing is hoisted beyond what `tanstack-db` hoists: an index is the library's own
structure, built and maintained by it.

## Not determined

- That the explicit `rank` index matches the orderBy's compare options and direction
  (`matchesCompareOptions` / `matchesDirection`, db/src/indexes/base-index.ts:321-370,
  utils/index-optimization.ts:58-67; the query side from `buildCompareOptions`,
  order-by.ts:394), so the warning is silenced and lazy loading used; both default to
  `DEFAULT_COMPARE_OPTIONS` by reading, not run.
- That the live query's initial load of an `inArray` / `eq` on `id` goes through the id
  index rather than a scan; read from `requestSnapshot` passing its `whereExpression` to
  `currentStateAsChanges` (db/src/collection/subscription.ts:1181-1270), not traced
  further, not run.
- Whether BasicIndex or BTreeIndex is the faster choice for `group` under the move
  scripts; chosen from the library's own guidance, not measured.
- The diamond running once per write; derived from the scheduler source, not run.
- Time effects of every choice on this card. Nothing was run.

bind.note: One DynamicView per view, applyFind({group}) plus applySortCriteria (adapters/lokijs.ts:111-125), each wrapped by a 'rebuild' listener (lokijs.ts:80-86). settle calls performSortPhase() on every view (lokijs.ts:89-93, 168-174): it returns at once when neither sortDirty nor resultsdirty is set (node_modules/lokijs/src/lokijs.js:4711-4715) and otherwise re-sorts and emits 'rebuild' (lokijs.js:4737-4739), and only then is data() read and delivered. A view is dirtied only when the written document was or becomes part of it (lokijs.js:4780-4783), so a write to group A does not redeliver view B. The re-sort per settled step is the library's passive design under a per-step settle; declared in departure (lokijs.ts:986-997).

bindPerGroup.note: The same body with fifty DynamicViews (lokijs.ts:1053); a write dirties one view (two on a move), so one or two of the fifty are re-sorted and delivered per settle.

frame.note: frame runs its writes directly (lokijs.ts:95-96, used at 248, 412, 620, 843, 960). LokiJS has no notification batch: Collection.startTransaction only snapshots data and indexes for rollback when the collection is transactional (lokijs.js:7095-7107), and the emitter calls every listener synchronously per event (lokijs.js:831-850). A passive view already coalesces a frame's writes into one re-sort at the next settle; the churn, relation and single listeners fire once per write. Declared in departure (lokijs.ts:991-992).

churn.row.note: LokiJS has no per-document subscription; each subscriber is a collection 'update'/'delete' listener that tests the document id and reads the label off the emitted document (lokijs.ts:350-354, 443-452). Every subscriber runs on every write. Each read is stored per slot and cleared on unmount (lokijs.ts:449, 451, 481), which is what the verify pass's read fold checks. Declared in departure (lokijs.ts:993-995).

churn.wide.note: One listener testing membership in a Set of the sources and reading every source through the unique index, keeping the first one's label (lokijs.ts:454-470), which is what churnWide's model expects every subscriber to read (scenarios.ts:2149-2154).

churn.column.note: Declined by the adapter (lokijs.ts:472, reason at 1010-1017), and the reason holds in the library: update is document-level and, with clone off and the delta changes API at its default (disabled), the emitted old document is the same object as the new one (lokijs.js:6058, 6062, 6126), so LokiJS cannot say which field moved.

churn.chain.note: Declined by the adapter (lokijs.ts:473, reason at 1018-1024): a DynamicView cannot take another view as its source and the collection emitter has no per-source channel, so a chain could only be the wide listener with the depth levels re-run by hand in its body. Removes lokijs from churnChain and chainFrameWrite.

churn.diamond.note: Declined by the adapter (lokijs.ts:474, reason at 1025-1031): LokiJS's derived structures are DynamicViews and Resultsets, filtered and sorted lists over one collection, and nothing computes a value from two others; the branches and the join could only be functions the adapter calls by hand inside a collection listener, which the contract forbids.

reads.byKey.note: by('id', key) per key, a hash hit on the unique index (lokijs.ts:599-607; lokijs.js:7003-7017, UniqueIndex.get 7559-7561).

reads.byWindow.note: scrollTo sets a number (lokijs.ts:611-614) and settle slices the view's sorted list (lokijs.ts:622-624). The paged view is persistent (lokijs.ts:510-513), so a clean read returns the maintained resultdata instead of copying the group (lokijs.js:4653-4661).

reads.byTwoAxes.note: applyWhere for the axis inside the view's pipeline (lokijs.ts:521-531). View B is delivered only when performSortPhase reports it rebuilt (lokijs.ts:625-627), so a document its applyWhere excludes before and after does not wake it (lokijs.js:4780-4783). The view is not persistent: no script scrolls view B, so it is read only when dirty, where a persistent view copies just the same (performSortPhase, lokijs.js:4730-4734) and keeps resultdata in step on every write besides; see lokijs.md.

reads.bySwitch.note: The paged view's group filter is registered with a uid (lokijs.ts:497, 514); switchGroup resets the offset and calls applyFind({group}, uid) with the new group (lokijs.ts:616-619). applyFilter replaces the pipeline entry with that uid and calls reapplyFilters (lokijs.js:4533-4545), which resets the Resultset, re-runs the find over the whole collection, empties resultdata and queues the sort (lokijs.js:4496-4523); the next settle's performSortPhase re-sorts and emits 'rebuild', and the view is delivered at offset 0. View B is untouched. This is LokiJS's own way to change a DynamicView's filter. The viewSwitch script writes nothing between switches (scenarios.ts:4535-4554), so every step is this re-filter alone.

relations.note: Three collections, each view re-read only when its own collection emitted (lokijs.ts:791-823, 845-854); writePair composes the key and probes the unique index on it per call (lokijs.ts:834-842).

single.note: One collection, two listeners on 'update' each testing the document id (lokijs.ts:923-948); LokiJS has no scalar and no per-document listener. LokiJS compares no values, so an equal write wakes the subscriber.

improvements: A binary index on group (ensureIndex / indices: ['group']) on the read binding's collection (lokijs.ts:508) would be consulted by the switch's fresh find (Resultset.find checks indices only while filterInitialized is false, lokijs.js:3547-3549), moving bySwitch from a whole-collection scan to an index range. It is a trade-off, not a fix: the index is maintained on every write of every read script and is read by none of the others (src/adapters/lokijs.md). Not done; a consumer of this table would pick it only for a switch-heavy workload.
card.summary: LokiJS DynamicViews over one collection, each delivered only when LokiJS itself dirtied it (performSortPhase emits 'rebuild' synchronously for a dirty view and returns at once for a clean one); collections run with the documented disableMeta; LokiJS has no notification batch, so a frame runs its writes directly; a view switch replaces the paged view's group filter by its uid; the column, chain and diamond churn shapes are declined.
card.body:
## Version

`version` is `1.5.12` (adapters/lokijs.ts:984) and
`node_modules/lokijs/package.json` declares `1.5.12`. The code read is
`node_modules/lokijs/src/lokijs.js`.

## What LokiJS documents and what the adapter does

The cited recipe is the DynamicView (techfort.github.io/LokiJS/DynamicView.html): a
filter pipeline and a sort registered once, re-evaluated per document as writes land.

- **Writes.** The adapter mutates the stored document and hands it back to `update`,
  the documented idiom with cloning off (the collection default, lokijs.js:5021). The
  upsert is `by('id')` then batched `insert`/`update`; `update(array)` loops
  `update(doc)` (lokijs.js:6012-6037). LokiJS compares no values: every `update` re-runs
  every DynamicView's `evaluateDocument` (lokijs.js:6079-6081), whose `indexOf` over the
  view's `filteredrows` is linear in the group (lokijs.js:4765). That cost is the
  library's.
- **Collections.** Every collection is created with `{ unique: [key], disableMeta: true }`
  (lokijs.ts:73-76). `disableMeta` is a documented collection option (lokijs.js:4946,
  5030) that skips the `meta` stamp, a `Date` and two field writes per update
  (lokijs.js:5238-5248); it requires the changes API off and no TTL (lokijs.js:1175-1184),
  which is this configuration.
- **Views.** `applyFind({ group })` plus
  `applySortCriteria([['rank', false], ['id', false]])`. The sort runs in
  `performSortPhase` through `compoundsort` (lokijs.js:4711-4743, 3321). No binary index
  is built; `src/adapters/lokijs.md` argues that the views are fed through
  `evaluateDocument`, which runs the pipeline over a one-element Resultset with
  `filterInitialized` already true, and `find` consults an index only when
  `filterInitialized` is false (lokijs.js:3547-3549, 4770-4777). The source agrees. The
  view switch is the exception (see `improvements`).
- **Signal.** LokiJS's own per-view signal is the `rebuild` event. On a passive sorted
  view a write calls `queueSortPhase`, which marks `sortDirty` and queues a `setTimeout`
  that emits `rebuild` later (lokijs.js:4687-4705, 4667-4680). The harness never yields,
  so that timer never fires inside a measurement. `settle` calls `performSortPhase()`
  instead, which emits `rebuild` synchronously when the view was dirty and returns
  early otherwise (lokijs.js:4711-4739). The listener's flag is cleared immediately
  before each call (lokijs.ts:89-93), so a timer that did fire between settles cannot
  cause a delivery; nothing depends on it firing.
- **Frame.** See the `frame` wiring: there is no API that defers notification across
  writes, so `frame` is a direct call (lokijs.ts:96).
- **View switch.** `applyFind(query, uid)` is documented as "Adds or updates a
  mongo-style query option in the DynamicView filter pipeline" (lokijs.js:4566-4573);
  with a uid already in the pipeline it replaces that entry and re-applies every filter
  (lokijs.js:4533-4545, 4496-4523). The reset Resultset runs a fresh find over the
  collection, so a switch costs a scan of the population plus a re-sort of the new
  group; that is the library's price for changing a view's definition.

## Declared departures, checked

- Collection-wide subscription on the churn rows: LokiJS's emitter has no per-document
  channel (lokijs.js:831-850), so every subscriber runs on every write
  (lokijs.ts:350-354). Declared (lokijs.ts:993-995).
- `churn.column`, `churn.chain` and `churn.diamond` declined, with reasons in the
  adapter (lokijs.ts:1009-1032). For the column: `update` emits `(returnObj, oldInternal)`
  (lokijs.js:6126); with cloning off `newInternal` is the document passed in
  (lokijs.js:6062) and `oldInternal` is the stored reference (lokijs.js:6058), the same
  object when the caller mutated it in place.
- The cell wiring after `pin` has no DynamicView, so it is driven by the collection
  emitter's flag (lokijs.ts:132-141, 176-180).

## Churn read fold

Every supplied churn mount stores its subscriber's read per slot at mount and in the
body and clears it on unmount (lokijs.ts:441, 449, 451, 468, 470, 481), so the verify
pass's fold over every standing subscriber (harness/render.ts:124-141) checks each one's
own source. Scripts on the declined shapes have no lokijs row.

## Hoisting

`pin` resolves the pinned documents once through the unique index (lokijs.ts:254-269)
and `holdRelation` resolves owner and pair documents once (lokijs.ts:791-823) — handles,
not values. `holdChurnRows` resolves nothing; every read in a churn body is either the
emitted document or a `by` lookup. `readKeys` resolves nothing in advance
(lokijs.ts:599-607).

## Not determined

- Whether the per-view delivery keeps every digest unchanged. By the reading above it
  only removes deliveries of views LokiJS left clean, whose text equals the previous
  one; not run.
- The persistent paged view's correctness under removals rests on `removeDocument`
  keeping `resultdata` aligned with `filteredrows` (lokijs.js:4878-4896); read, not run.
- That `reapplyFilters` on a persistent view leaves `resultdata` equal to the switched
  group's sorted rows after the next `performSortPhase` (lokijs.js:4496-4523,
  4730-4734); read, not run.
- Time effects of every claim on this card.

bind.note: computed + autorun per view over an observable.set bucket of row observables (adapters/mobx.ts:122-141). Rows are MobxRow instances (mobx.ts:51-71, created at mobx.ts:166) whose constructor calls makeObservable with group, rank, label and note annotated observable; id is a plain field. makeObservable goes through asObservableObject on the instance (node_modules/mobx/src/api/makeObservable.ts:22-34), which defines cached accessors directly on it (src/types/observableobject.ts:358-403, 676-688) rather than building the Proxy observable({ ...row }) builds in MobX 7 (src/api/observable.ts:209-216; src/types/dynamicobject.ts:54-60). The window computed uses compareShallow (mobx.ts:129; src/utils/comparer.ts:15-17), so a recompute that selects the same row objects in the same order does not re-run the autorun (src/core/computedvalue.ts:259-283). For a key already held all four fields are assigned unconditionally (mobx.ts:171-175); the no-change check is MobX's own prepareNewValue_ (src/types/observablevalue.ts:116-131, reached from src/types/observableobject.ts:155-178).

bindPerGroup.note: The same body with fifty views (mobx.ts:1005), each computed over its own group's bucket, so the dependency sets are disjoint.

frame.note: frame is runInAction around the script's writes (mobx.ts:47-49; src/api/action.ts:93-95; dist/mobx.cjs.development.js:2472, cited at mobx.ts:46), used by every wiring (mobx.ts:274, 408, 649, 834, 939). Each write method is itself a runInAction, which nests, so reactions wait for the frame's outermost action and settle is a no-op on the window wiring (mobx.ts:275).

churn.row.note: One autorun per subscriber over a resolved row observable (mobx.ts:338-349, 448-452). The body reads all four atoms of the row (wholeRow, mobx.ts:353-356) because MobX tracks per property and the row shape subscribes to the whole row (SCENARIOS.md, churnColumn: 'on one column instead of the row'); declared in departure (mobx.ts:965-972). The autorun stores its read per slot on every run including the first, and unmount clears it (mobx.ts:342, 494), which is what the verify pass's read fold checks.

churn.wide.note: One autorun whose body reads every one of the CHURN_WIDE rows whole and keeps the first one's label (mobx.ts:453-459), so MobX registers it on every source atom; the first label is what churnWide's model expects.

churn.column.note: autorun reading row.label alone (mobx.ts:463-466); a MobX property is its own atom, so this is the column with nothing standing for it.

churn.chain.note: depth computeds stacked, built inside the mount (mobx.ts:467-481): the bottom one reads the count roots whole (types.ts / SCENARIOS.md: derivations 'over several rows') and returns chainLevelOf(joined labels, 1), level k returns chainLevelOf(level k-1, k), and the autorun reads the head (harness/derivations.ts:1-13).

churn.diamond.note: Two computeds over the root row read whole (types.ts:69-70, 'two derivations over root row from') deriving diamondLeftOf / diamondRightOf of its label, one computed over both (diamondJoinOf), and the autorun on the join (mobx.ts:482-488). MobX computeds are glitch-free and the reaction runs at the end of the outermost action, so the join and the autorun run once per write. Read, not run.

reads.byKey.note: One ObservableMap.get per key outside any reaction (mobx.ts:630-638), nothing resolved in advance.

reads.byWindow.note: The offset is an observable.box written in an action (mobx.ts:517, 640-642); the paged computed re-runs a top-(offset+window) selection over the group bucket with compareShallow, and the autorun reads the offset itself (mobx.ts:530-540, 551-554). MobX keeps no ordered index, so the re-selection is the library's cost.

reads.byTwoAxes.note: onAxis computed with compareShallow (mobx.ts:541-548): a group move of a row the second predicate excludes leaves the selected objects unchanged, so view B's autorun does not re-run.

reads.bySwitch.note: The group view A selects from is a second observable.box (pagedGroup, mobx.ts:518) that the paged computed reads (mobx.ts:530-540); switchGroup sets it and the offset to 0 in one runInAction (mobx.ts:643-648), so view A's autorun runs once, at the end of the action. View B's computed never reads the box. Read, not run.

relations.note: Owners and pair records are MobxOwner and MobxPair instances, makeObservable with only name and mark annotated (mobx.ts:73-95), held in observable.maps (mobx.ts:767-774, 793); holdRelation resolves them once and mints pair records untimed (mobx.ts:779-814); writePair composes the key per call and does one pairs.get (mobx.ts:826-833).

single.note: observable.box plus autorun (mobx.ts:887-959), MobX's documented scalar; an equal set is dropped by the box's default compareDefault (src/types/observablevalue.ts:71, 131).

card.summary: MobX 7's documented store shape: rows, owners and pair records are class instances annotated with makeObservable (accessors on the instance, no Proxy) held in observable.maps, a computed per view with the shipped compareShallow comparer, an autorun per consumer, every write in an action and every script frame in one runInAction. The chain, the diamond and the view switch are computeds and boxes over observables, nothing derived by hand.
card.body:
## Version

`version` is `7.0.6` (adapters/mobx.ts:963) and `node_modules/mobx/package.json`
declares `7.0.6`. MobX 7 now has an `exports` map; its `node` condition (listed before
`import`) and its `default` both resolve to `dist/index.js`, which picks
`mobx.cjs.production.min.js` only when `NODE_ENV === 'production'`. The worker sets
`NODE_ENV: 'production'` (harness/measureBatch.ts:201). The package ships its
TypeScript source, and line references below are to `node_modules/mobx/src`.

## What MobX documents and what the adapter does

MobX's recipe is observable state, `computed` for derivations, a reaction to push them
out, and writes inside actions (cited `docs`: mobx.js.org/reactions.html#autorun). Its
store shape is a class whose constructor calls `makeObservable`
(mobx.js.org/observable-state.html). The adapter follows it in every wiring:

- Rows are `MobxRow` instances (mobx.ts:51-71): the constructor copies the five fields
  and calls `makeObservable(this, { group, rank, label, note: observable })`. `id` is
  not annotated, because nothing ever writes it. Owners and pair records are `MobxOwner`
  and `MobxPair` (mobx.ts:73-95) of the same kind.
- Every write method wraps its assignments in `runInAction` (e.g. mobx.ts:160-230), so
  reactions run once at the end of the outermost action. `frame` is one more
  `runInAction` (mobx.ts:47-49); see the `frame` wiring. The no-change check is MobX's
  own (`prepareNewValue_`, src/types/observablevalue.ts:116-131), not the adapter's,
  which is what the re-send rule in `TBinding.write` requires.
- The group index (`byGroup`, an `observable.map` of `observable.set`s, mobx.ts:106-118)
  is maintained by the adapter on insert, move and removal. MobX has no index of its
  own, so this is user code a MobX application writes, and it holds the row
  observables, not copies of values.
- The window computed calls the shared `visibleOf` over the bucket (mobx.ts:122-130,
  harness/render.ts:313-354). Inside it MobX tracks `group` of every bucket row and
  `rank` of the rows `compareRows` touches (dataset.ts:423-424), not `label` or `note`;
  `id` is a plain field and tracks nothing. The autorun around it tracks `rank` and
  `label` of the delivered rows (render.ts:31-43). So a label patch outside the window
  wakes nothing, and a `note` patch wakes nothing at all.

## Chain, diamond and view switch

All three use MobX's own `computed`, as the contract asks:

- **Chain** (mobx.ts:467-481). `depth` computeds, the bottom one over the `count` roots,
  each level applying `chainLevelOf` with its own level number, so the head carries
  `chainHeadOf(label, depth)`. The bottom computed reads each root whole (`wholeRow`,
  mobx.ts:353-356), the same four-atom read as the row shape; declared in `departure`.
- **Diamond** (mobx.ts:482-488). Two computeds read the root row whole (`wholeRow`), as
  types.ts:69-70 defines the shape ("two derivations over root row `from`"), and derive
  from its `label`; a third reads both, the autorun reads the third. Declared in
  `departure`.
- **View switch** (mobx.ts:518, 530-540, 643-648). The paged computed reads the group
  from an `observable.box`. The box and the offset are written in one action, so the
  autorun, which reads both the offset and the computed, runs once.

## makeObservable rows and the shallow comparer

**Non-proxy objects.** MobX 7 "now always uses Proxy-backed observable objects and
arrays", and `{ proxy: false }` is "no longer supported" (node_modules/mobx/CHANGELOG.md:
75-77): `observable(obj)` goes through `observable.object`, which always builds
`asDynamicObservableObject`, a `Proxy` (src/api/observable.ts:209-216,
src/types/dynamicobject.ts:54-60). `makeObservable` on a class instance does not: it
calls `asObservableObject(target)` (src/api/makeObservable.ts:22-34), and the
`observable` annotation defines the cached getter/setter descriptors on the instance
itself (src/types/observableobject.ts:358-403, 676-688). A read is the accessor and the
administration's `getObservablePropValue_`, with no `Proxy` `get` trap in front.

**Shallow comparer on the window computeds.** `computed` defaults to `compareDefault`
(`Object.is`), and `visibleOf` returns a fresh array per recompute (render.ts:350-354),
so without a comparer any recompute would re-run the autorun even when it selected the
same rows. `compareShallow` (src/utils/comparer.ts:15-17) is `deepEqual(a, b, 1)`, which
compares the arrays element by element at depth zero, where two distinct objects are
unequal (src/utils/eq.ts:23-28, 112-114). When it says equal, `trackAndCompute` keeps the
previous value (src/core/computedvalue.ts:259-283), so `deliverableRows` still returns
the array last delivered. `compareShallow` is the MobX 7 name for `comparer.shallow`
(CHANGELOG.md:79-93).

## Churn read fold

Every churn subscriber is an autorun that stores what it read per slot on every run
(mobx.ts:338-349) and is cleared on unmount (mobx.ts:494), so the verify pass's fold
over every standing subscriber (harness/render.ts:124-141) checks each one's own source.

## Declared departures, checked

- The row-shaped churn subscriber, the bottom computed of each chain and the two sides
  of each diamond read all four atoms (mobx.ts:353-356). That is the row in MobX's
  terms; reading one property is the column shape (mobx.ts:463-466), which has its own
  table. Declared (mobx.ts:965-972).
- The timed teardown disposes reactions only (mobx.ts:315-320, 496-501); the maps are
  per binding and left to the collector. Declared.

## Hoisting

`pin` resolves the pinned observables once and replaces the window autoruns with two
column autoruns (mobx.ts:234-261). `holdChurnRows` and `holdRelation` resolve
observables once (mobx.ts:439-447, 779-797). All three are the "handle for a key" the
contract allows. `readKeys` resolves nothing in advance (mobx.ts:630-638).

## Not determined

- The time effect of `makeObservable` rows against Proxy-backed `observable({...})`
  rows, and of the chain, diamond and switch wirings. Nothing was run.
- `digest` above was not recomputed against this code.
- Whether `compareShallow` changes any digest. By the reading above it removes only
  deliveries whose text equals the previous one, which the digest does not fold
  (harness/consumer.ts:46-49); not executed.
- Which build a bundled or ESM-loaded worker would pick if resolution did not take the
  `node` condition; the `import` condition points at `dist/mobx.mjs`.

bind.note: Derived atom per view (adapters/jotai.ts:156-161) built by selectIds (jotai.ts:89-124): it reads the group's ids atom, then per id the derived group and rank column atoms, and the label column atom of the ids it renders (columnFamiliesOf, jotai.ts:77-81) — never a row atom. Each column atom returns a primitive, so Object.is (node_modules/jotai/dist/vanilla/internals.js:684) stops a write the view does not read, and the view atom is recomputed only when one of its dependencies changed (hasChangedDeps, internals.js:295-310). The view atom returns the selected ids; its listener reads those rows through store.get and delivers them (rowsOf, jotai.ts:126-133, 162-170). The cell wiring after pin builds a label atom and a note atom per pinned row and subscribes each column's render to its own atoms (jotai.ts:301-333). A recompute that selects the same ids still returns a fresh array; keeping the previous one would need an equality function written here (see improvements).

bindPerGroup.note: The same body with fifty views (jotai.ts:1055), each over its own group's ids atom.

frame.note: frame is one store.set on a write-only frame atom; while it runs, every write method of the binding goes through that atom's get and set (access, jotai.ts:49-71), and a nested frame runs in place. The set a write function is handed does not flush while the outer write is synchronous (internals.js:495-531); only the outermost store.set recomputes and flushes in its finally (internals.js:695-709), cited at jotai.ts:48, so a multi-write frame reaches the listeners as one flush. Used by every wiring (jotai.ts:344, 456, 734, 917, 1007).

churn.row.note: store.sub directly on the resolved row atom for one source (jotai.ts:493-498); the listener reads the atom back through store.get and stores the label per slot (readRowInto, jotai.ts:404-407, 413-416), cleared on unmount (jotai.ts:551), which is what the verify pass's read fold checks.

churn.wide.note: A derived atom built at mount that reads every source atom (jotai.ts:500-510), subscribed; mounting it mounts the CHURN_WIDE sources. The listener reads the first source's row atom, which is what churnWide's model expects.

churn.column.note: A selector atom get(rowAtom).label subscribed (jotai.ts:512-520): a row write recomputes it and Object.is on the string decides whether the listener runs (internals.js:671-690).

churn.chain.note: depth derived atoms built inside the mount (jotai.ts:522-537): the bottom one reads the count root row atoms and returns chainLevelOf(joined labels, 1), level k returns chainLevelOf(get(level k-1), k); store.sub on the head mounts the chain and the roots, and the listener reads the head through store.get (headReaderOf, jotai.ts:409-411, 418-421), so the text is chainHeadOf(label, depth) (harness/derivations.ts:1-13).

churn.diamond.note: Two derived atoms over the root row atom (diamondLeftOf, diamondRightOf of its label), a third reading both (diamondJoinOf), store.sub on the third (jotai.ts:538-545). The store recomputes a flush's invalidated atoms in topological order and only those with a changed dependency (internals.js:229-313), and the flush collects listeners into a Set (internals.js:196-214), so the join is recomputed and its listener called once per write. Read, not run.

reads.byKey.note: rowFamily(key) plus store.get per key (jotai.ts:718-726); store.get outside a read function mounts and tracks nothing.

reads.byWindow.note: offsetAtom (jotai.ts:578) written through the frame-aware setter (jotai.ts:728-730); pagedAtom re-selects the top offset+window ids of the group through the column atoms, reading label only for the ids from the offset on, and returns a fresh { offset, ids } object (jotai.ts:588-602); the listener reads the rows through store.get (jotai.ts:607-616). jotai keeps no ordered index, so the re-selection is the library's cost.

reads.byTwoAxes.note: onAxisAtom (jotai.ts:603-605) reads the same column atoms, and none of a row the second predicate excludes (the axis test comes first, jotai.ts:104-105). A group move of such a row still rewrites the group's ids atom, which onAxisAtom read, so it recomputes and, returning a fresh array, still notifies view B. Keeping the previous array needs a comparator written in the adapter, which the contract forbids.

reads.bySwitch.note: pagedAtom reads the group from pagedGroupAtom beside offsetAtom (jotai.ts:579, 588-602); switchGroup sets both through the write-only atom switchPagedGroup (jotai.ts:580-583, 731-733), so the two writes reach view A's listener as one flush. onAxisAtom never reads pagedGroupAtom. Read, not run.

relations.note: Owner and pair atom families (jotai.ts:771-777); atoms resolved and pair records minted untimed in holdRelation (jotai.ts:822-830, 884-897); writePair composes the key per call and goes through pairFamily (jotai.ts:909-916). Two derived atoms render the two views (jotai.ts:832-847).

single.note: atom(initial) plus store.sub (jotai.ts:967-1027), jotai's own scalar and subscriber; an equal write is dropped by Object.is (internals.js:684).

improvements: NOT APPLIED: the contract forbids it. jotai.ts:89-124 and 588-605: return the previous ids array when the newly selected ids are the same in the same order, through the self-read selectAtom uses (node_modules/jotai/dist/vanilla/utils/selectAtom.js:9-27). jotai ships no array comparator (selectAtom's equalityFn defaults to Object.is and is otherwise the caller's), so the comparison would be a value check written in the adapter, which TBinding.write forbids. With the column atoms in place, the redundant deliveries left are recomputes that select the same ids: filterTwoAxes view B on a move of an excluded row, and batch steps landing in a watched group outside its window.
card.summary: A vanilla jotai 3 store with one atom per row (jotai-family, since jotai 3 no longer ships atomFamily), per-column derived atom families (group, rank, label) under a derived view atom per view that selects ids, store.sub per consumer, a per-column derived atom per pinned cell, derived atoms for the chain and the diamond, and every script frame written through one write-only atom. A note write, or a label write outside the window, stops at the column atoms; a view whose recompute selects the same ids still notifies, because jotai ships no array equality and the adapter may not write one.
card.body:
## Version

`version` is `3.0.1` (adapters/jotai.ts:1031) and `node_modules/jotai/package.json`
declares `3.0.1`. The adapter also bundles `jotai-family`, installed at `1.1.0`
(`getParams` at jotai-family/dist/atomFamily.js:43). jotai 3 no longer exports
`atomFamily` from `jotai/vanilla/utils` (node_modules/jotai/dist/vanilla/utils.js:1-12),
so `jotai-family` is the only family on offer. The code read is
`node_modules/jotai/dist/vanilla/internals.js`.

## What jotai documents and what the adapter does

The cited recipe is the framework-free store (`createStore`, `store.get`, `store.set`,
`store.sub`; docs: jotai.org/docs/core/store). In the installed source:

- `store.set` writes, then in its `finally` recomputes invalidated atoms and flushes
  listeners when anything changed (internals.js:695-709). One top-level `set` is one
  flush, which is why the batch writes go through write-only atoms (jotai.ts:201-269)
  and `settle` is a no-op.
- The `set` a write function is handed writes without flushing while the write is
  synchronous (internals.js:495-531). jotai has no other batching construct, so `frame`
  (jotai.ts:49-71) is one `store.set` on a write-only frame atom; see the `frame` wiring.
- A primitive atom counts as changed only when the new value is not `Object.is` the old
  (internals.js:684). Every row write stores a new object (`{ ...row }`), so a re-send of
  equal values invalidates every row atom; the column atoms over them recompute to equal
  primitives, and the view atoms above are not recomputed (internals.js:295-310). That is
  jotai's equality, not a check the adapter wrote.
- `store.sub` mounts the atom and its dependencies, then recomputes and flushes
  (internals.js:711-727).
- The invalidated atoms of one flush are recomputed after a depth-first topological sort
  of their mounted dependents, each only if a dependency changed (internals.js:229-313),
  so an atom reading two atoms that both changed in the flush is recomputed once, after
  both. This is what the diamond and the column-atom views rely on.

The group index is an ids atom per group holding keys only. A view atom reads it, then
per id the `group` and `rank` column atoms, and `label` for the ids it renders
(jotai.ts:77-124). Each column family is `atomFamily` over a derived atom, which
jotai-family allows ("`initializeAtom` ... can return any kind of atom",
node_modules/jotai-family/README.md:15). `splitAtom` was considered and does not fit:
it splits an array atom into item atoms, and this store keeps one atom per key, not an
array of rows.

## Chain, diamond and view switch

All three are jotai's own derived atoms (`atom(get => …)`):

- **Chain** (jotai.ts:522-537). `depth` derived atoms, each level applying `chainLevelOf`
  with its own number, so the head carries `chainHeadOf(label, depth)`. The listener on
  the head reads the head (`headReaderOf`, jotai.ts:418-421), not the root row, so the
  rendered text is the derivation's output.
- **Diamond** (jotai.ts:538-545). Left and right read the root row atom; the join reads
  left and right. Subscribing to the join mounts all three and the root.
- **View switch** (jotai.ts:579-583, 588-602, 731-733). `pagedGroupAtom` is what the
  paged view atom selects from; one write-only atom sets it and `offsetAtom` to 0, so the
  view never shows the old group at offset 0 or the new group at the old offset.

## Cells and windows route by column

A subscription to a row atom cannot be told which column changed. A derived atom
reading one column returns a primitive, and `Object.is` on it stops propagation.
`pin` builds one such atom per pinned row and column and subscribes the label render to
the label atoms and the note render to the note atoms (jotai.ts:301-333); a listener
subscribed to several atoms runs once per flush, because the flush collects listeners
into a `Set` (internals.js:196-214). A pinned label write therefore wakes the label view
only, as the churn column shape does (jotai.ts:512-520). The window and read views are
built from the same kind of column atom (jotai.ts:77-124), so a `note` write wakes no
view at all.

## Window identity

The window and axis atoms return a fresh array whenever they recompute. A reused buffer
would read as "no change"; keeping the previous array when the selection is equal is
what selectAtom does (selectAtom.js:12-25), but with an equality function supplied by
its caller. Not applied under the contract rule; see `improvements`.

## Churn read fold

Every churn listener stores what it read per slot (jotai.ts:404-421) and unmount clears
the slot (jotai.ts:551), so the verify pass's fold over every standing subscriber
(harness/render.ts:124-141) checks each one's own source.

## Declared departures, checked

- A removal rebuilds each touched group's ids atom once per batch (jotai.ts:237-253).
  Declared (jotai.ts:1033-1036).
- The timed teardown unsubscribes the view atoms only (jotai.ts:373-381). Declared.

## Hoisting

`pin`, `holdChurnRows` and `holdRelation` resolve family atoms once: the handle for a
key, which the contract allows. `readKeys` resolves nothing in advance
(jotai.ts:718-726).

## Not determined

- Whether `store.sub` calls the listener at subscription. `mountAtom` reads a fresh atom
  without marking it changed unless it was already invalidated (internals.js:455-460,
  570-585), so by reading it does not; not run.
- The time and memory effect of the three column families per row (created for every
  row a view reads, kept by the family), and of the cell, frame, chain, diamond and
  switch wirings. Nothing was run.
- `digest` above was not recomputed against this code.

bind.note: One `observe` per view (legend-state.ts:123-159) reading the group's member node with `get()` (:131) and then, per member id, the `group`, `rank` and `label` leaves with `get()` and the row with `peek()` (`trackedRowOf`, :74-79). Writes go through node `set`/`delete` inside `beginBatch`/`endBatch` (:181-228); the group index is written one key at a time, `byGroup[group][id].set(true)` / `.delete()` (`groupIndexOf`, :100-108), so a move or removal is O(1) on it. A `note` write reaches no view listener (:212-214). `frame` is Legend's `batch` (:69-71, wired at :267), and the same `frame` is carried by the churn (:368), read (:596), relation (:722) and single (:870) bindings.

bindPerGroup.note: Same `bindViews` body with fifty bindings (legend-state.ts:926); one `observe` per view (:164), disjoint dependency sets.

churn.row.note: `observe` over `node.get()` of the held row node (legend-state.ts:319-330, :400-404): the whole row, which is what the row shape subscribes to (SCENARIOS.md, churnColumn: 'on one column instead of the row'). Node proxies are resolved once in `holdChurnRows` (:392-399), which the churn contract allows. Each run stores what it read in `churnRead[at]` (:323) and `unmount` clears the slot (:447-453), so the verify-pass fold over every standing subscriber's read (render.ts:124-141) sees exactly the mounted ones. `settle` delivers once per frame only if a reaction woke (:372-382).

churn.wide.note: Same `mountOnRows` body with `count > 1`: one `observe` reading every source row node whole, ending on row `from` (legend-state.ts:405-411).

churn.column.note: `observe` over the leaf `node.label.get()` of held row 0 (legend-state.ts:413-416). The leaf is its own node, so the column identity is the library's, not the adapter's.

churn.chain.note: Level 1 is a Legend `computed` over the `count` source row nodes, each read whole (`labelOfRow`, :332-335), returning `chainLevelOf(joined labels, 1)`; levels 2..depth are each a `computed` returning `chainLevelOf(level below, level)`; an `observe` reads the head, because a computed is idle until read (legend-state.ts:417-433). Derivations over rows, as SCENARIOS.md defines churnChain.

churn.diamond.note: Two Legend `computed`s over root row `from`'s node read whole (`labelOfRow`, :332-335), as types.ts:69-70 defines the shape ('two derivations over root row from'), deriving `diamondLeftOf` / `diamondRightOf` of its label; a third `computed` over both (`diamondJoinOf`), and an `observe` on the join (legend-state.ts:434-446). Whether Legend runs the join once per frame was not traced in index.js; the diamond script's check is what asserts it.

reads.byKey.note: One proxy descent and one `get()` per key, nothing hoisted, outside every `observe` (legend-state.ts:599-607). `peek()` would skip the `updateTracking` call (index.js:1409-1414); with no active tracker that call does nothing, so no difference is expected.

reads.byWindow.note: View A's cursor is an observable node with `group` and `at` leaves (legend-state.ts:473-479), read only by view A's `observe` (:528-537), so a scroll (`cursor.at.set`, :609-611) re-runs A and not B. A re-selects the top `offset + window` of its group from the group's member node through the same leaf reads as `bind` (`selectInto`, :492-525).

reads.byTwoAxes.note: View B is a second `observe` with the second predicate over group A (legend-state.ts:538-545). The predicate reads only the immutable id, so it is tested before any leaf is tracked (:502), and an off-axis row's leaves are not a dependency of B; its arrival or departure still changes group A's member node, which B tracks.

reads.bySwitch.note: `switchGroup` sets the cursor's `group` leaf and resets its `at` leaf to 0 inside one Legend `batch` (legend-state.ts:612-617), so view A's `observe`, which tracks both leaves, re-runs once over the new group's member node. View B tracks neither leaf.

relations.note: Two more observables, owners and pairs keyed by a composed string (legend-state.ts:658-661). Owner and pair nodes for the views are resolved in `holdRelation` (:734-767); `writePair` composes the key and descends the proxy on every call (:775-779), as `TRelationBinding.writePair` requires.

single.note: `observable('')` scalars, one `observe` each, `set` outside a batch notifies before it returns; `settle` delivers only the side that woke (legend-state.ts:820-888).

improvements: legend-state.ts:74-79 — the leaf reads trade one listener per row for three on every view re-run (observe re-subscribes every run, index.js:1550 and setupTracking at :1479). They take the redundant wakes out of patchNote and batchPatchNote; whether the extra listeners slow patchColumn, patchOutsideWindow and batchPatch is unmeasured. If they do, the whole-row `node.get()` is the other documented arm and the two should be priced against each other. Left to the measurement phase.
card.summary: Rows live in one Legend-State observable keyed by id, the group index is a second observable mapping each group to an object keyed by member id and mutated a key at a time, each view is one `observe` over its own group's node and the `group`/`rank`/`label` leaves of each row, so a write wakes only the view over that row's group and a `note` write wakes none; every script frame and every multi-write method runs inside Legend's own `batch`/`beginBatch`; the chain and diamond are Legend `computed`s over whole row nodes and a view switch writes the view's own observable cursor.
card.body:
## Recipe and version

`node_modules/@legendapp/state/package.json` is `2.1.15`, the same as the adapter's
`version` (legend-state.ts:892). The recipe cited in `docs` is the v2 reactivity page:
an `observable` keyed by id (legend-state.ts:114) and one `observe` per consumer
(:123-159). That is the documented shape for a collection. v3 is the current beta line
and is not what is measured; see legend-state.md ('Which line is measured').

## What a view depends on, and what wakes it

- The group index is a second observable mapping each group to an object keyed by
  member id (legend-state.ts:116). A view reads its own group's member node with
  `get()` first (:131), which tracks that node and its children, so adding or deleting
  a member key reaches the view through it; the member values are always `true`.
- Per id, `trackedRowOf` (legend-state.ts:74-79) calls `get()` on the `group` leaf and,
  if the row is in this group, on `rank` and `label`, then takes the row with `peek()`.
  `get()` tracks exactly the node it is called on (index.js:1409-1414) and `peek()`
  tracks nothing (:1415). Those three leaves are what the filter, `compareRows`
  (src/harness/dataset.ts:425-426) and `deliver` (src/harness/render.ts:31-43) read, so
  every write that can change a rendered line still re-runs the view, and a `note`
  write re-runs none.
- A whole-row `set` (a re-send through `write`) reaches the tracked leaves: `updateNodes`
  compares key by key and calls `notify` on every changed child that has listeners
  (index.js:815-990, the `child.listeners` branch). A re-send whose values equal what is
  stored notifies nothing, and leaves the group index untouched (:186-188).
- A whole-row `node.get()` tracks the row node; a child write is reported up through
  `node.parent` (`computeChangesRecursive`, index.js:525-541), so with it `note` writes
  would re-run the view. The leaf reads are the documented fine-grained form of the same
  read. The open cost is under `improvements`.
- Outside a batch, `set` notifies before it returns (index.js:478-496: `runBatch` is
  called when `numInBatch <= 0`), so `settle` is a no-op in the view, read and relation
  bindings (legend-state.ts:270, :619, :781). The churn and single bindings' `settle`
  only turns what the reactions already recorded into one delivery (:372-382, :873-882).

## The derivation shapes and the view switch

The chain and diamond are Legend `computed`s ending in an `observe`, each reading its
root rows whole (`labelOfRow`, legend-state.ts:332-335), as SCENARIOS.md and types.ts
define those shapes; nothing between levels is the adapter's beyond the
`derivations.ts` function each level is defined by. Every churn subscriber records its
read per slot and `unmount` clears it (legend-state.ts:323, :452), which is what the
verify-pass fold of every standing read (render.ts:124-141, enabled by
`auditChurnReads`) checks. The view switch writes two leaves of the observable cursor
view A already reads for its offset; the `batch` around them is what makes it one
re-run and not two.

## Batching

`frame(run)` is Legend's `batch(run)` (legend-state.ts:69-71; index.js:591-610, which is
`beginBatch(); try { fn() } finally { endBatch() }`). Every binding, the single one
included, carries it, so a script's several writes before one `settle()` notify once when
the outermost batch ends. The `beginBatch`/`endBatch` brackets inside `write`, `remove`
and `setGroup`, and the `batch` inside `switchGroup`, nest by `numInBatch`
(index.js:611-630). A `set` inside a batch writes the raw value immediately and defers
only the notification, so the previous-group read in `setGroup` and `write` sees the
earlier writes of the same frame.

## Write paths

- `write` reads each row's previous group as a primitive (`group.peek()`), sets the row,
  and, when the group changed or the row is new, deletes the member key from the old
  group and sets it in the new one (legend-state.ts:181-193). A missing group object is
  created by Legend on the first `set` beneath it (`ensureNodeValue`, index.js:153-165).
- `setGroup` reads the previous group as a primitive leaf first, for the reason in
  legend-state.md ('Reading a previous value out of a node before the write'), then
  writes the row's `group` leaf and the two member keys in one batch (:216-228).
- `remove` deletes the member key and then the row with `delete()`, which removes the
  key (`deleteFn`, index.js:1266-1273), one pair per id (:197-206).
- Every row is stored as a copy (`{ ...row }`, :187), because `set` keeps the reference
  it is given.
- The read binding's write paths are the same code (:549-588).

## Library cost charged to this row, not the adapter

`beginBatch` arms a `setTimeout(onActionTimeout, 0)` when no batch is open
(index.js:611-616), and `endBatch` clears it (:626-627). `updateNodesAndNotify` opens a
batch on every `set` (index.js:1353), and an `observe` re-run opens one too (:1550).
So each un-batched write outside a batch pays a timer arm and clear. Any user of v2
pays this, so it belongs to the library's number. Inside `frame` the timer is armed once
per frame.

## Unverified

Whether a Legend `computed` join runs once per frame in the diamond was not traced.
The time effect of the keyed group index against per-group id arrays was not run.
The leaf-tracking cost question in `improvements` is for the measurement phase.
`digest` above was not recomputed against this code.

bind.note: One store per group, minted on first ask with ONE event, `opsApplied`, carrying an ordered array of write/patch/drop operations reduced by one `.on` that copies the Map at most once per call (effector.ts:74-104, asked through `nodeFor` :161-168), and an id → group-node handle table (:159). One `.map` and `.watch` per view over its own group's store (:210-220). A reducer must return a new reference for Effector to see a change (`e!==r` in the store node, node_modules/effector/effector.mjs line 1); a write wakes only the view over the written row's group. Outside a frame every method fires `opsApplied` with one operation (`send`, :182-194); inside `frame` (`groupFrame`, :196-203) operations queue per store and each touched store's event fires once when `run` returns, so a frame costs one Map copy and one view recompute per touched group, not one per write. A move is a drop on one store and a write on the other, the row read with `getState()` first, after firing the old store's queue if this frame already queued that row (:283-297; effector.md, 'What a frame is to Effector'). Every view's `.map` returns a fresh array (:119-148), so a view's watcher fires whenever its own store updates.

bindPerGroup.note: Same body with fifty bindings (effector.ts:1153): one `.map` per group store, so a write recomputes the one view over the written group, and a frame spread over every group fires one event per group.

churn.row.note: One store per row with its own event (effector.ts:381-387). `count === 1` subscribes with `.updates.watch` on the row store and records the store's current label as the slot's read at mount (:501-510). `.updates` skips the initial call, as effector.md says ('What a mount is'). Each watcher writes `churnRead[at]` (:399-402) and `unmount` clears it (:545-552), so the verify-pass fold over every standing read (render.ts:124-141) sees only mounted subscribers. `frame` is `run()` (:39-41): the three scripts that open a frame here (`churnList`, `appFill`, `appRound`) write distinct rows, so each row store already gets one event per frame (effector.md, 'What a frame is to Effector').

churn.wide.note: `combine` over the source row stores (`joinedOf`, effector.ts:404-420), then `.updates.watch` (:512-514).

churn.column.note: `row store.map(row => row.label)` (effector.ts:516-523). The store's own `===` skip on the derived string is what makes it a column (effector.mjs, `e!==r`). The adapter does not compare anything.

churn.chain.note: Level 1 is the `combine` over the `count` source stores returning `chainLevelOf(label of row from, 1)` (`chainJoinedOf`, effector.ts:422-431); levels 2..depth are each a `.map` returning `chainLevelOf(text, level)`; `.updates.watch` on the head (:524-533). `unmount` calls `clearNode` on every derived node (:545-552), Effector's public teardown.

churn.diamond.note: Two `.map`s of root row `from`'s store (`diamondLeftOf`, `diamondRightOf` of its label) and `combine(left, right, diamondJoinOf)`, with `.updates.watch` on the join (effector.ts:534-544). All three are cleared on unmount (:545-552). That the join runs once per write is left to Effector's kernel; not traced (effector.md, 'The derivation shapes'), and the diamond script's check is what asserts it.

reads.byKey.note: One `getState()` per page and one `Map.get` per key, nothing hoisted (effector.ts:754-763).

reads.byWindow.note: View A's cursor (group and offset) is its own store (effector.ts:678-680). View A is `combine($state, $cursor)` (:719-727) and view B is `$state.map` (:728-730), so a scroll reruns A only (:767). The population is one store here, for the reason in `reads.bySwitch`.

reads.byTwoAxes.note: View B is a `.map` of `$state` with the second predicate over group A (effector.ts:728-730, predicate at :698). One-store granularity: every write in this wiring recomputes both views and copies the population Map; the only timed writes are this script's four moves.

reads.bySwitch.note: `switchGroup` fires `switched` (effector.ts:768), on which the cursor store's reducer returns `{ group, offset: 0 }` (:680): one event, one cursor update, one recompute of view A over the new group's ids in `$state`. View B does not read the cursor. The population stays one store in this wiring because a `combine` fixes its inputs at creation and `TViewConfig` names only two groups at bind; a partition was considered and not made (effector.md, 'Which store the population lives in'), because it would add an id → group lookup to every key `readByKey` measures while four of the five read scripts write nothing.

relations.note: Rows and pairs are each one store (effector.ts:817-861, :866-886), and every owner has its own store and event (:920-930). View A is `combine` over the touched owner stores (:948-956), so a pair write cannot reach it. `writePair` composes the key on every call (:987-992). No relation script opens a frame.

single.note: `createStore('')` with `.on(event, (_, next) => next)` and `.updates.watch` (effector.ts:1030-1096). Re-sending an equal value is skipped by the store's own `===`.

improvements: APPLIED — the window wiring's population is partitioned into one store per group (effector.ts:74-104, :153-363), the layout nanostores' window wiring already uses; a store layout is the adapter's to choose. Unmeasured.

APPLIED 2026-10-20 — a frame in the window and cell wirings is one `opsApplied` event per touched group store with the array of the frame's operations (effector.ts:170-203), replacing one event and one Map copy per write. Expected to move batchPatch, batchPatchNote, patchMostRows, mixedFrame, moveAndReorder and resortWindow; unmeasured.

APPLIED 2026-10-20 — the cell wiring is a `.map` per pinned cell and column over the row's group store and a `combine` per column over its cells (`pinnedTextOf`, effector.ts:234-250), so a label write reaches only the label consumer by Effector's own `===` skip on the cell string. It replaced a `combine` over the whole group stores that rebuilt both columns' arrays on every pinned write. Expected to move cellDelivery; unmeasured.

DECLINED — derive each view into a store created with Effector's documented `updateFilter` option (node_modules/effector/index.d.ts:398) through `sample`, filtering on element-wise identity of the window rows. `updateFilter` is the library's option, but the element-wise comparator handed to it would be written in the adapter, and `TBinding.write` forbids an adapter supplying an equality its library does not ship. Not applied, by ruling.
DECLINED — partitioning the read wiring's population (see `reads.bySwitch`).
card.summary: Effector's own event-store-map-watch model. The window wiring holds one store per group, so a point write copies one group's Map and wakes that group's view alone; the read wiring keeps the population in one store, because a view switch has to re-point view A and a `combine` cannot change its inputs. The churn and relation wirings hold one store per row or owner. Effector 23 exports no batch function; in the window and cell wirings a frame is one event per touched group store carrying the array of the frame's operations, the Effector idiom for a bulk edit, and each pinned cell is its own `.map` down to one column's string.
card.body:
## Version and recipe

`node_modules/effector/package.json` is `23.4.4`, the same as `version`
(effector.ts:1100). The model is Effector's own: events, stores updated by `.on`
reducers, derived stores by `.map` and `combine`, subscriptions by `.watch` or
`.updates.watch`, teardown by `clearNode`.

## Batching

Effector 23's public exports (the export list at the end of
node_modules/effector/effector.mjs) contain no `batch(fn)`. The `batch` flags in
index.d.ts (:525, :541, and `sample`'s config at :1768-1778) belong to `sample` and to
the low-level `step` API and coalesce updates inside one launch, not across separate
event calls. Effector's idiom for a bulk edit is one event whose payload is the array of
changes. In the window and cell wirings `frame(run)` (`groupFrame`, effector.ts:196-203)
queues each operation on the group store it targets and, when `run` returns, fires that
store's one `opsApplied` event with the queue: one launch, one Map copy and one view
recompute per touched group per frame. No value is compared. In the churn, read, relation
and single wirings `frame` is `run()` (:39-41), and no frame there writes one store twice:
churn's three framing scripts write distinct row stores, and no read, relation or single
script opens a frame (effector.md, 'What a frame is to Effector').

## The store layout, per wiring

- `bind` builds its views before any row exists, and `.map`/`combine` fix their inputs
  when created, but the watched groups are known at bind. So the window wiring holds one
  store per group, minted on first ask (effector.ts:161-168), each with one `opsApplied`
  event (:74-104). A point write copies one group's Map, and only that group's view
  recomputes.
- A move is a drop on one store and a write on the other (effector.ts:283-297). The
  write carries the row, read out of the old store with `getState()` in the binding
  method — the same out-of-graph read the churn wiring's patches make (:445-464) —
  because a reducer sees only its own store's state.
- The cell wiring is a `.map` per pinned cell and column over that row's group store,
  returning one string, and a `combine` per column over its cells (`pinnedTextOf`,
  :234-250; `pin`, :301-324). `.map` skips a `===` result, so a label write updates one
  label cell, the note `combine` does not recompute, and the note consumer is not
  delivered.
- The read wiring keeps the one-store shape (`$state`, effector.ts:587-676): view A must
  follow a switch to any group, and a `combine` cannot change its inputs. There every
  point write copies the population Map and recomputes both views; the only timed writes
  are `filterTwoAxes`' four moves.
- Effector skips an update whose new state is `===` the old one (the store graphite
  node compares `e!==r`, node_modules/effector/effector.mjs line 1, minified). A pure
  reducer therefore has to allocate a new Map for every point write. That is the
  documented immutable-update contract applied to a Map, not extra work invented by the
  adapter.

## Where the granularity is finer

The churn wiring subscribes only after `holdChurnRows`, so it holds one store per
row (effector.ts:381-387), and a point write copies only that row (:445-464). The
relation wiring gives each owner its own store (:920-930). Both shapes are Effector's
own. Every churn mount records its subscriber's current read at mount time
(:509, :514, :522, :532, :543) and every wake overwrites it (:399-402), which is what
the verify-pass churn read fold checks.

## Teardown

`pin` and `dispose` call `clearNode` on every derived store, the cell `.map`s and
`combine`s included (effector.ts:301-306, :345-362). The group stores are roots and are
left to the collector, as the relation wiring leaves its owner stores (:1012-1015). That
is why this row does not carry the stale-derivation exposure nanostores carries.

## Unverified

Nothing here was run. The partition's, the frame event's and the per-cell `.map`'s
effects on any row are unmeasured. The diamond's single run per write is not traced in
the kernel. The cell `combine`'s callback relies on the tuple quirk the churn and
relation wirings already rely on (effector.ts:404-420, :948-956), and `.slice()`s the
array it is handed so the result is a fresh array whatever the kernel passes.

bind.note: One `map` store per group (nanostores.ts:51, :55-62) and an id → group-store handle table (:53). One `computed` + `.subscribe` per view over its own group's store (:115-122). Point writes use the documented `setKey` (:134-140), which itself spreads the store's record (node_modules/nanostores/map/index.js:14-19) — one group's, not the population's. Batched writes publish one whole-record `set` per touched store (`write` :162-179, `remove` :180-189); a move is two store writes (:194-209). The cell wiring built by `pin` (:227-249) is a `computed` per pinned cell and column over that row's group store, returning one string, and a `computed` per column over its cells (`pinnedTextOf`, :142-156): a label write leaves every note cell's string unchanged, the atom's `set` drops it (`Object.is`, atom/index.js), and the note consumer is not delivered. `frame` is `batch(run)` (:38-40; `batch` exported at index.js:1, defined at atom/index.js:43-57, documented at atom/index.d.ts:196-224). Inside it each view's `.subscribe` listener is queued once per batch and called once when the outermost batch returns, with the computed's value at that moment (atom/index.js:15-41, :96-119). `batch` coalesces notifications only: each `setKey` inside a frame still spreads its group's record (map/index.js:14-19).

bindPerGroup.note: Same body with fifty computeds, each over its own group's store (nanostores.ts:880), so a write in one group recomputes one view. Same `batch` `frame` as `bind`: a frame recomputes and delivers each touched group's view once.

churn.row.note: One `map` store per row (nanostores.ts:297), `listen` on it (:350), with the store's current label recorded as the slot's read at mount (:351). `listen` does not call the listener on subscribe (atom/index.js), so a mount is not also a wake. Each wake writes `churnRead[at]` (:287-290) and `unmount` clears it (:396-402), which is what the verify-pass fold over every standing read (render.ts:124-141) checks. The multi-row frames that reach this wiring — `churnList` (`writeFrame`, scenarios.ts:1881-1891), `appFill` (:2917-2922) and `appRound` (:2983-2993) — write each row once per frame, and every subscriber is its own listener closure (:287, :350), so under `batch` every subscriber on a written row still runs exactly once, at the end of the frame rather than inline; the woke counts the scripts expect (`churnListPrefix`, `APP_FILL_WOKE`, `appRoundWoke`) count subscribers on written rows and are unchanged by the switch.

churn.wide.note: `computed` over the source row stores, then `listen` (nanostores.ts:354-363). Unmount splices the listener, but the computed stays attached to its sources until `STORE_UNMOUNT_DELAY` (lifecycle/index.js:117, :136-145), which no sample reaches; a KNOWN EFFECT on this row, shared with `churn.chain` and `churn.diamond`, with no public workaround, and the `departure` says its direction is unmeasured (src/adapters/nanostores.md, 'A computed with no listener stays attached for a second'). `churnWide` writes one row per frame (`rowsWrittenIn: churnRowOnly`, scenarios.ts:2152), and `writeFrame` with a count of one calls `patchLabel` without opening a `frame` at all (scenarios.ts:1883-1886), so the switch to `batch` does not touch this wiring's script.

churn.column.note: `listenKeys(store, ['label'])` (nanostores.ts:365-370), the library's own key filter (listen-keys/index.js:3-29). The writes use `setKey('label', …)` (:306), which passes the key name the filter reads; `setKey` itself skips a value `Object.is`-equal to the held one (map/index.js:14). Inside a `batch` the `changed` key is `undefined` (atom/index.js:112, atom/index.d.ts:207-208) and `listenKeys` falls back to comparing the key's pre-batch and final values (listen-keys/index.js:9-16), which still filters by key; no script reaches this wiring inside a frame, because `churnColumn` writes one row (scenarios.ts:2255) and `writeFrame` opens no frame for one.

churn.chain.note: Level 1 is a `computed` over the `count` source stores returning `chainLevelOf(label of row from, 1)`; levels 2..depth are each a `computed` over the level below returning `chainLevelOf(text, level)`; `listen` on the head (nanostores.ts:371-386). It carries the same deferred-unmount exposure as `churn.wide`.

churn.diamond.note: Two `computed`s over root row `from`'s store (`diamondLeftOf`, `diamondRightOf` of its label), a third `computed([left, right], diamondJoinOf)`, and `listen` on the join (nanostores.ts:387-395). Read in node_modules/nanostores 1.5.5: a root write queues left's and right's recompute on the one listener queue before either runs (atom/index.js:96-119, the queue drains only when `runListenerQueue` was set by the outermost notify); each then queues the join, the first join run recomputes it and stamps `currentEpoch` (computed/index.js:32), and the second returns at `currentEpoch === epoch` (computed/index.js:12-13), so the listener fires once per write. Inside a `batch` the join's two queue entries share one listener (computed/index.js:62 registers the same `run` on both sources), and `drainQueue` skips the second because the first call cleared its pending set (atom/index.js:21-28), so the result is the same. Not run; `churnDiamond` writes one row per frame (scenarios.ts:2590) and its check is what asserts the count. Same deferred-unmount exposure as `churn.wide`.

reads.byKey.note: One `$rows.get()` per page and one property read per key, nothing hoisted (nanostores.ts:554-563).

reads.byWindow.note: View A's cursor is one atom holding group and offset (nanostores.ts:423). View A is `computed([$rows, $cursor])` (:470-479) and view B is `computed($rows)` (:480-482), so a scroll recomputes A only (:566-568). A scroll sets a fresh `{ group, offset }` object rather than a number. Both views are over one group, so this wiring keeps the population in one store (:421) beside a Set-per-group id index (:422). A point write spreads the 10 000-key record (`setKey`, :523-546); the only timed writes in this wiring are `filterTwoAxes`' four moves, and a partition was considered and not made (src/adapters/nanostores.md, 'What a computed can depend on').

reads.byTwoAxes.note: View B is `computed($rows)` with the second predicate (nanostores.ts:480-482, predicate at :448).

reads.bySwitch.note: `switchGroup` sets the cursor atom to `{ group, offset: 0 }` (nanostores.ts:569-571): one atom write, one notification, one recompute of view A over the new group's ids. src/adapters/nanostores.md gives the reason for one atom as `switchGroup` not being called inside a frame. Against 1.5.5 two atoms written inside `batch` would also reach view A's computed once (one `run` listener on both sources, computed/index.js:62); the one-atom shape needs no batch and costs nothing. View B does not name the atom.

relations.note: One `map` store per row, owner and pair (nanostores.ts:599-601). The views are computeds over the touched owner stores and over the pair stores (:673-692), so the two views have disjoint dependencies. `writePair` composes the key and looks up the store on every call (:713-717).

single.note: `atom('')` and `listen` (nanostores.ts:757-815). `atom.set` skips a value equal under the atom's `eq`, which is `Object.is` (atom/index.js:67, :123-129).

card.summary: The window wiring holds one `map` store per group with a computed per view over its own group's store, so a point write spreads one group's record and wakes only that group's view. `frame` is nanostores' own synchronous `batch(run)`, which queues every listener and drains once when the outermost batch returns, so a multi-write frame reaches each listener once, with final values. The cell wiring is a `computed` per pinned cell and column, so the atom's own `Object.is` keeps a label write away from the note consumer. The chain and diamond are nanostores' own `computed`. A computed that loses its last listener is detached only on a 1000 ms timer (`STORE_UNMOUNT_DELAY`) the worker never reaches, so after an unmount on the churn rows, and after `pin` for the two window computeds, the edges stay and keep recomputing; that is a library limit with no public workaround, stated as a known effect and not worked around.
card.body:
## Version and recipe

`node_modules/nanostores/package.json` is `1.5.5`, the same as `version`
(nanostores.ts:819). The `departure` (nanostores.ts:821-847) and src/adapters/nanostores.md
describe the 1.5.5 `batch`; the recipe comment at nanostores.ts:44 says "nanostores 1.5".
The adapter uses `map` for records, `computed` for derived state, `subscribe` /
`listen` for consumers, `setKey` for one key and `batch` for a frame. All five are
exported and typed in node_modules/nanostores/index.d.ts. The installed README only
links out to the docs (README.md:64-65), so this audit could not check the online README
the `docs` field cites. The recipe is checked against the shipped code, not the prose.

## Batching

nanostores 1.5.5 exports a synchronous `batch(fn)` (node_modules/nanostores/index.js:1,
atom/index.js:43-57), and the adapter's `frame(run)` is `batch(run)`
(nanostores.ts:38-40). Every wiring writes through it; no buffering is needed, because the
library's own batch already delivers each listener once per frame. What a listener sees, read from atom/index.js:

- While a batch is open, `notify` (:96-119) records each (listener, store) pair once in
  `batchSeen` and pushes at most one queue entry per pair; a second write to the same
  store inside the batch queues nothing more for that listener (:105). The entry carries
  the store's value from before its first change in the batch as `oldValue`, and
  `undefined` as the changed key (:112).
- The outermost `batch` drains the queue when `fn` returns (:49-51); a nested `batch`
  drains nothing (:44).
- `drainQueue` (:15-41) calls the listener with the store's value read at drain time
  (:31), so the listener sees final values. For a listener queued under several stores,
  the first entry clears its pending set and calls it, and later entries for stores that
  call already covered are skipped (:21-28).
- `batchSeen` stays set until the drain finishes (:53), so a computed recomputed during
  the drain queues its own listeners through the same path, and they too run once. A
  store that changes after its listener has already run in the drain queues that
  listener again (comment at :25-26) — so "once per batch" holds per listener unless one
  of its stores changes again after it ran within the same drain. No wiring here has a
  listener whose source changes twice in one drain: every computed is a single `set` in
  its `run`, and the epoch guard (computed/index.js:12-13) collapses a re-entry.

The typings state the same contract: "each listener fires at most once when the
outermost `batch` returns — with the final store values" (atom/index.d.ts:197-199).
`batched(stores, fn)` is a different thing, a computed whose recompute is scheduled with
`setTimeout` (computed/index.js:54-58).

**Verification, 2026-10-17.** The previous version of this card marked `bind`,
`bindPerGroup` and `churn.wide` `improvable` and the participant `improvable`, because
`frame` called `run()` directly on the 0.11 premise that no synchronous batch exists, and
listed switching `frame` to `batch(run)` as its one improvement. That switch has been
applied (nanostores.ts:1, :38-40), the improvement is closed, and the three wirings and
the overall verdict are re-judged `idiomatic`. Nothing faster documented by the library
remains unapplied in this adapter.

What the switch changes, by script, read from src/harness/scenarios.ts and not run:

- Under `bind` / `bindPerGroup`: `batchPatch` (:657-661), `batchPatchNote` (:753-757),
  `patchMostRows` (:845), `mixedFrame` (:934), `moveAndReorder` (:1046-1049) and
  `resortWindow` (:1181-1185) go from one view delivery per write that reaches a watched
  group's store to one delivery per touched view per frame. In `moveAndReorder` view B
  was delivered twice per step (the `setKey` of the move and the `setKey` of the rank);
  it is now delivered once. Every one of these checks either is `finalStateOnly`
  (:637, :817, :909, :1029, :1152) and asks for row counts, order or `atLeast` one new
  state per step, or (`batchPatchNote`, :760-762) asks for zero distinct renders, so none
  of them requires per-write delivery. That the checks pass under `batch` is not
  established by a run.
- Under `churn.row`: `churnList`, `appFill` and `appRound` write each row once per frame,
  so the same subscribers run the same number of times; only when they run moves, from
  inline to the end of the frame. `settle` (nanostores.ts:317-327) runs after `frame`
  returns, so the comment above it, "nanostores drains its notification queue inline",
  still holds at the moment `settle` reads `churnWoke`.
- Under `churn.wide`, `churn.column`, `churn.chain` and `churn.diamond`: no change. Their
  scripts write one row per frame and `writeFrame` opens no frame for one
  (scenarios.ts:1883-1886).
- The read, relation and single wirings: no script calls `frame` on them (every
  `binding.frame` call in scenarios.ts is one of the eight above).

## The window wiring's store per group

- `computed(stores, cb)` takes its dependency list once, at construction
  (computed/index.js:6-7, :61-67), and `bind` binds an empty store, so a view cannot be
  built over per-row stores that do not exist yet. What is known at bind is the watched
  groups (`TViewConfig`). The window wiring therefore holds one `map` store per group,
  created on first ask (nanostores.ts:55-62) — at bind for the watched ones — and each
  view's computed depends on its own group's store (:115-122).
- `setKey` creates `{ ...$map.value, [key]: value }` (map/index.js:14-19) unless the new
  value is `Object.is`-equal to the held one. A point write spreads one group's record,
  about 200 keys, and it reaches only the view over that group; under `bindPerGroup` one
  write recomputes one view of fifty. The adapter adds a second spread, of the row
  (`{ ...held, ...change }`, nanostores.ts:139), which also means the key's value is
  always a new object, so `setKey`'s equality skip never fires here. Inside a `batch` the
  spreads still happen once per `setKey`; only the notifications coalesce.
- A move takes the row out of the old group's store with one whole-record `set` and
  puts it into the new one with `setKey` (nanostores.ts:194-209): two store writes, one
  notification per view, and inside a frame one delivery per view. A re-send through
  `write` still publishes a fresh record per touched store, so it notifies, as a `map`
  store handed a new object does.
- `readAll` reads every group store's record (:211-218); `groupOrder` reads the group's
  own store (:220-224).
- `pin` (:227-249) resolves each pinned row's group store once, untimed, and builds a
  `computed` per pinned cell and column over that store returning one string, and a
  `computed` per column over its cells (`pinnedTextOf`, :142-156). A label write
  recomputes the cells over the written group's store; the note cells return the same
  string, `atom.set` drops it under `Object.is`, the note column's sources are unchanged,
  and the note consumer is not delivered. A pinned write still looks its key up through
  the id → store table, so `patchPinnedLabel` costs what `patchLabel` costs.

## The derivation shapes

The chain and diamond are built from `computed` alone; nothing between levels is the
adapter's beyond the `derivations.ts` function each level is defined by. A 1.5.5
computed also skips its callback when every source value is `eq` to the previous one
(computed/index.js:15). Their computeds are subject to the deferred detach described
below, so an unmount leaves their edges standing for the rest of the sample. Every churn
mount records the subscriber's current read (:351, :363, :369, :385, :394) and `unmount`
clears it (:401), which the verify-pass churn read fold relies on.

## The computeds that never detach — a known effect on churn rows and on the pin

This is stated, not worked around. On the churn rows it applies to every
`mountOnRows` over more than one row, every chain and every diamond: an unmount
splices the listener and leaves the computed's source edges standing, so later writes
in the sample recompute a computed nobody reads. `pin` unsubscribes the window
computeds (nanostores.ts:228). A computed's sources are
detached only in a `setTimeout(…, STORE_UNMOUNT_DELAY)` callback
(lifecycle/index.js:117, :136-145). The worker runs synchronously, so the two window
computeds keep recomputing on every `cellDelivery` write to their own groups' stores
and nothing reads the result. The synchronous escape, `cleanStores`, throws when
`NODE_ENV === 'production'` (clean-stores/index.js:5-10) and the per-store `clean`
hooks it calls are only installed outside production (atom/index.js:138,
lifecycle/index.js:147); workers run as production (src/harness/measureBatch.ts:201).
This is a library limit with no public workaround. It counts against nanostores on
`cellDelivery` and on the churn rows named above; which way it moves them is unmeasured.

## Unverified

The `departure` says per-key `setKey` writes in `write` "would make one call to write
into ten thousand record copies, batched or not". The copy per `setKey` follows from
map/index.js:14-19 and is independent of `batch`; the figure of ten thousand was not
traced to the operating point, and nothing was measured. The per-cell computeds' effect on
cellDelivery is unmeasured. The per-group partition's effect on patchColumn, patchNote,
batchPatch, patchMostRows, cellDelivery and moveGroup is unmeasured, and so is the cost
of the cursor object a scroll allocates. The effect of the switch to `batch` on the timed
rows listed under Batching is unmeasured, and that each of those scripts' checks passes
under it was established by reading the checks, not by a run.

bind.note: One `store.subscribe` (redux-toolkit.ts:274-283) over one memoised selector per view (:260-271), each declared with `SHALLOW_RESULT` (:211), i.e. `memoizeOptions: { resultEqualityCheck: shallowEqual }` with react-redux's `shallowEqual`. A recomputed window holding the same row objects returns the previous array (reselect.mjs:151-156), so the reference bail-out — `useSelector`'s default (`refEquality`, react-redux.mjs:958-962) — skips it. Row writes go through `rowEditorOf` (:178-204): one `edited` action per write outside a frame, one per frame inside it.

bindPerGroup.note: Same body with fifty views (redux-toolkit.ts:838). Every notification calls all fifty selectors, and any write to `entities` makes all fifty recompute; only views whose window's row objects changed get a new reference and are delivered.

churn.row.note: One `store.subscribe` per subscriber over `entities[id]`. A wake is counted only when the selected reference changed (redux-toolkit.ts:359-373), which is `useSelector`'s default semantics. Every subscriber body still runs on every notification, so the time carries Redux's global notification (redux-toolkit.md, 'What the counter on a subscription-churn row counts'). The read is recorded at mount (:365) and on every wake (:371), and `unmount` clears it (:459-465). The store is the rows slice without the group index (:112-121).

churn.wide.note: Same subscriber, selecting a string composed from `count` rows (redux-toolkit.ts:378-387, :423-431).
