churn.column.note: `mountOnColumn` (redux-toolkit.ts:432-435) is `useSelector(state => entities[id].label)`: the same subscriber as `churn.row`, selecting the label string and comparing it by `===`. Redux keeps no column identity; the column is the selector, which is how a react-redux user subscribes to one field.

churn.chain.note: Level 1 is a `createSelector` over `entities` returning `chainLevelOf(label of row from, 1)`; levels 2..depth are each a `createSelector` over the level below (redux-toolkit.ts:436-446); the subscriber selects the head. reselect's `identityFunctionCheck` only runs outside production (reselect.mjs:183-200, :336-353). Same subscriber as `churn.row`.

churn.diamond.note: An input selector for root row `from`'s label, two `createSelector`s over it and a third over both, the subscriber on the join (redux-toolkit.ts:447-458). Reselect memoises each result function on its inputs, so an unchanged label re-runs neither branch nor the join.

reads.byKey.note: One `getState()` per page and one `entities[id]` per key, no dispatch (redux-toolkit.ts:552-561).

reads.byWindow.note: View A's cursor is a second slice (redux-toolkit.ts:477-489). The listener (:529-543) is two `useSelector`s for view A — the page rows (`selectPageRows`, :508-516, shallow result check) and `view.offset` — and one for view B (`selectOnAxis`, :517-521). On a scroll (:564) view B's inputs are unchanged and it is not delivered.

reads.byTwoAxes.note: View B is a `createSelector` over `entities` and group A's ids with the second predicate (redux-toolkit.ts:517-521, predicate at :226), with the shallow result check, so a write that leaves B's rows the same objects does not deliver B.

reads.bySwitch.note: `switchGroup` dispatches `view/switched` (redux-toolkit.ts:565), whose reducer sets `group` and resets `offset` in one draft (:484-487). The slice is pointed at group A by that action once, before any subscriber exists (:505).

relations.note: Three slices in one store (redux-toolkit.ts:632-639), so an owner write leaves `state.pairs` unchanged and the pair selector hits its cache; both selectors carry the shallow result check (:657-666). `renderBoth` (:670-682) delivers a view only when its selector's reference changed.

single.note: Two `store.subscribe` listeners (redux-toolkit.ts:750-765), each selecting one string and rendering only when it is not `===` the last, `useSelector`'s default. No script writes a single inside a frame, so `frame` runs its function (:772).

card.summary: A normalised RTK slice with `createSelector` views, every array selector carrying reselect's `resultEqualityCheck: shallowEqual` and every subscriber applying react-redux `useSelector`'s default reference bail-out; a frame's row writes are buffered and dispatched as ONE `edited` action; the chain and diamond are memoised reselect selectors, a view switch is an action into the `view` slice; `churn.column` selects the label string and compares it by `===`.
card.body:
## Version and recipe

`node_modules/@reduxjs/toolkit/package.json` is `2.13.0`, the same as `version`
(redux-toolkit.ts:793). Installed beside it: `redux` 5.0.1, `immer` 11.1.21,
`reselect` 5.3.0, `react-redux` 9.2.0 (each `node_modules/<name>/package.json`; RTK
declares `immer ^11.0.0` and `reselect ^5.1.0`). The adapter imports `createSelector`
from `reselect` directly (redux-toolkit.ts:4) and `shallowEqual` from `react-redux`
(:3). `react-redux` is not declared in `packages/bench/package.json`; it resolves
because `packages/redux-adapter` declares it and npm hoists it, and importing it loads
React's module (react-redux.mjs:2) without rendering anything. The
recipe follows the `docs` page on deriving data with selectors: a slice with `entities`
and an id index, `createSelector` per view, `store.subscribe` as the change signal.

## What is idiomatic

- Reducers mutate the Immer draft (`applyEdit`, redux-toolkit.ts:71-110). The upsert
  in a `write` edit assigns the four columns onto the stored draft row. Immer's set
  trap returns without marking the draft changed when the value `is` the current one,
  so a re-send produces the same root. That line reference was last read on
  2026-10-17 and not re-read for this edit.
- A one-column write is a `patch` edit carrying `{ id, <column> }`, applied with
  `Object.assign(stored, patch)` onto the draft (:105), the update shape the Redux
  normalisation guide teaches; `setGroup` is the same edit with `group`, and the group
  array moves only when the group value differs.
- Every row write is the one `edited` reducer (:112-122 and :159-171) over a list of
  edits. Outside a frame a write is one action with one edit; inside `frame` the edits
  are buffered and dispatched as one action when the frame returns (`rowEditorOf`,
  :178-204) — the style guide's "Avoid Dispatching Many Actions Sequentially". The
  buffer compares nothing; an empty frame dispatches nothing.
- A group array is rebuilt once per action (`regroupingOf`, :126-157): leaves and joins
  are recorded per group, and `commit` filters the array read through `original()` —
  Immer's "for expensive search operations, read from the original state" tip — once
  per touched group, where the earlier code ran `indexOf` + `splice` on the draft per id.
- No `createEntityAdapter`. Its update path builds `Object.assign({}, original,
  changes)` for every row (`takeNewKey`,
  node_modules/@reduxjs/toolkit/dist/redux-toolkit.modern.mjs:1168-1180), which would
  defeat the Immer no-op. The hand-written reducer is the faster of two documented
  ways, and it is the same kind of draft mutation the RTK docs teach. The `departure`
  declares it.
- `immutableCheck` and `serializableCheck` are turned off. RTK only adds them when
  `NODE_ENV !== 'production'` (redux-toolkit.modern.mjs:334-345), and workers run as
  production (src/harness/measureBatch.ts:201), so turning them off changes nothing at
  run time. Both line references are from the 2026-10-17 audit and were not re-read.
  Immer's auto-freeze stays on: it is Immer's default in production as well.
- The pin hoists nothing, because a write is an action carrying an id. That is the
  accurate answer for this library.
- Two row slices, not one. `groupedRowsSlice` (:159-171) keeps `idsByGroup` beside
  `entities` and serves the window and read wirings, whose views walk a group.
  `rowsSlice` (:112-122) is `entities` alone and serves the churn and relation wirings,
  where no view is derived and `groupOrder` answers `undefined`: maintaining a key index
  nothing reads would be work this task does not ask for.

## The derivation shapes

The chain and the diamond are reselect's `createSelector`, the memoised selector the
`docs` page recommends; nothing between levels is the adapter's beyond the
`derivations.ts` function each level is defined by. The subscriber's `===` on the head
string is the same `useSelector` bail-out every subscriber here applies.

## The bail-out

Every subscriber keeps what its selector returned last and delivers only on a
different reference: the window views (redux-toolkit.ts:274-283), the read views
(:529-543), the relation views (:670-682) and the single listeners (:750-765), the
same check the churn wiring makes (:366-373). That is react-redux `useSelector`'s
default equality (react-redux.mjs:958-962). Every selector returning an array is
declared with `SHALLOW_RESULT` (:211), reselect 5's `resultEqualityCheck` set to
react-redux's `shallowEqual` (react-redux.mjs:454-468): when a recomputed array holds
the same elements as the last one, reselect returns the last one
(reselect.mjs:151-156), so a write elsewhere in `entities` no longer delivers a view
whose rows did not change. The cell wiring (`pin`, :300-329) keeps each cell's last
string and delivers a column's consumer only when one of its cells is not `===` its
last — one `useSelector` per cell, written as one listener.

## Batching

Redux's `dispatch` notifies every listener before it returns, and the Redux style
guide's "Avoid Dispatching Many Actions Sequentially" says to dispatch one event that
makes all the updates instead. `frame` does that for row writes: it buffers the edits
and dispatches one `edited` action as it returns (`rowEditorOf`, redux-toolkit.ts:178-204),
so the listeners run once per frame. A nested frame joins the outer buffer. Cursor,
owner, pair and single writes are their own actions and are not buffered; no script
issues one inside a frame. `configureStore`'s default enhancers include
`autoBatchEnhancer` (redux-toolkit.modern.mjs:424-429), but it defers only actions whose
`meta` carries `SHOULD_AUTOBATCH` (:405-417), and no action here does, so every
dispatch notifies before it returns.

## Code volume

The figures are `npm run lines`' cell for each wiring; they have not been re-run since
this edit. What each wiring holds beyond the median, and why the library needs it:

- **Every wiring pays for the store recipe.** The edit model shared by every row store
  (`applyEdit`, the `edited` reducers and `rowEditorOf`, redux-toolkit.ts:57-204), and
  `configureStore` with the production middleware options (:206-209). Redux has no
  batch of its own, so the buffered single action is how a frame notifies once.
- **churn.row**: the rows slice and the editor above, plus the per-subscriber
  `store.subscribe` with its own last-value comparison (:366-373). Redux's listener
  receives no change information, so the selected-value compare is the only edge a
  subscriber has.
- **relations**: three slices — rows, owners (:590-606), pairs (:610-627) — because a
  reference-identical branch is what lets the untouched view's memo hold; and two
  `createSelector`s plus the bail-out in `holdRelation` (:654-684).
- **single**: a slice of two values with a seed reducer and a write reducer, the store,
  two `store.subscribe` listeners each comparing its value (:716-789).
- **reads.byKey**: the binding is the same for every read shape, so it carries both
  views: the grouped slice with its regrouping (:126-171), the `view` slice (:477-489),
  the two memoised selectors and the bail-out subscriber (:508-543), and the shared
  top-k selection (:219-238).
- **bind**: the grouped slice with its regrouping (:126-171), the selection (:219-238),
  one memoised selector per view and the one global subscriber (:260-283), and the cell
  wiring's listener (:300-329).

## Unverified

Nothing in this card was re-run after the 2026-10-20 edit: no verify pass, no lines
cell, no `digest` (the value above is the 2026-10-17 one and is now stale). The claim
that `useSelector` is how an ordinary user consumes this store comes from react-redux
being the documented React binding; this bench drives no React. In the single wiring,
the cells, `churn.column` and the churn chain and diamond the selected value is a
string, so `===` there is a value comparison; it is applied because it is
`useSelector`'s default — the same rule now applied to `churn.column`, which this card
previously declined under B3 for exactly that comparison. `react-redux` is reached as an
undeclared, hoisted dependency.

bind.note: `computed` over one bucket signal and the `group`/`rank` signals of its records, ending in an `effect` that reads the selected records' `label` (preact-signals.ts:158-165). `write` and `remove` touch only the row signals and the touched buckets (:178-238). `readAll` reads every field signal's `.value` through `byId`, outside any effect and so untracked (:308). `frame` is `batch` (:126-128, wired at :304), and the same `frame` is carried by the churn (:410), read (:632), relation (:749) and single (:921) bindings.

bindPerGroup.note: Same body with fifty views (preact-signals.ts:975); disjoint dependency sets, routed by preact.

churn.row.note: An `effect` reading all four field signals of row `from` and rendering its label (`labelOfWholeRow`, preact-signals.ts:367-372; mount :436-440), so it is a subscription to the WHOLE row, as types.ts:55-60 and SCENARIOS.md define the shape; `churn.column` is the label-only contrast. The first run is the mount and is not counted (:354-365; preact-signals.md, 'Why an effect's first run is not a wake-up'). Every run, the first included, records the read in `churnRead[at]` (:358) and `unmount` clears it (:474-480).

churn.wide.note: One `effect` reading every field signal of `count` rows, ending on row `from` (preact-signals.ts:441-447).

churn.column.note: `computed(() => churnSignals[0].label.value)` under the `effect` (preact-signals.ts:449-452). A `note` write touches a signal the computed never read.

churn.chain.note: Level 1 is a `computed` over the `count` sources returning `chainLevelOf(their labels joined, 1)`; levels 2..depth are each a `computed` returning `chainLevelOf(level below, level)`; the effect reads the head (preact-signals.ts:453-466). `depth` computeds in all.

churn.diamond.note: Two `computed`s over root row `from`'s `label` signal (`diamondLeftOf`, `diamondRightOf`) and a third `computed` over both (`diamondJoinOf`), with the effect on the join (preact-signals.ts:467-473). That the join runs once per frame is left to preact's own graph; the adapter adds no guard, and the diamond script's check is what asserts it.

reads.byKey.note: One `byId.get` and the `.value` reads of `shownOf` per key, outside any effect, nothing hoisted (preact-signals.ts:635-645).

reads.byWindow.note: `$offset` (preact-signals.ts:505) is read only by `$paged`, which slices `$sorted` (:518-533), so a scroll re-runs the slice and never the sort. `scrollTo` is one setter call (:647-649). A scroll does not touch view B (:534-536).

reads.byTwoAxes.note: View B is a computed over the same bucket with the second predicate (preact-signals.ts:534-536, predicate at :112).

reads.bySwitch.note: View A's group is a `signal` (`$group`, preact-signals.ts:506) read by `$sorted` (:518-529). `switchGroup` writes `$group` and resets `$offset` to 0 inside one `batch` (:650-655), so the effect re-runs once, over the new group's bucket. View B reads neither signal.

relations.note: Owner and pair records each get their own signal. View A's effect reads owner signals and view B's reads pair signals (preact-signals.ts:796-811), so the two views have disjoint dependencies. `writePair` composes the key on every call (:821-825). The owner and pair `$...Population` signals (:689, :694) are written only in the untimed `writeOwners` and `holdRelation`.

single.note: Bare `signal.value = v` with no `batch` (preact-signals.ts:916-918). The setter opens and closes its own batch (node_modules/@preact/signals-core/src/index.ts:461-487).

card.summary: A row is a signal per mutable field, a bucket signal per group replaced copy-on-write, and a computed plus effect per view, routed by preact's own graph; every script frame and every multi-signal write runs inside preact's `batch`, single-signal writes go through the self-batching setter, a row subscription reads every field signal of its row, the cell wiring reads one field signal per pinned cell, and the chain, diamond and view switch are preact's own `computed` and `signal`.

## Version and recipe

`node_modules/@preact/signals-core/package.json` is `1.14.4`, the same as `version`
(preact-signals.ts:942). The recipe is the signals-core README's: `signal`, `computed`,
`effect`, `batch`. Each view ends in an `effect`, because a computed is pull-based
(preact-signals.md, 'How consumption is forced').

## What preact routes, and what the adapter adds

- The id map and the group map hold signal handles (preact-signals.ts:136, :140). Each
  view's computed reads one bucket signal and that bucket's records' `group` and
  `rank` signals (:158-161). A write to a row of group Z therefore reaches only the
  view over Z. A move writes three signals in one batch (:250-261): the row's `group`,
  the old bucket and the new bucket.
- Buckets are copy-on-write: preact has no way to announce a mutated value, so a move
  allocates two bucket arrays (:257, :259) and `write` drafts each touched bucket once
  per batch (:182-191), which avoids a quadratic load. This is where the row differs
  from alien's, which mutates in place and calls `trigger`.
- `readAll` iterates `byId.values()` and reads each field's `.value` through `rowOf`
  outside every effect (:308, :423, :657, :827); no `peek()` is used anywhere.

## Batching

`frame(run)` is `batch(run)` (preact-signals.ts:126-128; node_modules/@preact/signals-core/src/index.ts:95-106).
Every binding, the single one included, carries it, so a script's several writes before
one `settle()` reach preact as one batch and effects run once when it returns. The
batches inside `write`, `remove`, `setGroup` and `switchGroup` nest: `batch` at
depth > 0 only calls the function (src/index.ts:96-98).

Methods that write one signal (`patchLabel`, `patchNote`, `setRank`, the pinned
patches, `scrollTo`, `patchOwnerName`, `writePair`, the churn and relation field
patches) call the setter bare. The setter batches its own notification
(src/index.ts:461-487). `settle` is a no-op in the view, read and relation bindings
because effects have already run when the outermost batch returns; in the churn and
single bindings it only turns what the effects recorded into one delivery
(:412-422, :923-932).

## The derivation shapes

The chain and the diamond are built only from preact's `computed`; the adapter computes
nothing between levels beyond the `derivations.ts` function each level is defined by.
Whether the diamond's join runs once per frame is preact's own glitch-freedom, not
traced in its source by this audit; the diamond script's check is what asserts it.

## The cell wiring

`pin` resolves the pinned row records untimed (preact-signals.ts:269-297), and each
cell effect reads that column's field signal (`label` or `note`) of every pinned row
directly. A `note` write touches a signal the label effect never read, so it does
not re-run.

## What is idiomatic

No value guard sits in a patch method (`TBinding.write`). What compares is preact's
own `!==` on each field signal (src/index.ts:462).

## What was not traced

Nothing was compiled or run; line numbers were re-read against the current file on
2026-10-20. The card needs a second reader before it is stamped.

`node_modules/alien-signals/package.json` is `3.2.1`, the same as `version`

esm/index.mjs:67-74; the `departure` says the pair was read from the declarations
(alien-signals.ts:901-907). Without it, every signal write flushes the effect queue
(esm/index.mjs:301-311, `if (!batchDepth) flush()`), and the load would deliver once per row.

`frame(run)` is `inBatch` (alien-signals.ts:137-144): `startBatch()`, `run()`, `endBatch()`
in a try/finally. Every binding, the single one included, carries it, so a script's several
writes before one `settle()` flush once at the outermost `endBatch`. The batches inside
`write`, `remove`, `setGroup` and `switchGroup` nest by depth counter (esm/index.mjs:67-74).

`scrollTo`, `patchOwnerName`, `writePair`, the churn and relation field patches) call the
setter bare: an unbatched write flushes exactly once anyway (esm/index.mjs:301-311). The
churn and relation `remove` write no signal and are a map delete (:425-427, :689-691).
`settle` is a no-op in the view, read and relation bindings; in the churn and single
bindings it only turns what the effects recorded into one delivery (:447-457, :880-890).

## What alien routes, and what the adapter adds

- The id map and group map hold signal handles (alien-signals.ts:238, :242). Each view's
  computed reads one bucket and that bucket's records' `group` and `rank` (:259-262), so
  a write reaches only the view over the written row's group.
- A bucket is mutated in place and announced with `trigger(() => { bucket(); … })`
  (alien-signals.ts:146-150; README.md "Manual Triggering", esm/index.mjs:154-180). A move
  splices one handle out and pushes it onto the destination (:213-229); a load pushes onto
  each touched bucket (:152-183); a removal compacts each touched bucket once (:185-211).
  The preact row cannot do this — it has no trigger — and allocates two bucket arrays per
  move, so the two rows differ by this as well as by the reactivity.
- Write-path reads are untracked, because alien links a dependency only when `activeSub`
  is set (esm/index.mjs:323-326), and the harness calls write methods outside every
  effect.
- `readAll` iterates `byId.values()` and calls each field signal (:348, :458, :621, :788).

## The derivation shapes

The chain and the diamond are built only from alien's `computed`; nothing between levels
is the adapter's beyond the `derivations.ts` function each level is defined by. The
diamond's glitch-freedom was not traced in esm/index.mjs by this audit.

## The cell wiring

`pin` resolves the pinned row records untimed (alien-signals.ts:308-336), and each cell
effect reads that column's field signal (`label` or `note`) of every pinned row directly.
A `note` write touches a signal the label effect never read, so it does not re-run.

## What was not traced

Nothing was compiled or run; line numbers were re-read against the current file on
2026-10-20. The card needs a second reader before it is stamped.

bind.note: One store (zustand.ts:203-205) and one `subscribeWithSelector` listener per view selecting that group's top-k window through `selectionOf`, compared with `shallow` (:208-220), the comparison `useShallow` applies (node_modules/zustand/esm/react/shallow.mjs:4-10). Writes are immutable `setState` updaters built from a list of edits (`entitiesEdited`, `rowsEdited`, :83-132). `frame` (`rowEditorOf`, :139-165) buffers the row writes issued inside it and applies them as one `setState` when it returns; outside a frame each write is its own `setState`. A write to group B re-runs view A's selector and the `shallow` comparison leaves it undelivered. The cell wiring (`pin`, :235-253) is two listeners selecting the pinned `label` and `note` strings with `shallow` and `fireImmediately`, so a label write delivers the label consumer only.

churn.row.note: One `subscribeWithSelector` listener per subscriber selecting `entities[id]` with the default `Object.is` (zustand.ts:277-291, :324-329; equality at esm/middleware.mjs:254-258). The mount subscribes with `fireImmediately`, so the selector runs once per mount and that first call records the read; the middleware passes the same slice as next and previous there (esm/middleware.mjs:263-265), which is how the listener tells it from a wake (:285-288). `unmount` deletes the listener and clears the read slot (:344-350). Every `setState` runs every standing subscriber's selector, so the time carries zustand's global notification. The store holds `entities` alone (`onlyEntitiesEdited`, :134-137): no churn script reads a grouping.

churn.wide.note: The subscriber selects the tuple of its `count` rows and compares it with `shallow` (zustand.ts:330-336), the documented multi-value selection (README.md:216-221); the rendered text is the first row's label (:296-303). Because the tuple holds the row objects, a write to any of the `count` rows wakes the subscriber, not only a write to the first; churnWide writes only the first (harness/scenarios.ts:2139-2140).

churn.column.note: The subscriber selects `entities[id].label` with the default `Object.is` (zustand.ts:338-341), so a write to another column of the row re-runs the selector and does not wake it. The column filter is the middleware's equality on a selected string (esm/middleware.mjs:254-258), the same thing the README's `state.paw` example shows (README.md:209-210); the adapter compares nothing.

churn.chain.note: Declined with a written `absent` (zustand.ts:587-593, :626-629); `mountOnChain` throws through `declinedMount` (:342). The package ships no derived value: a selector is re-run per notification and nothing caches a level's output (esm/vanilla.mjs:1-21, esm/middleware.mjs:249-271), so a chain would be either one flat function or memoisation written in the adapter.

churn.diamond.note: Declined for the same reason and with the same text as `churn.chain` (zustand.ts:587-593); `mountOnDiamond` throws (:343).

reads.byKey.note: One `getState()` per page and one `entities[id]` per key, nothing resolved in advance and no `setState` (zustand.ts:409-418).

The selection is a top-k walk and not a re-sort.

reads.byTwoAxes.note: View B selects group A's window under the second predicate (zustand.ts:391-401, predicate in `selectionOf` at :182). A move of a row view B's predicate excluded replaces only that row's object, so B's window stays `shallow`-equal and is not delivered.

reads.bySwitch.note: `switchGroup` sets `cursor` to `{ group, offset: 0 }` in one `setState` (zustand.ts:424-426); view A's selector reads the new group's id list (:378-390); view B's inputs are unchanged and `shallow` holds.

The views select the owners' names and the pairs' marks as string arrays with `shallow` and `fireImmediately` (:478-491), so an owner write leaves the pair view undelivered and a pair write the owner view. Both selectors run on every `setState`, and the pair selector composes each key per line per notification. `writePair` composes its key per call (:501-508).

card.summary: One vanilla `createStore` per wiring holding the normalised shape, written by immutable `setState` updates, with every consumer a `subscribeWithSelector` listener compared by `Object.is` or the shipped `shallow`; a frame's row writes are buffered and applied as ONE `setState`, every `setState` re-runs every selector in the store, a re-send of unchanged values notifies because nothing compares values, and `churn.chain` and `churn.diamond` are declined because zustand has no derivation primitive.
card.body:
## Version and recipe

`node_modules/zustand/package.json` is `5.0.15`, the same as `version`
(zustand.ts:597). The adapter imports `createStore` from `zustand/vanilla`,
`subscribeWithSelector` from `zustand/middleware` and `shallow` from
`zustand/vanilla/shallow` (zustand.ts:1-3); the last because `zustand/shallow`
also re-exports `useShallow` and so imports React (esm/shallow.mjs:1-2). The
recipe is the README's "Using subscribe with selector" and "Using zustand without
React" (README.md:192-251) with state "updated immutably" (README.md:31).

## The store and its notification

`createStore` keeps one state value and one `Set` of listeners; `setState` skips
only when the updater returns the current state by `Object.is`, otherwise merges
the partial into a new top-level object and calls every listener synchronously
(esm/vanilla.mjs:1-21). `subscribeWithSelector` wraps `subscribe` so that a
listener is called only when `equalityFn(previousSlice, nextSlice)` is false,
default `Object.is`, and can be fired on subscribe (esm/middleware.mjs:249-271).
The adapter's updaters return `state` unchanged only when no edit found its id
stored (zustand.ts:131, :136, :497, :505); that is an existence test, not a value
test.

## Writes

A row write is an edit (`write`, `remove`, `patch`; `setGroup` and `setRank` are
patches) applied by `entitiesEdited` (zustand.ts:83-119), which copies `entities`
once per `setState` and gives every changed row a fresh object. The grouped stores
wrap it in `rowsEdited` (:124-132), which copies each touched group list once
(`bucketsDraftOf`, :62-76) and splices a leaving id out of that copy (:78-81); the
churn and relation stores use `onlyEntitiesEdited` (:134-137). A re-send makes a
fresh object per row and notifies: no zustand API compares values before notifying,
and the window views are delivered again with unchanged text.

## Batching

None exists in 5.0.15: the package's exports are `createStore`, `create`,
`useStore` (esm/index.mjs:1-2, esm/react.mjs:22), the middlewares `combine`,
`createJSONStorage`, `devtools`, `persist`, `redux`, `subscribeWithSelector`
and `unstable_ssrSafe` (esm/middleware.mjs:490) plus `immer` from its own entry,
`createWithEqualityFn`/`useStoreWithEqualityFn` (esm/traditional.mjs:26), and
`shallow`/`useShallow`; `setState` notifies before returning (esm/vanilla.mjs:9).
These export lists are from the 2026-10-17 audit and were not re-read. None of
these defers or groups notifications, and none is a derived value, which is also
what the `churn.chain`/`churn.diamond` decline rests on.

The library's way of applying several changes together is one `setState` that
makes all of them, so `frame` (`rowEditorOf`, zustand.ts:139-165) buffers the row
writes issued inside it, in order and with nothing compared, and applies them as
one `setState` when it returns: one copy of `entities`, one copy of each touched
group list, one notification of every listener. This is the bench-wide rule that an
adapter may buffer a frame's writes into the library's own bulk update
(harness/types.ts:23-25; valtio.ts buffers inside a frame the same way). Outside a
frame each write is its own `setState`. Cursor, owner, pair and single writes are
not buffered; no script issues one inside a frame.

## Code volume

The figures are `npm run lines`' cell for each wiring; they have not been re-run
since the 2026-10-20 edit.

- **The writes are the library's recipe.** zustand has no update primitive beyond
  `setState(updater)`, so an immutable upsert, removal and patch are spelled out
  (zustand.ts:83-137), plus the frame buffer (:139-165). The window and read wirings
  keep `idsByGroup` beside `entities`, which needs the per-group copy-on-write draft
  (:62-81); the churn and relation wirings keep `entities` alone
  (`onlyEntitiesEdited`, :134-137), because no script there reads a grouping.
- **reads.byKey** carries both read views, because one binding serves every read shape:
  the cursor state and the two selectors (:377-402) over the shared top-k selection
  (:171-194), which a zustand selector has to spell out because zustand derives
  nothing.
- **bind** carries the grouped writes, the selection, one listener per view
  (:208-220) and the cell wiring's two listeners (:235-253).

## Unverified

The normalised `entities` + id-list shape is the instruction this adapter was
written to; the shipped README does not prescribe a state layout. The `immer`
middleware (README.md:316-334) would turn a re-send into a no-op, as Immer does
for Redux Toolkit, at the cost of a draft per write; neither arm is measured. The
cost of every `setState` running every listener's selector — fifty top-k
derivations per `setState` under `bindPerGroup`, and N or N×8 selectors per `setState` in
the shared-root churn scripts — is stated from the source, not measured. The
`shallow` comparison builds two `Map`s per array comparison
(esm/vanilla/shallow.mjs:2-18, :43-46), also unmeasured: an array has an
`entries` method, so `hasIterableEntries` is true for it and arrays go through
`compareEntries` rather than the cheaper `compareIterables`. The adapter has no
choice there, since `shallow` is the comparator the package ships. Nothing here was
run, and the `digest` above is the 2026-10-17 value, stale since the 2026-10-20 edit.

bind.note: One `proxy({ rows, byGroup })` (valtio.ts:151-155) holding each row proxy under the population and under its group bucket (:93-132). Each view is `subscribe(bucket, mark, true)` (:157-174); `settle` delivers each marked view once through `visibleOf` over the bucket's values (:247-270). The sync arm is the only one that runs here: the default arm defers to a microtask (node_modules/valtio/vanilla.js:210-216), the flag calls back inside the set (:206-208). `frame` calls its function directly (valtio.ts:52-54); the vanilla entry exports no batch (vanilla.js:278-285). A subscription hears its whole bucket, so a note write or a write below the window marks the view and delivers text it already shows. The cell wiring (`pin`, valtio.ts:203-236) is `subscribeKey` on `label` and `note` of each pinned row proxy (vanilla/utils.js:5-17), so a label write marks the label view only.

bindPerGroup.note: Same body with fifty bucket subscriptions (valtio.ts:738). A write reaches only the listeners of the bucket its row is filed in; a parent with no listener is never wired to its children (vanilla.js:120-133), so the population record costs nothing per write.

churn.row.note: `subscribe(row, body, true)` on the row proxy resolved at `holdChurnRows` (valtio.ts:312-343). The read is taken from the proxy at mount and is not a wake; `woke` is counted only in the body; `unmount` releases the listener and clears the read slot (:359-365). The churn and application scripts driven through this wiring write rows with `patchLabel` (harness/scenarios.ts:1883, :1888, :2484, :3040-3044), so a whole-row subscription wakes exactly the subscribers on the written rows; a write to another column of the row would wake it too, which is what a row subscription means.

churn.wide.note: `subscribe` takes one proxy (vanilla.js:193-225), so the subscriber is one `subscribe` per source sharing one body, released together on unmount (valtio.ts:320-346); the rendered text is the first source's label. Mount pays `count` listener registrations, which is what a valtio user over several proxies writes.

churn.column.note: `subscribeKey(row, 'label', body, true)` (valtio.ts:344-356), the shipped per-property subscription: a whole-proxy `subscribe` whose callback runs only when `Object.is` says `label` moved (vanilla/utils.js:9-13). The adapter compares nothing.

churn.chain.note: Declined with a written `absent` (valtio.ts:675-684, :717-720); `mountOnChain` throws through `declinedMount` (:357). valtio 2.3.2 ships no derived value: `derive` left for the separate `derive-valtio`, the shipped utils are listed at vanilla/utils.js:575-583, getters are unmemoised functions with no change signal (README.md:300-313), and `watch` is deprecated (vanilla/utils.js:21-27) and an effect, not a value.

churn.diamond.note: Declined for the same reason and with the same text as `churn.chain` (valtio.ts:675-684); `mountOnDiamond` throws (:358).

reads.byKey.note: One `rows[id]` property read through the proxy per key, nothing resolved in advance and nothing written (valtio.ts:417-426).

reads.byWindow.note: View A's cursor is a `cursor` proxy in the same state (valtio.ts:383-387). View A listens to the cursor (:401) and to the bucket of the cursor's group (`subscribePagedBucket`, :397-399). A scroll is one set of `cursor.offset` (:427-429), which marks view A through its `cursor` subscription; `settle` takes the top `offset + window` of the cursor's bucket with `visibleInto` and delivers the page at the offset (:436-454). View B listens to group A's bucket only and is not marked by a scroll. The selection is a top-k walk, not a re-sort.

reads.byTwoAxes.note: View B is `subscribe(groupA bucket, mark, true)` (valtio.ts:402-408), delivered through `visibleOnAxisInto` (:455-468). Any write into group A marks it, including rows its predicate excludes, and those deliveries are redundant.

reads.bySwitch.note: `switchGroup` releases view A's bucket subscription, subscribes to the new group's bucket, and sets `cursor.group` and `cursor.offset` (valtio.ts:430-435): two notifications on the cursor proxy, one delivery at `settle` of the new group's bucket at offset 0. A write to any other group does not mark view A. The re-subscription is inside the timed switch and pays what valtio charges for it: the first listener on a bucket wires every row proxy in it (`addListener`, vanilla.js:142-152), and the last listener leaving unwires them (vanilla.js:153-163); group A's bucket keeps view B's listener, so switching back to it wires nothing.

relations.note: Owners and pairs are two records of one state (valtio.ts:482-486). The line sources are resolved once at `holdRelation` and the two views are `subscribe(owners)` and `subscribe(pairs)` with the sync flag, delivered at hold and then at `settle` when marked (:583-592). An owner write does not mark the pair view and a pair write does not mark the owner view. `writePair` composes its key per call and looks it up through `pairs`.

single.note: One `proxy({ value, bystander })` and two `subscribeKey` listeners (valtio.ts:608-673). A write of `value` runs both listeners, because both are subscriptions to the same proxy, and only the `value` callback passes `Object.is` (vanilla/utils.js:9-13), so the bystander is not delivered. A re-send of the stored value is a no-op in the set trap (vanilla.js:56-58) and wakes neither.

card.summary: One vanilla `proxy` state per wiring mutated in place, every consumer a `subscribe` or `subscribeKey` with the sync flag because the default microtask arm never runs in a worker that does not yield, each listener marking its view and `settle` rendering the marked ones; there is no batch, a subscription hears its whole subtree, valtio's per-property `Object.is` makes a re-send silent, and `churn.chain` and `churn.diamond` are declined because 2.3.2 ships no derivation primitive.
card.body:
## Version and recipe

`node_modules/valtio/package.json` is `2.3.2`, the same as `version`
(valtio.ts:688). The adapter imports `proxy` and `subscribe` from
`valtio/vanilla` and `subscribeKey` from `valtio/vanilla/utils`
(valtio.ts:1-2). The recipe is the README's "Use it vanilla" (README.md:260-273):
a `proxy` mutated in place and `subscribe` on it.

## The store and its notification

`proxy` wraps an object; the `set` trap compares the new value with the old by
`Object.is` and returns without notifying when they match, otherwise wraps a
plain object value in its own proxy, wires it to this proxy's listeners and
notifies (vanilla.js:53-68). Notification bumps a global version and calls this
proxy's listeners; a child proxy is wired to a parent only while the parent has
listeners (vanilla.js:120-165), so it climbs only through subscribed ancestors.
`subscribe` with `notifyInSync` calls back inside the set (vanilla.js:206-208);
without it, once per microtask (vanilla.js:210-216).

## Why each listener marks and `settle` renders

No worker yields between a write and its settle, so the default arm's microtask
never runs before the audit reads the consumers: the sync flag is the only arm
that can drive a consumer here. Delivering inside every sync callback would
render each intermediate state of a batch — the load is one notification per row
— where the library's default arm coalesces them. Marking in the callback and
rendering at `settle` is that coalescing at the harness's frame boundary; a view
the library did not notify is never rendered (valtio.ts:247-270, :436-469,
:583-592, :658-667).

## Writes

A new row is assigned as a copy and becomes a proxy (vanilla.js:63); an existing
row gets `Object.assign` of the incoming row (valtio.ts:56-63, :103-117), so only
properties whose value moved notify. A group move sets `group`, deletes the row
from its old bucket and assigns it into the new one (valtio.ts:95-100,
:124-131). A removal deletes from the population and the bucket
(valtio.ts:116-123). Point writes are one property set on the row proxy found
through `rows[id]` (valtio.ts:68-83).

## Batching

None exists in 2.3.2: the vanilla entry's exports are `getVersion`, `proxy`,
`ref`, `snapshot`, `subscribe` and three `unstable_` hooks (vanilla.js:278-285).
`frame` calls `run()` (valtio.ts:52-54); every set inside it runs the sync
listeners of its proxy and of each subscribed ancestor.

## Unverified

The `{ rows, byGroup }` shape is this adapter's choice; the README does not
prescribe a layout, and a single `rows` record with a group filter at render
would wake every view on every write. Whether the per-row Proxy allocation of
the load, the two-parent wiring of each row, or `Object.values` through the
`ownKeys` trap dominates any row is not measured. Getters as "computed
properties" were not built as a chain arm. Nothing here was run.

A React user of valtio reads through `useSnapshot`, which tracks the properties
a render touched (proxy-compare, a dependency of valtio, vanilla.js:3) and skips
a re-render when only untracked ones moved; the vanilla `subscribe` the adapter
is limited to has no such filter, so the window views here are delivered on note
writes and below-window writes that a `useSnapshot` component would ignore. That
is redundant delivery, which the harness permits, and it is the vanilla API's
behaviour rather than something the adapter adds; it was not measured.

bind.note: One rows store (xstate-store.ts:115-169) and one `store.select(..., shallowEqual)` per view, subscribed (:260-268). Every point event spreads the whole `rows` record (:105-113, :151-166), the README's immutable pattern (node_modules/@xstate/store/README.md:28-45). A transition that changes the snapshot recomputes both views (store-55b22bbd.js:751-755); `shallowEqual` (xstate-store.js:13-27) delivers only a view whose window holds a different row object. `frame` (`rowWritesOf`, :201-228) buffers the row events and sends one `framed` event whose handler (:60-76) re-triggers them with `enqueue.trigger`, so a frame is one transition and one `atom.set` (store-55b22bbd.js:847-875, :646-649).

bindPerGroup.note: The same body with fifty selections (xstate-store.ts:689, body :258-303). One write recomputes all fifty selectors, since all depend on the one store atom; `shallowEqual` keeps the forty-nine whose window did not change from delivering.

churn.row.note: `store.select(context => context.rows[id])` per subscriber, subscribed, with the row's label recorded at mount (xstate-store.ts:335-341, :362-367). The first effect run does not call the observer (store-55b22bbd.js:365-372), so a mount is not a wake. A write to another row returns the same row object and `Object.is` keeps the subscriber silent (store-55b22bbd.js:395, :405). The initial read at xstate-store.ts:340 is `source.get()` on a computed the effect has just evaluated, so it returns the cached snapshot without re-running the selector (store-55b22bbd.js:421-436). `unmount` stops the effect and clears the slot (:398-404); the selection purges its edge to the store synchronously (store-55b22bbd.js:252-258, :517-521). Every subscriber's selector runs on every transition. The store is `createEntitiesStore` (:171-199), the rows record without the group index, because no churn script reads a grouping.

churn.wide.note: `store.select` returning the `count`-tuple of row objects (xstate-store.ts:368-373) compared with the package's `shallowEqual`, rendering the first defined row's label (`firstLabelOf`, :317-324). A write to any of the `count` rows yields a different tuple element and wakes the subscriber; a write elsewhere leaves every element the same object. The same shape as zustand's wide subscriber (zustand.ts:330-336).

churn.column.note: `store.select` of row 0's label alone (xstate-store.ts:375-378). The library's own selection comparator (`Object.is`, store-55b22bbd.js:395, :405) is what tells a label write from a write to another column; the adapter compares nothing. The store still has one change signal, so every column selector runs on every write — the same cost as `churn.row`, with a different filter.

churn.chain.note: Level 1 is `store.select` returning `chainLevelOf(composed label, 1)`; levels 2..depth are `createAtom(() => chainLevelOf(below.get(), level))`; the subscriber is on the head (xstate-store.ts:379-389). `createAtom` with a getter is the package's computed (store-55b22bbd.js:343-437). Teardown cascades down the levels through `unwatched` (:252-258). Level 1 composes a string, as alien-signals' level-1 computed does (alien-signals.ts:456-462), so the chain's cut-off is the library's `Object.is` on that string.

churn.diamond.note: A `select` of root row `from`'s label, `createAtom`s for `diamondLeftOf` and `diamondRightOf` over it, a `createAtom` join over both, the subscriber on the join (xstate-store.ts:390-397). The reactive core is alien-signals adapted in-package (store-55b22bbd.js:3-5, propagate :95-144, checkDirty :145-211), which marks the join pending once and recomputes it once per write. Not run; the diamond script's check is what asserts it.

reads.byKey.note: One `getSnapshot()` per page and one property read per key, nothing resolved in advance, no event sent (xstate-store.ts:459-468).

reads.byWindow.note: View A's cursor is a second store with `scrolled` and `switched` events (xstate-store.ts:417-429). View A is a `createAtom` reading both stores via `store.get()` (:431-443), the README's tracked read (README.md:353); view B is a `select` over the rows store alone (:444-447), so a scroll recomputes A only. A scroll is one `send` (:469). View A's atom compares its `offset` and then its rows with `shallowEqual` (:443), through `createAtom`'s `compare` option (store-55b22bbd.js:395).

reads.byTwoAxes.note: View B is `select` over the rows store with the second predicate (xstate-store.ts:444-447, predicate in `selectionOf` :244) and `shallowEqual`. View A is the `paged` atom (:431-443); it depends on the rows store's atom, so every transition filterTwoAxes causes recomputes it (scenario lines from the 2026-10-17 audit, not re-read), and its comparator — same offset and `shallowEqual` rows — keeps it from delivering when the moved row was outside its window, as zustand's sliced page under `shallow` does (zustand.ts:378-390).

reads.bySwitch.note: `switchGroup` sends one `switched` event setting `{ group, offset: 0 }` (xstate-store.ts:424-427, :470): one atom write, one recompute of view A over the new group's bucket. View B does not read the cursor store.

relations.note: Rows, owners and pairs in a store each (xstate-store.ts:487-527). View A is a `select` over the owners store, view B over the pairs store, both with `shallowEqual` (:541-550), so a write to one type never marks the other view. `writePair` composes the key on every call (:556-557).

single.note: One store with `value` and `bystander` in context and a `select` of each, subscribed (xstate-store.ts:572-637); no script writes a single inside a frame, so `frame` runs its function (`runDirectly`, :34-36). A re-send of the same value produces a new context and notifies the store atom, and the selection's `Object.is` (store-55b22bbd.js:405) keeps both subscribers silent.

improvements: Unmeasured: inside a frame every triggered event is still its own handler, so a frame of k point writes spreads the rows record k times. One bulk event applying all k edits to one copy would spread it once; `enqueue.trigger` is what the package ships for one transition, and a bulk event is the adapter's own transition, so it is left as a question.

Unmeasured: partitioning the rows record by group (one record per group inside context, or one store per group as the nanostores adapter does) would cut a point write's copy from the population to one group. It is not a pattern the README shows, and it is a different normalisation rather than a faster use of the same API.
card.summary: One `createStore` per entity type with immutable transitions sent as `store.send` events, every consumer a subscription to a `store.select` or `createAtom` computed over the store; the package ships no batch, so `frame` buffers its row events and sends ONE `framed` event that re-triggers them through `enqueue.trigger`, one transition and one notification per frame; window, cell, relation and both read views compare with the package's own `shallowEqual`, and the wide churn subscriber selects the `count`-tuple of row objects under it; every churn shape, including the column, chain and diamond, is built from `select` and `createAtom`.

## Version and recipe

`node_modules/@xstate/store/package.json` is `4.2.3`, the same as `version`
(xstate-store.ts:641). The package's entry exports `createStore`, `createStoreConfig`,
`createStoreLogic`, `createAtom`, `createAtomConfig`, `createAsyncAtom`,
`createReducerAtom`, `fromStore` and `shallowEqual` (dist/xstate-store.js:2, :90;
dist/declarations/src/index.d.ts:1-4). The adapter uses `createStore`, `store.send`,
`store.select`, `store.get` / `getSnapshot`, `createAtom` with a getter and a `compare`,
and `shallowEqual`. The online docs the `docs` field cites were not read; the recipe is
checked against the shipped code and the shipped README.

## Batching

There is no batch, transaction or deferred notification in 4.2.3. `send` calls `receive`,
which runs the transition and `atom.set`s the snapshot once (store-55b22bbd.js:646-649);
`atom.set` propagates and flushes the effect queue before returning (:439-447,
:270-278; these two from the 2026-10-17 audit, not re-read). The coalescing the package
ships is `enqueue.trigger` inside one transition: a triggered event is pushed onto the
transition's pending queue and processed in the same macrostep (:847-875), and the README
says so (README.md:330-332). It is reachable only from inside a handler, so `frame`
(`rowWritesOf`, xstate-store.ts:201-228) buffers the row events issued inside it, in order
and with nothing compared, and sends ONE `framed` event; its handler (`framed`, :60-76)
re-triggers each buffered event and returns `undefined`. A frame is therefore one
transition, one `atom.set` and one notification. This is the bench-wide rule that an
adapter may buffer a frame's writes into the library's own bulk mechanism
(harness/types.ts:23-25). Cursor, owner, pair and single writes are not buffered; no
script issues one inside a frame.

## Events, and what each one allocates

Events are sent as literal objects through `store.send` (`rowWritesOf`,
xstate-store.ts:201-228). `store.trigger.x(payload)` is documented as equivalent
(README.md:51) and builds the event by spreading the payload (store-55b22bbd.js:543-549,
:590-598). Every sent event runs `createStoreTransition`, which allocates an effects
array and a pending-events array, and every event it processes — a triggered one too —
builds an enqueue object with two `Proxy`s (`createEnqueueObject`, :551-571, called at
:859-862); `enqueue.trigger` also spreads each payload into a fresh event (`toEvent`,
:543-549).

## Equality

`select` and `createAtom` take a comparator (`equalityFn`, store-55b22bbd.js:751-755;
`compare`, :395). The adapter uses the default `Object.is` for the row, column, chain,
diamond and single subscribers, and the exported `shallowEqual` (xstate-store.js:13-27)
for every array-returning view and the wide tuple. View A of the read wiring returns
`{ offset, rows }`, so its `compare` checks the offset by identity and passes the rows to
`shallowEqual` (xstate-store.ts:443) — the one comparator the adapter composes, and it is
composed only of the package's own. `_update` treats an `undefined` previous value as
always changed (:405); no selector here returns `undefined` for a view, because
`selectionOf` hands back a fresh array even for a group with no bucket yet
(xstate-store.ts:233-256).

## Immutability

Change is detected by identity, so every transition returns new objects: a point event
spreads the row and the whole `rows` record (`rowReplaced`, xstate-store.ts:105-113), a
move also copies the two buckets (:155-164), and `write` / `remove` copy each touched
bucket once per event (:80-103, :119-153). Inside a frame these copies are per triggered
event. A missing id returns `undefined`, which leaves
the snapshot unchanged and notifies nothing (store-55b22bbd.js:863, :869-874); that is a
presence check, not a value check. Every `write` copies each incoming row, so a re-send
of unchanged values notifies: the package compares no values before committing
(store-55b22bbd.js:869-874 compares the context by identity only), and the contract
forbids the adapter to add a check its library does not have (harness/types.ts:11-12).

## Code volume

The figures are `npm run lines`' cell for each wiring; they have not been re-run since
the 2026-10-20 edit, and the `digest` above is the 2026-10-17 value, now stale.

- Every row store carries the `framed` event types and handler (xstate-store.ts:49-76) and the buffering
  writer (:201-228).
- Two row stores. `createRowsStore` (xstate-store.ts:115-169) keeps `idsByGroup` beside
  `rows` for the window and read wirings, whose views walk a group, and needs the
  per-event bucket drafts (:80-103). `createEntitiesStore` (:171-199) is `rows` alone and
  serves the churn and relation wirings, where `groupOrder` answers `undefined`. Each
  transition is written out because the package's only update primitive is a handler
  returning the next context (README.md:28-45).
- **reads.byKey** carries both read views, because one binding serves every read shape:
  the cursor store (:417-429), the `paged` atom and the axis selection (:431-451), over
  the shared top-k `selectionOf` (:233-256), which a selector has to spell out because
  the package derives nothing from a collection.
- **bind** carries the grouped store, the selection, one selection per view
  (:260-268) and the cell wiring's two selections (:278-294).

bind.note: `computed` over one bucket ref and the `group`/`rank` refs of its records, ending in an effect that reads the selected records' `label` (vue-reactivity.ts:277-284). `write`, `remove` and `setGroup` mutate the touched buckets in place and `triggerRef` each once (`fileRows` :185-214, `unfileRows` :216-239, `moveRow` :241-254). `readAll` reads the field refs outside any effect, untracked (:348). `frame` is `run()` (:129-131); `settle` drains the effect queue (:134-155, wired at :347).

bindPerGroup.note: Same body with fifty views (vue-reactivity.ts:847); each view's computed reads only its own bucket, so Vue's dep graph routes a write to one view.

churn.row.note: An effect reading all four field refs of row `from` and rendering its label (`labelOfWholeRow`, vue-reactivity.ts:384-389; mount :450-455), so it is a subscription to the WHOLE row, as SCENARIOS.md defines the shape. The effect's creation run (reactivity.cjs.prod.js:457-474) is the mount and records the read in `churnRead[at]` without counting (:372-381); `unmount` stops the runner and clears the slot (:478-484). `settle` drains the queue, then delivers once if anything woke (:432-437).

churn.wide.note: One effect reading every field ref of `count` rows, ending on row `from` (vue-reactivity.ts:391-397, :450-455).

churn.column.note: `computed(() => record.label.value)` under the effect (vue-reactivity.ts:456-459). A `note` write touches a ref the computed never read, so neither runs.

churn.chain.note: Level 1 is a `computed` returning `chainLevelOf(labels of the count sources joined, 1)`; levels 2..depth are each a `computed` over the one below; the effect reads the head (vue-reactivity.ts:460-470). `depth` computeds in all.

churn.diamond.note: Two `computed`s over root row `from`'s label ref (`diamondLeftOf`, `diamondRightOf`) and a third over both (`diamondJoinOf`), the effect on the join (vue-reactivity.ts:471-477). The effect is in the queue once however many branches notify it, and `settle` runs it once; the diamond script's check asserts it.

reads.byKey.note: One `byId.get` and one untracked `.value` per field read per key, nothing hoisted (vue-reactivity.ts:564-572).

reads.byWindow.note: View A's group and offset are two refs (vue-reactivity.ts:508-509). A `sorted` computed orders the group's bucket and a `paged` computed slices it (:512-527), so a scroll re-runs only the slice. `scrollTo` is one ref write (:573-575). View B's computed reads neither ref (:528-530).

reads.byTwoAxes.note: View B is a computed over the same bucket with the second predicate (vue-reactivity.ts:528-530, predicate at :116).

reads.bySwitch.note: `switchGroup` writes the group ref and resets the offset ref (vue-reactivity.ts:576-579); view A's effect is queued by both and is in the set once, so it runs once at `settle` over the new group's bucket.

relations.note: Owner and pair records each get their own `shallowRef`. View A's effect reads owner refs and view B's reads pair refs (vue-reactivity.ts:682-697), so the two views' dependencies are disjoint. `writePair` composes the key on every call (:702-706). The population refs (:597, :600) are written only in the untimed `writeOwners` and `holdRelation`.

single.note: Bare `ref.value = v` (vue-reactivity.ts:784-786). The setter compares with `hasChanged` (reactivity.cjs.prod.js:1428); a changed value queues the effect, and `settle` runs it and delivers (:790-800).

card.summary: The preact and alien wiring in @vue/reactivity's primitives — a shallowRef per mutable field of each row, a shallowRef bucket per group mutated in place and announced with the documented `triggerRef`, a computed plus effect per view. The package exports no batch, so every effect is created with the `scheduler` option: a trigger queues it, and `settle` runs each queued effect whose `dirty` is set — the job queue @vue/runtime-core keeps and this package does not ship, the same mark-then-render-at-settle mechanism the valtio row gets.
card.body:
## Version and recipe

`node_modules/@vue/reactivity/package.json` is `3.5.43`, the same as `version`
(vue-reactivity.ts:810). The worker runs under `NODE_ENV=production`
(src/harness/measureBatch.ts:201), so `index.js` loads
`dist/reactivity.cjs.prod.js`, and every library line below is in that file. The
primitives are `shallowRef`, `computed`, `effect`, `stop` and `triggerRef` — all
exported (:1866-1905). The shape is the preact and alien rows': a ref per mutable
field, a bucket ref per group, a computed plus effect per view
(vue-reactivity.md, 'The recipe').

## Batching

`startBatch` (:311) and `endBatch` (:314-348) exist but are not in the export list
(:1856-1905) or in `dist/reactivity.d.ts`. What is exported is the `scheduler`
option (`ReactiveEffectOptions`, d.ts :270-274): a triggered effect with one calls
it instead of running (`ReactiveEffect.trigger`, :277-285). Every effect is made by
`createEffectQueue` (vue-reactivity.ts:134-155): the scheduler adds the runner to a
`Set`, and `settle` runs each queued runner whose `effect.dirty` (d.ts :309,
`isDirty` :376-386) is set — the check the default trigger makes in `runIfDirty`
(:289-293). `frame(run)` is `run()`. A frame's several writes therefore render once
per view at `settle`, and the order of a move's three writes no longer matters.
`effectScope` pause/resume was not used: it parks effects of a scope, and as a frame
would walk every effect twice (vue-reactivity.md, 'What a frame is').

## The cell wiring

`pin` stops the window effects and builds, untimed, one effect per column reading
that column's ref of every pinned row directly (vue-reactivity.ts:313-339). A
`note` write touches a ref the label effect never read.

## Unmount

`stop(runner)` (reactivity.cjs.prod.js:475-477) unlinks the effect from its
dependencies (:266-276); a computed whose last subscriber goes unlinks from its own
sources (`removeSub`, :423-445). A stopped runner still in the queue has no deps,
so `dirty` is false and `settle` skips it.

## What the adapter adds, and what it does not

No equality function is written in the adapter: every skip is the ref setter's
`hasChanged` (:1428), a computed's (:408), or `dirty`'s version comparison. The
effect queue is the one piece of machinery the adapter adds, and it is the part of
Vue that lives in `@vue/runtime-core`; the departure says so.

## What was not traced

Neither the author nor a verifier compiled or ran this version of the adapter;
every claim above is read from the source. The card needs a second reader before
it is stamped.

bind.note: A `createMemo` over one bucket signal and the `group`/`rank` signals of its records, ending in a `createEffect` that reads the selected records' `label`, all inside one `createRoot` (solid-signals.ts:240-250). `write`, `remove` and `setGroup` mutate the touched buckets in place inside `batch` and set each to its own array, which notifies because the bucket signal has `equals: false` (`bucketOfIn` :127-136, `announce` :138-140, `fileRows` :154-185, `unfileRows` :187-212, `moveRow` :214-230). `readAll` calls each field getter through `byId` outside any tracking scope (:313). `frame` is `batch` (:123-125; node_modules/solid-js/dist/solid.js:452-454).

bindPerGroup.note: The same body with fifty views (solid-signals.ts:825); disjoint dependency sets, routed by Solid's graph.

churn.row.note: A `createEffect` inside its own `createRoot` reading all four field getters of row `from` and rendering its label (`labelOfWholeRow`, solid-signals.ts:358-363; `subscribe` :338-354; mount :437-442), so it is a subscription to the WHOLE row, as types.ts:55-60 and SCENARIOS.md define the shape; `churn.column` is the label-only contrast. The first run is the mount, writes the read slot and is not counted; `unmount` disposes the root and clears the slot (:466-472). The first run happens before `createRoot` returns, because the root's `runUpdates` drains the effect queue (dist/solid.js:177-197, :222-229, :819-834, :875-877). That holds only for a mount outside an open batch — inside one, `runUpdates` sets `wait` (:823) and the first run is deferred to the outer batch's end.

churn.wide.note: One `createEffect` reading every field getter of `count` rows, ending on row `from` (solid-signals.ts:365-371, :437-442).

churn.column.note: A `createMemo` returning the row's label under the effect (solid-signals.ts:356, :443-445). A `note` write touches a signal the memo never read, so nothing re-runs and the column identity is Solid's.

churn.chain.note: Level 1 is a `createMemo` over the `count` sources returning `chainLevelOf(their labels joined, 1)`; levels 2..depth are each a `createMemo` over the one below; the effect reads the head (solid-signals.ts:446-457). All `depth` memos are owned by the subscriber's root, so `unmount` disposes them (dist/solid.js:946-979).

churn.diamond.note: Two `createMemo`s over root row `from`'s `label` getter (`diamondLeftOf`, `diamondRightOf`) and a third over both (`diamondJoinOf`), the effect on the join (solid-signals.ts:458-465). Once-per-frame is Solid's own: a node is queued only while clean (dist/solid.js:669-670, :935-945). The adapter adds no guard; the diamond script's check asserts it.

reads.byKey.note: One `byId.get` and the getter calls of `shownOf` per key, untracked, nothing hoisted (solid-signals.ts:544-552).

reads.byWindow.note: The offset is a `createSignal` (solid-signals.ts:490) read only by the `paged` memo, which slices the `sorted` memo (:496-511), so a scroll re-runs the slice and never the sort — the shape of the preact and alien read wirings. `scrollTo` is one bare setter call (:553-555). View B's memo reads neither signal (:512-514).

reads.byTwoAxes.note: View B is a `createMemo` over the same bucket with the second predicate (solid-signals.ts:512-514, :518-520, predicate at :110).

reads.bySwitch.note: View A's group is a `createSignal` (solid-signals.ts:491) read by the `sorted` memo. `switchGroup` writes the group and resets the offset to 0 inside one `batch` (:556-561), so the effect re-runs once over the new group's bucket.

relations.note: Owner and pair records each in their own `createSignal`. View A's effect reads owner getters and view B's reads pair getters, in one root created by `holdRelation` (solid-signals.ts:673-687), so the two views have disjoint dependencies. `writePair` composes the key on every call (:693-697).

single.note: Two signals, two effects in one root, the bare setter (solid-signals.ts:737-756, :763-765). The setter calls `writeSignal`, which runs its own `runUpdates` (dist/solid.js:206-211, :663-681), and a re-send of the stored value is stopped by Solid's `===` comparator (:654).

improvements: Coverage, not speed: Solid's documented collection API is `createStore` from `solid-js/store` with `reconcile`/`produce`. It is unreachable under this harness: `store/dist/store.js:1` imports the bare `solid-js`, which under node resolves to `dist/server.js` (package.json `exports['.'].node`), and `solid-js/store` itself resolves to `store/dist/server.js` under `node`. Spawning the solid-js worker with `--conditions=browser` (src/harness/measureBatch.ts, the worker's `args`, where no conditions flag is passed today) would let a store-backed wiring be measured as a second participant beside this one. Nothing shows a store is FASTER than a signal per field — a store is per-property signals behind a proxy — so this is not what `improvable` means and the verdict is not lowered for it.
card.summary: Solid's signal layer outside components: a createSignal per mutable field of each row, a bucket signal per group created with `equals: false` and mutated in place, a createMemo plus createEffect per view inside a createRoot, every script frame in Solid's own batch; the chain, diamond and view switch are createMemo and createSignal. The reactive build is imported by path because under node `solid-js` resolves to the inert server build, and solid-js/store is not used because it imports the bare `solid-js` and would sit on that server build.
card.body:
## Version and build

`node_modules/solid-js/package.json` is `1.9.15`, equal to `version`
(solid-signals.ts:788). Its `"."` export resolves to `dist/server.js` under the `"node"`
condition and to `dist/solid.js` only under `"browser"` or the default. The worker is
spawned as `node --expose-gc --import tsx …` (src/harness/measureBatch.ts) with no
conditions flag, so `import 'solid-js'` would load the SSR build, where `createEffect`
is empty (dist/server.js:78), signals have no observers (:62-66) and `batch` only calls
its argument (:102-104). The adapter imports `solid-js/dist/solid.js`
(solid-signals.ts:2), permitted by the package's `"./dist/*"` export, and types it with
the package's `types/index.d.ts` (:3, :40). `dist/solid.js` is the production build
(`IS_DEV = false`, dist/solid.js:149). This is stated in `departure`.

## Why the verdict is idiomatic, and what is not measured

`improvable` means "a documented, FASTER way exists and is not used" (audit/README.md),
and no line here shows a store is faster than a `createSignal` per field — a store wraps
per-property signals in a proxy. What a store wiring would add is coverage, and it is
blocked by the module graph (see `improvements`).

## What Solid routes, and what the adapter adds

- The id map and the group map hold `[get, set]` pairs (solid-signals.ts:236-237); no
  value lives outside a signal. Each view's memo reads one bucket signal and that
  bucket's records' `group` and `rank` (:242-244), so a write to a row of group Z reaches
  only the view over Z. A move writes the row's `group` and announces both buckets in
  one `batch` (:214-230).
- Bucket signals carry `equals: false` (:132), Solid's documented option for a signal
  that is always treated as changed (`comparator: options.equals || undefined`,
  dist/solid.js:204; `writeSignal`, :654). That is what lets a bucket be mutated in
  place and set to the same array, as alien does with `trigger`, instead of copying it
  per move. Every other signal and memo keeps Solid's default `===`.
- Every effect lives in a `createRoot` whose `dispose` the adapter keeps; disposal is
  `cleanNode` over the root's owned computations (dist/solid.js:946-979).

## Batching

`frame(run)` is `batch(run)` (solid-signals.ts:123-125), which is `runUpdates(fn, false)`
(dist/solid.js:452-454, :819-834); a nested `runUpdates` only calls its function (:820),
so the `batch` inside `write`, `remove`, `setGroup` and `switchGroup` nests inside a
frame. A method that writes one signal calls the setter bare. `settle` is a no-op in the
view, read and relation bindings; in the churn and single bindings it turns what the
effects recorded into one delivery (solid-signals.ts:414-424, :769-778).

## Cost that is Solid's and not the adapter's

An effect or memo re-collects its sources on every run: `updateComputation` calls
`cleanNode` first (dist/solid.js:685-688), and `readSignal` pushes each source back
(:619-650). A view memo over a bucket of N rows therefore re-subscribes N sources per
re-run. That is Solid's model, and the preact and alien rows pay their own equivalents.

## What is not traced here

That the diamond's join runs once per frame is argued from `writeSignal` and
`markDownstream`, not traced end to end through `runTop`/`lookUpstream`; the diamond
script's check is what asserts it. Nothing was compiled or run; line numbers were
re-read against the current file on 2026-10-20. The card needs a second reader before
it is stamped.

bind.note: A derived store per view over one bucket store and its row stores, consumed by `subscribe` (tanstack-store.ts:205-214, selection at :50-80). `write` and `remove` touch only the row stores and the touched buckets, each inside one `batch` (:106-170). `frame` is `batch` (:39-41; node_modules/@tanstack/store/src/atom.ts:70-79), carried by every binding. `readAll` reads `.state` of each row store through `byId` (:276).

bindPerGroup.note: Same body with fifty views (tanstack-store.ts:741); disjoint dependency sets, routed by the library's graph.

churn.row.note: `subscribe` on the row store, reading `label` (tanstack-store.ts:380-384, helper :303-314). `subscribe` does not call back on subscribe (src/atom.ts:178-191), so the mount reads `.state` into `churnRead[at]` (:312) and is not counted; each callback records the read and counts a wake (:308-311); `unmount` unsubscribes and clears the slot (:412-418).

churn.wide.note: A derived store over the `count` row stores, ending on row `from`, subscribed (tanstack-store.ts:316-322, :385-386). A subscription watches one store (src/atom.ts:178-191), so several sources are expressed as the library's own derived store over them.

churn.column.note: `createStore(() => source.state.label)` under the subscription (tanstack-store.ts:388-392). The derived store's `Object.is` compare (src/atom.ts:201, :222) stops a `note` write there, so the column identity is the library's.

churn.chain.note: Level 1 is a derived store over the `count` sources returning `chainLevelOf(label of row from, 1)`; levels 2..depth each derive `chainLevelOf(level below, level)`; `subscribe` on the head (tanstack-store.ts:393-402).

churn.diamond.note: Two derived stores over root row `from` (`diamondLeftOf`, `diamondRightOf` of its label), a third over both (`diamondJoinOf`), `subscribe` on the join (tanstack-store.ts:403-411). The subscription effect is queued once per propagation because `propagate` queues only a WATCHING sub (src/alien.ts:151-153) and `notify` clears that flag as it queues (src/atom.ts:52-55); it re-runs only after `checkDirty` (src/atom.ts:302-309); not run here, the diamond script's check asserts it.

reads.byKey.note: One `byId.get` and one `.state` read per key, outside any tracking context, nothing hoisted (tanstack-store.ts:480-488).

reads.byWindow.note: Offset store (tanstack-store.ts:436) read only by view A's derived store, which returns the offset with the rows (:440-452), subscribed at :463-465. `scrollTo` is one `setState` (:489-491). View B (:453-460) does not read the offset.

reads.byTwoAxes.note: View B is a derived store over the same bucket with the second predicate (tanstack-store.ts:453-460, predicate at :61).

reads.bySwitch.note: View A's group is a store (`$group`, tanstack-store.ts:437) that view A's derived store reads beside `$offset` (:440-452). `switchGroup` sets `$group` and resets `$offset` to 0 inside one `batch` (:492-497), so the subscription runs once over the new group's bucket. View B reads neither.

relations.note: Owner and pair records each get a store. View A is a derived store over the owner stores and view B over the pair stores (tanstack-store.ts:598-611), so the dependencies are disjoint. `writePair` composes the key on every call (:622-626). The population stores (:514, :517) are written only in the untimed `writeOwners` and `holdRelation`.

single.note: `createStore('')` and `subscribe`, written with a bare `setState` (tanstack-store.ts:650-706). The setter flushes on its own (src/atom.ts:261-268) and skips an `Object.is`-equal value (src/atom.ts:222), which is what `singleResend` meets.

improvements: DECLINED, docs checked 2026-10-20 — every store here is a `Store`, which wraps an atom and binds three methods per instance (node_modules/@tanstack/store/src/store.ts:30-37; dist/store.js:7-9); `createAtom` (src/atom.ts:146-273) is the primitive underneath. The TanStack Store docs present `Store` as the API: the quick-start opens with 'You'll start by creating a new store instance, which is a wrapper around your data' and never mentions `createAtom` (tanstack.com/store/latest/docs/quick-start); `createAtom` appears only as a bare signature in the generated reference (docs/reference/functions/createAtom), with no guidance on when to prefer it. The docs do not point to the lighter primitive, so the per-row `Store` (tanstack-store.ts:126, :339, :541) stays. What it costs — one wrapper object and three bound functions per row on `batchInsert`, `coldStart`, `appFill` and `growUnderSubscription` — is unmeasured.
card.summary: A `Store` per row, a bucket `Store` per group, and a derived store (`createStore(fn)`) per view with `subscribe` as its consumer, all on @tanstack/store 0.11's alien-signals core; every frame and every multi-store write runs inside the library's `batch`, the cell wiring narrows to a column with a derived store per pinned cell, and the chain, diamond and view switch are the library's own derived stores. 0.11.2 exports no `Derived` or `Effect` class: `createStore(fn)` is the derivation and `subscribe` the only subscriber.
card.body:
## Version and recipe

`node_modules/@tanstack/store/package.json` is `0.11.2`, the same as `version`
(tanstack-store.ts:710). The package ships no README; `docs` is the homepage from
package.json, and this audit did not read the online documentation. The recipe is
checked against the shipped `src/` (listed in the package's `files`) and its exports
in `dist/index.d.ts`: `createStore` (src/store.ts:86-105), `Store.setState`
(:43-45), `.state` (:46-48), `subscribe` (:52-56 → src/atom.ts:178-198) and `batch`
(src/atom.ts:70-79). `Derived` and `Effect`, which earlier lines of the library
exported, do not exist in 0.11.2 (src/index.ts:1-4; dist/index.js exports
`ReadonlyStore, Store, batch, createAsyncAtom, createAtom, createStore, flush, shallow,
toObserver`); `createStore(fn)` returning a `ReadonlyStore` is the derivation
(src/store.ts:59-84, :98-99, src/atom.ts:237-255).

What runs is `dist/index.js` (the `import` arm of `exports['.']`, the package being
`"type": "module"`), not `src/`. The verifier checked that the dist files carry the
same mechanisms the `src/` lines describe: `batchDepth` and the flush guard
(dist/atom.js:34-49), `options?.compare ?? Object.is` (dist/atom.js:124, :134), the
skipped first callback (dist/atom.js:112) and the three binds (dist/store.js:7-9).

## Batching

`frame(run)` is `batch(run)`. While `batchDepth > 0`, `flush` returns at once
(src/atom.ts:89-92), so every `setState` inside a frame propagates and queues the
effected subscriptions, which run once when the outermost `batch` returns. Methods
writing several stores carry their own nested `batch`; single-store methods call
`setState` bare, because `Atom.set` calls `flush` itself (src/atom.ts:261-268).

## What the adapter adds

- The id and group maps hold store handles (tanstack-store.ts:202-203), never values.
- `write` drafts each touched bucket once per batch (tanstack-store.ts:112-121).
- Subscriptions deliver nothing at creation (src/atom.ts:183-185), so `pin`,
  `holdRelation` and `holdSingle` deliver once, untimed, after subscribing
  (tanstack-store.ts:265-266, :616-617, :682-683), as the Redux adapter does.
- The derived stores that feed a consumer an array build a fresh array per recompute
  (:230-236, :598-611), because the compare is `Object.is`.
- No equality function is written in the adapter. `createStore` takes no compare
  option (src/store.ts:86-97), so every skip is `createAtom`'s default `Object.is`
  (src/atom.ts:201). The library ships `shallow` (src/index.ts:4) and `createAtom`
  accepts `compare`; neither is used, which leaves the library's default and gives the
  adapter no check of its own.
- The bucket drafts in `write` and the per-touched-group filter in `remove` are
  ordinary copy-on-write over an array store, the same shape as the preact, vue and
  solid rows, and skip no work the script asks for.

## Teardown

A derived store whose last subscriber leaves is `unwatched` and purges its deps
synchronously (src/alien.ts:101-128, src/atom.ts:56-62). `pin` dropping the window
subscriptions and a churn `unmount` therefore leave no live edges behind, unlike the
nanostores adapter's deferred detach.

## Unverified

Nothing here was run. Type-checking of the overload resolution `createStore<T>(value)`
versus `createStore(fn)` (src/store.ts:86-97) and of the structural `TSource` type
(tanstack-store.ts:45-48) is left to the compile.

Verified 2026-10-17 by a second reader: every adapter line cited held except one
(`churnRead[at]` read at :312, not :313). Every `src/store.ts` line in the first draft
was off by two to six lines and has been corrected (`createStore` :86-105, `setState`
:43-45, `.state` :46-48, `subscribe` :52-56, `ReadonlyStore` :59-84, binds :34-37);
the `src/atom.ts` and `src/alien.ts` lines held. The note that the dist build, not
`src/`, is what loads was added. TanStack's online docs were read on 2026-10-20 for
`Store` against `createAtom`; see `improvements`. Adapter line numbers re-read the same day.

card.models: Initial hydration: the first fetch of a list screen writes the whole dataset into a store whose views are already mounted.
card.measures: Bulk-load throughput into an empty store with subscriptions standing, ending at both views' first full render.
favours: Stores that ingest a batch in one pass and build their indexes once at the end (deferred index build, a bulk-load path) over stores that maintain an ordered index row by row as rows arrive.
Stores that adopt the given objects rather than copying them into their own representation; the harness hands one cloned array (worker.ts:85) and copying is legitimately extra work.
biases: Construction and subscription are outside the clock (`rebuild: true`, scenarios.ts:3085; `rebuild`, worker.ts:354-357, run from `settleForSample`, worker.ts:371-379, as the sample's untimed `setup`, measure.ts:73). Libraries expensive to construct and cheap to write look cheaper than at a real cold start; `coldStart` exists for that.

The empty render some libraries make on subscribe is discarded by `reset(forgetBetweenSamples)` before the clock (worker.ts:368-379; scenarios.md 'Two frames at a cold start'). Neutral here, but it hides a user-visible frame that `coldStart` shows.
One `write(rows)` call (scenarios.ts:3091-3094): every adapter may batch inside it, so eager and deferred stores are on equal terms. It is not wrapped in `frame`.
Five short columns per row (dataset.ts:29-35): stores whose load cost scales with field count (per-field observables, deep proxies) pay less than on application-width entities.

`repeatable: false` with a rebuild per sample (scenarios.ts:3085-3088; cells/runBatch.ts:55): one run per sample and a `collect` call before it (measure.ts:73-77), which forces a GC when `global.gc` is exposed (worker.ts:63-67), so GC triggered by the load's allocations is likely outside the timed region.
card.summary: A real, once-per-screen operation at a realistic size; it excludes construction and GC, so read it with coldStart and the memory pass.
